action: Prints the ration card, seeds Aadhaar, links the FPS, delivers / enables digital download
note: issuance and FPS assignment via URCMS/e-PDS

action: Identify the two demographic updates needed: name (new/hyphenated surname) and address (marital home).
note: Name and address are separate demographic-update requests but can be lodged in one visit. Applicant self-service step; not a listed UP-revenue post.

action: Confirm eligibility: no pucca house owned in India, first home, EWS/LIG/MIG income band.
note: PMAY-U 2.0 (active since 01 Sept 2024). Family must not own a pucca house anywhere in India; income band decides EWS/LIG/MIG. Confirm current slabs with ULB.

action: Checks form completeness and documents, forwards the file to the Supply Inspector of the area
on_reject: returns incomplete form for correction
note: preliminary document check and routing

action: Opens the mutation file, verifies fee, and routes it to the field revenue staff
note: File prepared for field enquiry

action: Apply for new domestic LT connection online via UPCL portal, UMANG, or at UPCL sub-division office
note: Choose domestic (LT) category and state requested connected load in kW. Portal: UPCL WSS (www.upcl.org) or Uttarakhand Apuni Sarkar single-window.

action: Collect RC, insurance, PUC; sign Form 29 (2 copies) and Form 30
note: Sale is completed by delivery + signed transfer forms; forms are prescribed under CMVR rr.55-56.

action: If vehicle was on loan, issue NOC and Form 35 to terminate hypothecation
on_reject: Loan must be closed before transfer can proceed cleanly.
note: Termination of hypothecation under MV Act s.51 and CMVR r.61 / Form 35; done at the RTO holding registration.

post_name: Assistant/Additional Regional Transport Officer (ARTO), original RTO
action: If buyer is under a different registering authority, issue NOC (Form 28)
time_limit: NOC deemed granted if no communication within 30 days (MV Act s.48)
on_reject: NOC may be withheld only for recorded cause (dues, blacklist, court/enforcement hold).
note: Form 28 NOC required for movement to another registering authority; CMVR rr.58-60. Skip for same-RTO transfers.

action: Report the transfer to the registering authority in Form 29
note: Statutory duty of the transferor to report within 14 days of transfer; delay attracts penalty.

action: Apply to register the transfer in Form 30 with fee and documents
time_limit: 14 days same authority / 45 days different authority (MV Act s.50(1)(b))
note: Transferee reports within 14 days (same registering authority) or 45 days (different authority); typically filed online via Parivahan/VAHAN then document verification.

action: Receive application, verify Forms 29/30, documents, fee; forward file
on_reject: Deficiency memo issued; applicant re-submits missing papers.
note: Scrutiny/data-entry against VAHAN record before officer decision.

action: Inspect vehicle / verify chassis and engine number where required
on_reject: Mismatch halts transfer pending clarification.
note: Physical/particulars verification is commonly required, especially on inter-state re-registration.

post_name: Assistant/Additional Regional Transport Officer (ARTO), registering authority
action: Approve transfer and endorse/re-issue RC in buyer's name
on_reject: Rejection recorded with reasons; appealable to Transport Commissioner.
note: Registering authority endorses transfer of ownership on the RC under CMVR r.57 and updates VAHAN.

action: Issue updated Registration Certificate to the buyer (print/Smart Card)
note: Smart-card RC dispatched or downloadable; VAHAN record now shows new owner.

action: Self-check eligibility: UP resident widow, age 18-60, income below rural 46080 / urban 56460 ceiling.
note: Income ceilings ₹46,080 (rural)/₹56,460 (urban) are widely cited; some recent SSPY notifications state a ₹2 lakh ceiling. No remarriage; not drawing another pension.

post_name: Controller of Examinations / Registrar (University Examination Branch)
action: Apply to issuing university for degree genuineness verification / verification letter
on_reject: Re-apply with correct enrolment/roll details; obtain duplicate if certificate is disputed
note: Many universities emboss the certificate or issue a sealed verification letter; e-Sanad requires the university to be an onboarded issuing authority.

post_name: Controller of Examinations / Registrar (University Examination Branch)
action: University confirms records and certifies the degree as genuine
on_reject: Escalate to Vice-Chancellor's office if records mismatch
note: Genuineness verification is the base of the chain; on e-Sanad this verification is done digitally by the university before MEA acts.

post_name: Attestation Cell, State Higher / Technical Education Department (Secretariat)
action: Submit degree for state-level education-department authentication before MEA
on_reject: Attach university verification proof; use e-Sanad if the department is onboarded
note: State step MEA requires for education documents; in some states routed via a designated SDM/collectorate attestation counter or GAD/Home cell instead of a Secretariat counter.

action: Attest/authenticate the certificate at the notified state counter where required
on_reject: Return for university reverification; correct notarisation
note: In several North-Indian states the SDM or a designated officer provides the pre-MEA state attestation for personal/education documents. Applies only where the state uses this route.

post_name: Deputy Secretary / Section Officer, State Education Department
action: Sign and stamp state-level attestation on the certificate
on_reject: Rectify document/route errors flagged at counter
note: This state attestation is the precondition MEA checks before central apostille/attestation.

action: Lodge apostille/attestation application; submit document, passport, fee
on_reject: Provide missing state attestation or ID; resubmit
note: MEA no longer accepts direct walk-ins; documents are collected, forwarded to MEA and returned via authorised service providers, or lodged through e-Sanad.

action: Prerequisite: hold a valid 40%+ disability certificate / UDID from the medical board.
on_reject: Apply/re-assess for disability certificate at the CMO's medical board before proceeding.
note: Certificate already held per the citizen input; UDID (Unique Disability ID) card is preferred where available.

action: Issue/verify income certificate confirming family income within the rural/urban ceiling.
note: UP ceiling: Rs 46,080 rural / Rs 56,460 urban per year. Income certificate is a required enclosure; issued via Lekhpal/SDM through the e-district service.

action: Countersign/issue the income and residence (domicile) certificates for the applicant.
note: Income certificate is issued by Lekhpal/SDM; domicile proof also required. These are prerequisite certificates, not the pension decision.

action: Register and submit disability-pension application online on the state pension portal with enclosures.
note: UP: sspy-up.gov.in, choose 'Divyang and Leprosy Pension' > Apply Online. Uttarakhand: ssp.uk.gov.in disability grant form. Enclose disability certificate, Aadhaar, domicile, income certificate, bank passbook, photo. Guardian may apply where the applicant cannot.

action: Field-verify applicant's disability, residence and circumstances at village/ward level.
on_reject: Applicant may correct/resubmit documents flagged at verification.
note: Rural verification by Gram Panchayat / block functionary; in urban areas a municipal/ward-level officer performs the equivalent field check. Portal notes verification by 'Gram Panchayat/Block/District Social Welfare Office'.

action: Verify the application at block level and forward with recommendation to the district office.
on_reject: Deficiency memo to applicant; resubmit corrected documents.
note: Block-tier verification/forwarding on the pension portal before district scrutiny; exact routing varies by district.

post_name: District Disability Welfare Officer / District Social Welfare Officer (Zila Divyangjan/Samaj Kalyan Adhikari)
action: Scrutinise application and documents; validate disability certificate against issuing medical board.
on_reject: Return for correction; applicant may re-submit or seek grievance redress on the portal.
note: The District Disability/Social Welfare Officer runs the scheme locally (UP: Divyangjan Sashaktikaran Adhikari; Uttarakhand: DSWO at Vikas Bhawan). This is the substantive district scrutiny step.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Give oral/written info of the cognizable offence; SHO must record and register the FIR.
time_limit: Immediate (no waiting period for cognizable offences)
on_reject: If SHO refuses, escalate in writing to the Superintendent of Police (Step 4) under BNSS S.173(4).
note: BNSS S.173: officer in charge must reduce cognizable-offence information to writing, read it back, and register the FIR. Info can be given electronically (e-FIR), signed within 3 days. For specified sexual offences a woman officer records the statement.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Register FIR in station records and issue a free copy of the FIR to the complainant.
note: BNSS S.173(2): the informant is entitled to a copy of the recorded information free of cost. Filing an FIR carries no fee.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: For offences punishable 3-7 years, may hold a 14-day preliminary enquiry with senior officer's permission before FIR.
on_reject: Enquiry cannot indefinitely delay registration; if suppressed, escalate to SP (Step 4).
note: BNSS S.173(3): with prior permission of an officer not below DSP rank, the SHO may conduct a preliminary enquiry (within 14 days) into whether a prima facie cognizable case exists for 3-7 year offences. For grave offences FIR must be registered forthwith.

post_name: Superintendent of Police (SP) / Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP)
action: Send substance of complaint in writing by registered post to SP if SHO refused to register.
on_reject: If SP takes no action, approach the Judicial Magistrate under BNSS S.175(3) (Step 6).
note: BNSS S.173(4): a person aggrieved by refusal to record information may send its substance in writing, by post, to the SP; in commissionerate cities the equivalent authority is the DCP. Keep the postal receipt as proof.

post_name: Station House Officer (SHO), jurisdictional police station
action: Give oral/written account; officer must reduce it to writing, read back, obtain signature, register FIR
on_reject: If refused, escalate under s.173(4) to the Superintendent of Police (step 4)
note: For a cognizable offence, registration is mandatory under s.173(1) BNSS — no discretion; Lalita Kumari v. Govt. of U.P. (2014) 2 SCC 1 makes registration compulsory. Give jurisdiction over the place of offence, but s.173(1) applies 'irrespective of the area' (zero-FIR): any station must register and transfer later.

action: Issue the free copy of the registered FIR to the complainant immediately
on_reject: Demand the copy in writing; non-issue is itself grounds for the s.173(4) SP complaint
note: s.173(1) BNSS entitles the informant to a copy of the FIR free of cost, forthwith.

post_name: Deputy Superintendent of Police (permission) / Station House Officer (enquiry)
action: Where FIR not immediately registered, verify whether a 14-day preliminary enquiry lawfully applies before deciding registration
on_reject: If enquiry not concluded or wrongly invoked, escalate to SP under s.173(4)
note: s.173(3) BNSS permits a preliminary enquiry ONLY for offences punishable 3-7 years, with prior permission of a DSP-level officer, capped at 14 days. It is not a general escape from mandatory registration. NOTE: for a purely non-cognizable offence, s.174 BNSS applies instead — police only enter it in a register and cannot investigate without magistrate order; the refusal-to-register FIR framing is specific to cognizable offences.

post_name: Superintendent of Police (SP) — or Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in a Police Commissionerate
action: Send substance of the information in writing by (registered) post; SP must investigate or direct a subordinate
on_reject: If SP remedy yields no result, apply to the Judicial Magistrate under s.175(3) (step 6)
note: s.173(4) BNSS: a person aggrieved by the SHO's refusal sends the substance in writing, by post, to the SP; if satisfied a cognizable offence is disclosed the SP shall investigate or direct a subordinate who then has SHO powers. Registered post gives proof of submission. Recourse to the SP is now a MANDATORY precondition before the magistrate route.

post_name: First Appellate Officer (DIG range) then Second Appellate Officer (Zonal ADG), U.P. Police — Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam
action: Optionally lodge a service-guarantee appeal for non-action within the stipulated time
time_limit: First appeal within 30 days; second appeal within 60 days
on_reject: Second appeal to Zonal ADG; independent of, and parallel to, the s.175(3) magistrate route
note: U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 gives time-bound service delivery with a First Appeal (30 days) and Second Appeal (60 days). UP Police designate the First Appellate Officer (DIG) and Second Appellate Officer (Zonal ADG) for police-service grievances; useful for non-action/delay but does not itself compel FIR registration — the statutory compulsion route is s.175(3).

action: Inspect premises; check hygiene, licence/registration, storage and expiry of stock
note: FSA 2006 s.38 empowers the FSO to enter, inspect and seize; verifies FBO licence/registration under s.31.

action: Signs/issues the official allotment order directing the private school to admit the allotted child
on_reject: school refusal escalated to BSA/CEO
note: binding order under s.12(1)(c); school cannot charge fees

action: Fill TC particulars: DOB, admission/leaving dates, class, conduct, standing
note: Entries must match the admission register; errors propagate to the new school and board records.

action: Issues public notice and opens objection period for other heirs/claimants
note: Mandatory public notice / munadi at the tehsil and village so any co-heir or claimant may object before entry. Rule 35 UP Revenue Code Rules 2016.

post_name: Reader / Bench Clerk of the District Court
action: Publish notice in newspaper and on court notice board; open objection window
note: Objection window commonly ~45 days by local practice; the Act fixes no uniform number - treat as typical, not statutory.

action: File objections/rival claims within the notice period, if any
note: s.373: if there is contention as to right, court may decide it or grant to applicant with best prima facie title. Contested matters run much longer.

action: Hear the petition and any objections; determine entitlement (s.373)
on_reject: Petition dismissed or grant to a rival with better title; challengeable on appeal (s.384)
note: s.373(3)-(4): where right is contested and cannot be summarily decided, court grants to the person with prima facie best title.

action: Furnish surety/security bond as directed before certificate issues (s.375)
on_reject: Certificate withheld until adequate security is furnished
note: s.375: court may require bond with surety to indemnify persons who may be entitled, as a condition of grant.

action: Grant the succession certificate specifying the debts and securities (ss.373, 374)
on_reject: Appeal to the High Court under s.384
note: s.374: certificate specifies debts/securities and empowers the holder to receive interest/dividends or negotiate/transfer them. This is the decisive grant.

action: Reviews AE scrutiny, confirms structural/FAR compliance, recommends the file upward
on_reject: returns file with objections
note: engineering-side recommendation before planning vetting

post_name: Building / Town Planning Officer (Nagar Niyojan Adhikari)
action: Vets the plan for zoning, land-use, master-plan and planning-norm conformity
on_reject: planning objection returned to applicant
note: town-planning vetting

action: Final technical clearance for large/high-value projects exceeding delegated limits
on_reject: returns with technical objection
note: only for cases above lower officers' delegated FAR/area limit

action: Sanctions plans within the delegated financial/area limit on the Commissioner's behalf
on_reject: rejection with recorded reasons
note: delegated sanctioning authority for routine/mid-size plans

action: Grants final sanction for plans beyond the delegated limit; approves the permit
on_reject: rejection with recorded reasons; appeal within 30 days
note: head sanctioning authority (or Vice-Chairman in a development authority)

action: Issues the stamped sanction letter / permit and sanctioned drawings via OBPAS
on_reject: deemed-approval if not communicated within statutory time; appeal within 30 days of rejection
note: deemed-approval provision under Ease of Doing Business

action: Citizen submits application and documents; clerk registers and issues acknowledgement receipt
note: intake at Supply Office / e-district / CSC counter

action: Conducts field/home verification of the family, residence and eligibility details
on_reject: adverse verification report can lead to rejection
note: primary NFSA field verification; visits the applicant's home

action: Sign and seal the certificate; office issues certified copy to holder
note: Sealed certificate is conclusive as against the debtors paying in good faith (s.381). Extension for further securities is via s.379.

action: Alternative lighter route: approve legal-heir certificate for pension/PF/insurance/mutation after field check
on_reject: Escalate to SDM / Additional District Magistrate or state grievance portal
note: For pensions, gratuity, PF, insurance and property mutation a revenue legal-heir certificate suffices - issued via state e-district after Lekhpal/Patwari verification and Tehsildar/SDM approval; not a court certificate. Applies under UP/Uttarakhand RTS timelines (~15-45 days). Choose court route only for debts/securities of an intestate.

action: Field-verify heirs and residence for the legal-heir certificate before Tehsildar approval
on_reject: Adverse verification report; applicant may re-apply with corrected proof
note: Village revenue functionary conducts ground verification; report feeds the Tehsildar's decision on the revenue legal-heir certificate.

post_name: Registering Authority - Regional Transport Officer / ARTO
action: Assign a new registration number and re-register if vehicle moved from another state.
note: Only on inter-state transfer: after NOC (Form 28) the new state assigns a fresh registration mark and levies re-registration road tax (with possible refund of unexpired tax from the origin state). Same-state transfer keeps the existing number.

action: Re-issue the Registration Certificate showing the buyer as registered owner.
note: Updated smart-card RC is issued/dispatched. Buyer should verify ownership on the Vahan portal; seller retains the dated Form 29 acknowledgement as proof of reported sale to defend against future liability.

action: Report the transfer to the registering authority within statutory window to end own liability.
note: MV Act s.50(1)(a): transferor must report within 14 days. Failure keeps seller liable for the vehicle and attracts penalty; keep the dated Form 29 acknowledgement.

action: File Form 30 with RC, insurance, PUC, ID/address proof, sale note, and clearance of dues.
time_limit: 14 days if same registering authority; 45 days if a different one (MV Act s.50(1)(b))
note: Filed on Vahan/Parivahan portal or at the RTO/ARTO. Requires valid insurance in buyer's name, current Pollution-Under-Control (PUC) certificate, and address proof. Late filing attracts penalty per rules.

action: If loan cleared, issue Form 35 to terminate hypothecation; else lender consent required.
note: MV Act s.51 / CMV rule 61: a hypothecated (financed) vehicle needs Form 35 (with No-Objection) to remove the lender's charge before or with transfer, or the transfer records continuing hypothecation.

post_name: Registering Authority (RTO of origin) - Regional Transport Officer / ARTO
action: For inter-state/inter-RTO purchase, issue No-Objection Certificate (Form 28) after dues/theft check.
time_limit: NOC deemed granted if no objection within 30 days (MV Act s.48)
on_reject: Apply to Transport Commissioner if NOC wrongly withheld
note: Only if the vehicle is registered at a different RTO or another state. Form 28 (3 copies) confirms no dues/no criminal record so the vehicle can move to the new jurisdiction. Not needed for same-RTO transfer.

action: Scrutinise Forms 29/30, documents, insurance, PUC, tax and fee payment.
on_reject: Deficiency memo issued for buyer to cure documents
note: Verifies completeness and that transfer fee and any transfer road-tax/re-registration charges are paid. Fees are set by state schedule and vary; verify current amount on Vahan.

action: Inspect vehicle where required (re-registration/inter-state or roadworthiness check).
on_reject: Rectify defects and re-present vehicle
note: Physical inspection is commonly required for re-registration or inter-state transfer to verify chassis/engine number against records; may be waived for routine same-RTO transfers. Official designation: Motor Vehicle Inspector (MVI).

post_name: Registering Authority - Regional Transport Officer / ARTO
action: Record the change of ownership in the register and approve the transfer.
time_limit: As per UP Janhit Guarantee / Uttarakhand Right to Service schedule (commonly 7-30 working days)
on_reject: Written rejection appealable to the State/Deputy Transport Commissioner under MV Act s.50
note: This is the decisive act: MV Act s.50(2) - the registering authority makes the entry of transfer. The RTO/ARTO is a field office of the State Transport Department (secretariat-department class).

action: Register the death and obtain the death certificate from panchayat (rural) or municipal registrar (urban).
on_reject: Apply with late-registration affidavit; escalate to District Registrar (Births & Deaths).
note: Registration of Births and Deaths Act 1969. Urban: apply to Municipal Commissioner (Nagar Ayukt)/registrar instead. Nothing downstream proceeds without this.

action: File varasat application online at vaad.up.nic.in (RCCMS) or e-District/e-Sathi, or at Jan Seva Kendra.
on_reject: Resubmit; use CSC/Jan Seva Kendra assistance if portal upload fails.
note: UP routes agricultural-land inheritance as varasat (mutation) through the Revenue Court system (RCCMS), NOT a standalone certificate. For dues/pension file the Surviving Member Certificate on e-District in parallel.

action: Attach death certificate, applicant ID/address proof, heir list affidavit, khatauni/khasra extract, ration card.
on_reject: Add missing documents on portal query; affidavit of all legal heirs on stamp paper is commonly required.
note: Exact list varies by tehsil and by purpose (property mutation vs dues). Self-declaration naming ALL heirs is central.

action: Conduct field inquiry (mauka) verifying death, heirs, and possession; file spot-verification report.
on_reject: If report adverse, submit objections/evidence before the Tehsildar; request re-inquiry.
note: Lekhpal is the UP revenue field officer; this is the step that most often causes delay.

action: Publish public notice inviting objections from other claimants to the inheritance.
on_reject: If objection filed, case is contested and heard as a revenue suit (vaad) before the court.
note: UP Revenue Code 2006 §§33-34: notice/objection period before recording succession in records.

action: Hear the varasat case and pass order recording legal heirs in the revenue records (khatauni).
on_reject: Appeal to SDM (Assistant Collector), then ADM/Collector, then Commissioner, then Board of Revenue.
note: UP Revenue Code 2006 §35. Tehsildar/Naib-Tehsildar sits as the revenue court; order effects the mutation (dakhil-kharij).

action: Issue the Surviving Member / legal-heir certificate for claiming dues, pension and benefits.
on_reject: Appeal to SDM; file delay complaint under Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011.
note: Parallel e-District instrument to the property mutation; downloaded from the portal after Tehsildar approval.

action: Adult of a rural household applies (plain paper, prescribed form, or orally) to the Gram Panchayat for household registration.
note: You register as a HOUSEHOLD, not an individual; the card covers all adult members. Oral application must be reduced to writing by the GP. Application may also be made to the Programme Officer. Schedule II, para 1-2.

action: Gram Panchayat (Secretary with Gram Rozgar Sahayak) verifies applicants are local residents and adults of the household.
on_reject: Complaint to Programme Officer (BDO) at block if verification is arbitrarily withheld.
note: Light residence/adult-membership check only. NOT a means test - MGNREGA is universal for rural households, not income-targeted. Schedule II, para 3.

action: Gram Panchayat registers the household and issues the Job Card with photos and a unique registration number, free of cost.
on_reject: Non-issue is a grievance: escalate to Programme Officer (BDO) at block; then District Programme Coordinator; then MGNREGA Ombudsman.
note: Job Card must be issued within 15 days of registration, free of cost. This is the decisive step that creates the entitlement. Schedule II, para 4-5. Keep the card - it is presented to demand work.

action: Card-holder submits a written application for work to the Gram Panchayat or Programme Officer and obtains a dated receipt.
on_reject: If receipt is refused, apply directly to the Programme Officer (BDO); the demand can be sent by post.
note: Having the card is NOT the same as having work. The dated receipt starts the legal 15-day clock for the guarantee. Minimum 14 days' continuous work may be sought. Schedule II, para 6-8.

action: Programme Officer (usually the BDO) allots work and directs the Gram Panchayat to provide employment within 5 km of residence.
on_reject: Failure to provide work triggers unemployment-allowance liability (step 6); complaint to District Programme Coordinator / Ombudsman.
note: Employment must be provided within 15 days of the work-demand (or the later date sought). Work ordinarily within 5 km; beyond 5 km, extra wages payable. Section 3; Schedule II. In UP the Programme Officer is generally the BDO.

action: If no work provided within 15 days, Programme Officer sanctions daily unemployment allowance to the applicant.
on_reject: Non-payment of allowance is itself a grievance: escalate to District Programme Coordinator, then MGNREGA Ombudsman.
note: Unemployment allowance is the enforcement teeth of the guarantee; it is a State liability. Rate is State-notified (not below one-fourth of wage for first 30 days, one-half thereafter). Section 7; Schedule II.

action: If GP refuses registration or the card, escalate the grievance to the Programme Officer at the Block.
on_reject: Next level: District Programme Coordinator.
note: The Programme Officer (Section 15) is the supervisory authority over Gram Panchayats for MGNREGA at the block. In UP this is the BDO.

action: Conduct field/physical verification of widowhood, residence and household income; report back.
on_reject: Adverse report can be contested before the SDM/DPO with documentary proof.
note: Village-level verifier; Gram Panchayat / Ward may endorse. Exact title state-specific but Lekhpal is the UP designation.

post_name: District Social Welfare Officer / Women Welfare Officer (block-level review)
action: Scrutinise verified application and forward eligible cases to the district sanction committee.
on_reject: Deficiency memo to applicant; escalate to District Probation Officer.
note: Second-tier scrutiny after field verification, per SSPY four-phase timeline.

post_name: District Probation Officer (DPO) / District-level Sanction Committee under the District Magistrate
action: Approve (sanction) the pension and add the beneficiary to the widow-pension roll.
on_reject: Written reasons issued; represent to DPO, then District Magistrate grievance cell; CPGRAMS; RTS appeal where applicable.
note: In UP the widow pension is run by the Women Welfare Dept (Mahila Kalyan Vibhag); the District Probation Officer is the district nodal officer and the sanction committee sits under the DM/Collector.

post_name: District Probation Officer (DPO) / Treasury via PFMS
action: Release sanctioned pension by DBT to the Aadhaar-linked account; ₹3,000 quarterly.
time_limit: Fund transfer via PFMS ~1 month after sanction; thereafter quarterly.
on_reject: Report non-credit to the DPO / bank; check status on sspy-up.gov.in with registration ID.
note: ₹1,000/month (₹500 state + ₹500 central), paid quarterly as ₹3,000 by DBT/PFMS. Rescinds if beneficiary remarries or income rises.

post_name: District Probation Officer (DPO) grievance cell / District Magistrate (Collector) grievance cell
action: If delayed or rejected, file grievance; track via portal, DPO helpline, or IGRS/CPGRAMS.
on_reject: Escalate to Director, Women Welfare Directorate; then CPGRAMS; ultimately a writ petition to the Allahabad High Court.
note: SSPY helpline 1800-419-0001; UP IGRS (jansunwai.up.nic.in) and CPGRAMS are the standing grievance channels.

post_name: First / Second Appellate Officer under U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011
action: Where the service is RTS-notified, appeal breach of statutory time limit for a directed decision.
time_limit: Appeals decided within the periods fixed by the Adhiniyam (typically 30 days each tier).
on_reject: Second appeal; the appellate authority may impose a penalty (₹250/day up to ₹5,000) on the defaulting designated officer.
note: The RTS route squarely covers the prerequisite certificates (income/domicile) and death registration; whether the pension sanction itself is a notified service varies by the current UP RTS schedule - verify per district notification.

action: Gather supporting documents from the UIDAI Regulations Schedule for name (PoI) and address (PoA).
note: Name: marriage certificate or gazette notification or other accepted PoI in new name. Address: PoA in new name, OR Head-of-Family (HoF) proof + Proof of Relationship. Acceptable-document list is Schedule to the Aadhaar (Enrolment and Update) Regulations, 2016 — verify current list.

action: Choose channel: myAadhaar online portal (address only) or Aadhaar Seva Kendra in person (name + address).
note: Online supports address update only and requires a registered mobile for OTP. Name update generally requires a centre visit. Name may be updated at most twice on ordinary documents; further changes need gazette notification.

action: Book appointment or walk in at an Aadhaar Seva Kendra / enrolment centre for in-person update.
note: Centres are UIDAI-run or registrar-operated (often hosted at post offices/banks). Appointment booking available online where offered.

action: Fill Aadhaar Update Form with corrected name and address; capture applicant's biometrics.
note: Operator uses Update Client Standard/Lite. Post is a UIDAI-registered enrolment-agency operator, not a listed UP-revenue post (task is run by UIDAI, a central authority).

action: Verify submitted documents against UIDAI Schedule; scan originals; collect the update fee.
on_reject: Operator refuses if documents insufficient; applicant re-lodges with correct PoI/PoA, or escalates via 1947 if wrongly refused.
note: Demographic-update fee is a fixed UIDAI charge (Rs 50 per update per official charge schedule; Rs 75 is also cited — verify current amount). Online and in-person fees may differ.

action: Issue acknowledgement carrying the Update Request Number (URN) or Enrolment ID (EID).
note: In-person: 14-digit URN/EID on receipt. Online: Service Request Number (SRN) sent by SMS. Keep it — it is how status is tracked.

action: Review the request and documents; validate the demographic change against records.
time_limit: 30 days (90% of requests); up to 90 days outer bound
note: Central UIDAI back-end processing. Online-uploaded documents are verified at this stage rather than at the counter. Post is a UIDAI central function, outside the listed UP-revenue posts.

action: Approve or reject the update; on approval, commit the corrected name/address to the Aadhaar record.
on_reject: Rejection reason is stated; applicant resubmits with stronger documents, then escalates via 1947 / UIDAI grievance portal / regional office if unresolved.
note: This is the decisive step that grants the request. UIDAI is the central statutory authority under s.54 of the Aadhaar Act, 2016.

action: Track status by URN/SRN and download the updated e-Aadhaar PDF once approved.
note: Status at myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in Check Aadhaar Update Status. Fresh e-Aadhaar can be downloaded and printed once the change reflects.

action: Escalate stalled, wrongly-rejected, or refused requests via 1947, help@uidai.gov.in, or the grievance portal.
on_reject: Further escalation to the regional UIDAI office; ultimately RTI or writ remedy.
note: If processing exceeds ~90 days, call 1947 or email help@uidai.gov.in. Regional UIDAI office is the next tier. Grievance mechanism under UIDAI, not a district/municipal office.

post_name: District Programme Coordinator (District Magistrate / CEO Zila Panchayat)
action: District Programme Coordinator reviews unresolved grievances on registration, card issue, work, or wage/allowance.
on_reject: Next level: MGNREGA Ombudsman for the district.
note: District Programme Coordinator (Section 14) is the District Magistrate / CEO of the Zila Panchayat - the district-level authority. Real designation noted as it falls outside the standard post list.

action: Independent Ombudsman receives and adjudicates complaints on non-registration, card denial, delayed work, or unpaid allowance/wages.
on_reject: Parallel routes: State MGNREGA helpline and Social Audit before the Gram Sabha (Section 17).
note: Every district has an independent MGNREGA Ombudsman (Ombudsman Rules/Guidelines, 2009) for grievance redressal. Real designation noted as it is outside the standard post list.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: File a police complaint only if there is criminal intimidation, mischief/damage, or a breach-of-peace threat.
on_reject: Police normally redirect a pure boundary dispute to revenue/civil courts; if there is a threat of violence, seek preventive action from the Executive Magistrate (SDM) under CrPC/BNSS public-order powers.
note: A civil boundary dispute is not itself a police matter; the police/magistrate route is for criminal acts or imminent breach of peace accompanying the encroachment. Section 145-type preventive orders on possession are passed by the Executive Magistrate, not the SHO.

action: Where title is genuinely contested, file a civil suit for declaration, permanent injunction and possession.
on_reject: Appeal within the civil hierarchy (District Judge → High Court) per CPC; interim injunction can restrain further construction pending trial.
note: Specific Relief Act, 1963 (declaration + permanent injunction) with CPC possession is the definitive remedy when ownership itself — not merely the boundary line — is in dispute. This is the final authority where revenue demarcation cannot resolve competing title claims. Contested suits commonly run for years.

post_name: Chief Inspector (Labour Department), UP Shops & Establishments Act
action: On being satisfied fee is deposited and particulars are in order, register the establishment.
on_reject: Written representation to the Chief Inspector; then appeal to the appellate authority under the Act (Labour Commissioner's office).
note: Statutory registering authority: 'The Chief Inspector shall, on being satisfied that the prescribed fee has been deposited, register the shop or commercial establishment' (India Code / PRS). Includes Deputy Chief Inspector / Inspector.

action: Enter the shop in the statutory register and issue the Registration Certificate.
time_limit: Typically 7-15 working days from valid application
note: Chief Inspector maintains the register of all shops and commercial establishments (Sec 5 read with rules); certificate is issued digitally.

action: File Section 80 land-use-change application to SDM via UP e-district portal with documents
note: Attach khatauni/record of rights, khasra number, site map, current land-revenue receipts, ID/address proof; pay conversion charge as assessed.

action: Register application, check completeness of documents and fee, forward to SDM office
on_reject: Application returned for missing documents or unpaid conversion charge before processing.
note: Intake and scrutiny at the tehsil/SDM registry; generates application/reference number for tracking.

action: Mark application to Tehsildar/Lekhpal for field verification and report
note: SDM (Sub-Divisional Officer) is the competent authority under Section 80 UP Revenue Code for declaring change of land use.

action: Inspect the plot; verify ownership, actual current use, boundaries, and no litigation/acquisition
on_reject: Adverse field report (disputed title, ongoing agricultural use in a protected zone, litigation) can lead to refusal.
note: Ground-truthing by the village revenue accountant; confirms khasra entries against physical site.

action: Consolidate Lekhpal report, verify revenue records/khatauni, submit recommendation to SDM
note: Tehsildar collates the field report and revenue-record check into a consolidated report for the SDM.

action: Publish public notice inviting objections to the proposed land-use change
on_reject: Sustained valid objections (e.g. zoning conflict, public land, encroachment) can lead to rejection.
note: Objection/public-notice stage under Section 80 procedure; also allows master-plan/zoning consistency to be tested.

post_name: District Town Planner / Development Authority (Vikas Pradhikaran)
action: Confirm master-plan zoning permits residential use for the plot (if in planning area)
on_reject: Land zoned agricultural-only, green belt, or water body is refused here.
note: Applies where the plot lies inside a development-authority or regulated/planning area; skipped for purely rural gram-panchayat land outside any master plan.

action: Assess and require payment of conversion charge / bhu-parivartan shulk before final order
on_reject: Non-payment of assessed conversion charge halts the order.
note: Conversion charge is a state-set formula, commonly linked to circle rate of the converted (residential) use.

action: Pass Section 80 order declaring the land use changed to non-agricultural (residential)
time_limit: 90 days (deemed permission under Section 80(2) if no order passed)
on_reject: Appeal against refusal to the Additional Commissioner/Commissioner, then Board of Revenue under the Revenue Code.
note: Sanctioning act. Section 80(2) provides deemed permission if the SDM does not decide within the prescribed period (90 days).

action: Mutate revenue records (khatauni) to record the changed non-agricultural land use
note: Post-order record update so the khatauni reflects residential use; prerequisite for building-plan sanction.

action: Apply for building-plan / map sanction to development authority, Nagar Nigam, or Gram Panchayat
on_reject: Map sanction refused if plans breach building bye-laws/setbacks/FAR.
note: Separate downstream approval; only after Section 80 conversion and mutation can construction be legally sanctioned.

action: Escalation: file appeal against refusal or fee assessment; use RTPS grievance if deadline missed
on_reject: Onward appeal to Board of Revenue; writ petition in the Allahabad/Uttarakhand High Court as last resort.
note: Revenue Code appeal ladder SDM -> Additional Commissioner/Commissioner -> Board of Revenue; parallel: UP Jansunwai/IGRS grievance and RTI. Also usable if the 90-day RTPS/Section 80(2) deadline is breached.

post_name: Head Master / Principal (In-charge, School Mid-Day Meal)
action: Submit dated written complaint at school; inspect meal register and menu board; keep copy.
note: Head Master is the on-site officer answerable for the day's meal, quantity and quality. Ask to see the daily MDM register, menu/notice board and food-grain receipt. If a child fell ill, seek medical help first and record it.

action: Raise the complaint before the SMC (includes parents) as local oversight forum.
note: Under the RTE Act, 2009 the SMC monitors school functioning including the mid-day meal; parents are members and can formally minute the grievance and demand corrective action.

post_name: Block Education Officer (BEO) / Khand Shiksha Adhikari
action: Escalate in writing to the block MDM in-charge if school does not resolve.
note: The block education office supervises the school kitchen, cook-cum-helpers and conversion-cost/foodgrain supply; the block-level MDM co-ordinator/nodal officer is the first supervisory tier above the school.

action: Route quantity/supply or fund-diversion angle through the block administration.
note: Foodgrain lifting, kitchen infrastructure and cook honorarium flow partly through block/panchayat administration in UP/Uttarakhand, so the BDO is a parallel block-tier authority for supply-side failures.

post_name: District Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA) / District Education Officer
action: Lodge written complaint with district education officer supervising PM POSHAN.
note: The BSA (basic education) is the district officer directly accountable for mid-day-meal delivery in government primary/upper-primary schools and can order inspection and correction.

action: Report immediately for any food poisoning, contamination or illness from the meal.
note: Any illness/contamination sharply raises priority; the CMO/MO documents the medical cause and can trigger sample testing. Food-safety failures can also go to the district FSSAI/Food Safety Officer.

post_name: PM POSHAN District Nodal Officer / District Steering-cum-Monitoring Committee
action: File before the district monitoring committee that oversees scheme implementation.
note: PM POSHAN guidelines require a District-level Steering-cum-Monitoring Committee, chaired by the District Magistrate, to monitor quality, quantity and hygiene of meals.

action: Complain to the DM's office as the district-accountable chair of the monitoring committee.
note: The DM/Collector chairs the district PM POSHAN monitoring committee and is the senior accountable district authority who can direct all subordinate offices to act.

action: Issues the physical/e-job card with photo to the household
note: job card valid 5 years; entitles up to 100 days work/year

action: Confirm eligibility: UP resident, family income up to limit, max girls per family.
note: Standing scheme rule caps girl children benefiting per family and sets a household income ceiling (historically Rs 3 lakh); verify current ceiling and child-count cap on mksy.up.gov.in — the FY 2024-25 revision may have updated these.

action: Assist applicant with documents and stage selection; guide offline route if online unavailable.
note: First-contact field functionary of the Bal Vikas / ICDS department at village/ward level; the fallback offline application is filed through the Anganwadi/CDPO office where online access is limited.

action: Register on mksy.up.gov.in, create citizen login, enter girl/applicant details, select stage.
note: Online submission on the official MKSY citizen portal is immediate. Offline application via the block CDPO / District DPO office is the notified fallback.

action: Upload stage-milestone documents: birth/immunization record or school admission/bonafide certificate.
note: Each stage requires the document proving that life-event milestone (birth, immunization, Class 1/6/9 admission, Class 12/degree/diploma admission). A fresh claim is filed as each milestone is reached.

action: Verify applicant particulars, eligibility and uploaded documents at block level.
on_reject: Application returned to applicant for correction/resubmission of documents.
note: Block-level officer of the Bal Vikas / ICDS department; performs the first verification tier before forwarding to the district. Real designation for this scheme (not among the six generic office classes).

action: Scrutinise verified application and sanction the stage benefit for eligible girl child.
on_reject: Applicant informed of rejection with reason; may correct and re-apply, or escalate via grievance route (step 9).
note: District nodal / sanctioning authority for MKSY under the Directorate of Women Welfare / ICDS — confirmed as the district contact on balvikasup.gov.in. This is the decisive approval step.

action: Release sanctioned amount by Direct Benefit Transfer to mother's/guardian's bank account.
note: Payment is by DBT to the linked bank account after sanction. Benefit is one instalment of the cumulative total (revised to Rs 25,000 across stages w.e.f. FY 2024-25).

action: At each next milestone, re-file a fresh stage claim with that stage's document.
note: The benefit is staged over the girl's life (birth to higher-secondary/graduation); the applicant repeats steps 3-7 at each qualifying milestone. Exact number/merger of stages was revised in FY 2024-25 — confirm current structure on the portal.

action: If stuck or rejected, escalate via portal grievance/helpline, DPO office, then Jansunwai (IGRS).
note: Escalation ladder: Anganwadi/Supervisor -> CDPO -> DPO -> Directorate of Women Welfare; plus the MKSY portal grievance/helpline and the UP Jansunwai / IGRS (jansunwai.up.nic.in) grievance portal.

action: File a statutory NFSA grievance; DGRO investigates and may recommend relief.
on_reject: Appeal to the State Food Commission (Step 11).
note: NFSA, 2013 Sec. 15: every district has a DGRO to redress grievances over entitlements, which include the mid-day meal (Sec. 5). The DGRO can recommend relief, including a food-security allowance under Sec. 8 where the meal was not supplied.

post_name: CPGRAMS / State PM POSHAN Grievance Portal (Dealing Officer)
action: Lodge parallel online grievance for a tracked, time-bound reference number.
note: Use the national CPGRAMS portal (pgportal.gov.in) and/or the UP Mid Day Meal Authority (upmdm.up.nic.in) / state education grievance portal; these generate a tracking number and route to the responsible office. Confirm the current helpline for the citizen's district.

action: Appeal unresolved NFSA grievance; Commission can penalize the defaulting official.
on_reject: Approach the State/National Commission for Protection of Child Rights or the High Court.
note: NFSA, 2013 Sec. 16: the State Food Commission hears appeals against the DGRO and may impose a penalty on a public servant/authority who fails to comply with the relief recommended.

post_name: State PM POSHAN Directorate / State Project Director (UP Mid Day Meal Authority)
action: Escalate to state scheme directorate for systemic or repeated failures.
note: In UP the Uttar Pradesh Mid Day Meal Authority (MDM Pradhikaran) / State Project Director runs the scheme; in Uttarakhand the state PM POSHAN directorate. Appropriate for policy-level or recurring district failures.

action: Final approval, sanctions the ration card, allots the category and Fair Price Shop
on_reject: rejection with recorded reasons; appeal to DGRO
note: card-issuing authority sitting in the district collectorate

action: NFSA grievance: the District Grievance Redressal Officer hears appeals on rejection or delay
on_reject: further appeal to the State Food Commission (NFSA s.16)
note: NFSA s.14 grievance channel; DGRO role often held by a district officer

post_name: State / National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (SCPCR / NCPCR)
action: Pursue rights-based route for child entitlement violation or safety failure.
note: NCPCR/SCPCR take up mid-day-meal quality, safety and entitlement violations as breaches of the child's rights; a quality/quantity failure is a violation of the child's statutory entitlement.

action: Confirm the road-owning authority (Nagar Nigam vs PWD vs development authority vs NHAI) at the ward/engineering counter.
note: Only the road owner can grant a cut; if not Nagar Nigam's road the file routes to that owner (PWD/NHAI). Decides everything downstream.

action: Submit road-cut application with ownership proof, trench site-plan, and connection details to the Engineering/Jalkal section.
note: For a water pipe the request is usually bundled with the water-connection application to the Jalkal Vibhag (UP) / Jal Sansthan (Uttarakhand); for cable/telecom the utility often applies on the citizen's behalf.

action: Submit written or oral application to Gram Panchayat listing adult household members with photos and residence/age proof.
note: Any adult member of a rural household willing to do unskilled manual work may apply. Application can be on plain paper or prescribed form; oral requests must be recorded. No fee. Under Schedule I/II of MGNREGA.

action: Receive application, issue dated acknowledgement/receipt, and enter details in the registration register.
note: The Gram Rozgar Sevak is the MGNREGA village-level functionary handling day-to-day processing. A dated receipt starts the statutory clock.

action: Verify that applicants are local residents and genuine adult members of a single household.
on_reject: Application returned for correction; applicant may re-apply or escalate to the Programme Officer.
note: Verification is a household-level check (definition of household under the Act). Usually a quick field check by the Rozgar Sevak / Panchayat Secretary.

action: Register the verified household under MGNREGA and assign a unique registration number.
on_reject: If registration refused, applicant escalates to the Programme Officer at the Block.
note: The Gram Panchayat is the statutory registering authority under Section 3 and Schedule II of MGNREGA.

action: Issue the job card with names, photographs, and registration number within 15 days of application.
note: Schedule II mandates issue of the job card within 15 days; the card is valid for 5 years. Photographs are affixed free of cost.

action: Oversee registration and job-card issuance at the Block; verify the Gram Panchayat is issuing cards on time.
note: At the Block level the Programme Officer role is typically held by the Block Development Officer (BDO) and supervises Gram Panchayats under MGNREGA.

action: Submit a written application for work (minimum 14 days continuous) to the Gram Panchayat or Programme Officer.
note: The job card only enables the right; work must be separately demanded in writing. Obtain a dated receipt to establish the 15-day work clock under Section 7.

action: Allot work within 15 days of the demand, ordinarily within 5 km of the village.
on_reject: If work is not provided within 15 days, the applicant is legally entitled to an unemployment allowance under Section 7.
note: Unemployment allowance is a statutory entitlement paid by the State if work is not provided in time. Wages at the notified MGNREGA rate.

post_name: Programme Officer (Block) then District Programme Coordinator (DM / CDO / Zilla Panchayat CEO)
action: Escalate grievance if the card or work is refused or delayed.
note: Grievance ladder: Panchayat Secretary / Gram Rozgar Sevak -> Programme Officer (Block/BDO) -> District Programme Coordinator (District Magistrate or CDO). Use the MGNREGA grievance-redressal mechanism, social audit / Gram Sabha, the state MGNREGA helpline / grievance portal, and RTI to force a paper trail.

action: Report the lapse; get it logged in the school complaint register / SMC.
on_reject: Escalate to the School Management Committee and Block Education Officer
note: Under MDM Rules 2015 the School Head and School Management Committee (SMC, with parent members) are responsible for the meal and first-level redress; use the mandated info-board helpline if displayed. Uncertainty: register/SMC functioning varies by school.

post_name: Block Education Officer (BEO) / Khand Shiksha Adhikari
action: Escalate unresolved complaint; BEO directs supply, cook-cum-helper, or vendor correction.
on_reject: Escalate to District Basic Shiksha Adhikari / District Education Officer
note: Cook-cum-helper and food supply are administered at block level (Block/Nagar MDM in-charge under the Khand Shiksha Adhikari). Uncertainty: exact MDM nodal designation differs by district.

action: Refer supply/vendor or Gram Panchayat-side lapse to the block-level MDM monitoring committee.
on_reject: Escalate to district level
note: The block/mandal-level MDM monitoring committee (MDM Rules 2015) meets fortnightly; the BDO can act on Gram-Panchayat-administered cook/supply arrangements. Optional parallel tier.

post_name: District Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA) / District Education Officer (DEO) - District MDM/PM POSHAN Nodal Officer
action: File written district complaint; DEO orders inspection and directs corrective action.
on_reject: Escalate to District Magistrate / Collector and State Project Director
note: In UP the district MDM authority is the Basic Shiksha Adhikari; the DEO/BSA is district nodal officer for PM POSHAN and convenes district inspection. This is the substantive district office for the task.

action: Chairs district MDM monitoring committee; orders inspection, penalizes vendor, enforces compliance.
on_reject: Approach District Grievance Redressal Officer (NFSA) or State Food Commission
note: The district-level MDM monitoring committee (MDM Rules 2015) meets monthly and is chaired by the DM/Collector, the senior authority who can order inspection and corrective action - the effective decision point once school and block fail.

post_name: Junior Engineer (Avar Abhiyanta), Jal Kal Vibhag
action: Obtain road-cutting NOC (PWD/Nagar Nigam roads dept) if the main lies across a public road.
note: Required where tapping needs excavation of a public carriageway; restoration charge already collected in the demand.

action: File statutory NFSA grievance; DGRO investigates and recommends relief within time-bound process.
on_reject: Appeal to the State Food Commission
note: NFSA 2013 (Sec. 14) makes the mid-day meal a legal entitlement enforceable via the District Grievance Redressal Officer; the State Food Commission (Sec. 15-16) hears appeals and can impose penalty on defaulting officials. Confirm the district's designated DGRO locally.

post_name: State Project Director / State Nodal Officer, PM POSHAN (Samagra Shiksha / Education Dept.)
action: Escalate systemic or unresolved complaint; state directorate directs district and vendor action.
on_reject: File on CPGRAMS or approach State Food Commission
note: State PM POSHAN directorate (UP: Mid-Day Meal Authority / Prayavaran; Uttarakhand: Samagra Shiksha). Many states run a toll-free MDM helpline - number is state-specific; verify locally. Uncertainty: helpline existence/number varies.

post_name: CPGRAMS Grievance Officer (Dept. of School Education & Literacy)
action: File online grievance at pgportal.gov.in; get tracking ID; grievance routed to department.
on_reject: Use the CPGRAMS appeal option after closure if feedback is 'Poor'
note: CPGRAMS is the central 24x7 grievance portal; routes to the relevant department with a tracking number and an appeal path. Parallel channel usable at any time. Timeline is a general target, not a statutory MDM limit.

action: Issue income certificate via e-District after Lekhpal income verification
note: Prerequisite. Applied at Tehsil / e-District (edistrict.up.gov.in). A scheduled service under the UP Janhit Guarantee Act 2011; Lekhpal does the field income check, Tehsildar signs. Rural income ceiling ~Rs 46,080/yr, urban ~Rs 56,460/yr (VERIFY - revisable).

action: Register and submit online pension application on sspy-up.gov.in, upload documents
note: Self-service on the SSPY portal or via a Jan Seva Kendra / CSC. Eligibility: age 60+; not drawing another govt pension for the same person; BPL/low-income. Uploads: Aadhaar, age proof, Aadhaar-linked bank passbook, income certificate, photo, residence proof. Pension commonly ~Rs 1,000/month (VERIFY current rate).

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (District Social Welfare Office)
action: Scrutinise application and documents for completeness at district office
note: The application routes electronically to the District Social Welfare Office (Zila Samaj Kalyan Adhikari karyalaya) for initial scrutiny before field verification.

action: Conduct field verification of applicant age, residence and income
note: Revenue field officer performs on-ground verification. In rural areas the report feeds the BDO; in urban areas the SDM.

action: Verify and forward rural applications with recommendation
note: Rural verification channel. For urban/nagar-nigam applicants the corresponding verifying authority is the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM). One of these forwards a verified recommendation to the DSWO.

action: Verify and forward urban applications with recommendation
note: Urban verification channel (parallel to the BDO for rural). SDM certifies age/residence/income for municipal-area applicants.

post_name: District Social Welfare Officer (Zila Samaj Kalyan Adhikari)
action: Sanction the pension and add beneficiary to the payment roll
note: Sanctioning authority for the district. Sanction typically batched to quarterly cycles. On rejection the applicant is notified with reason via the portal.

post_name: District Social Welfare Officer (Zila Samaj Kalyan Adhikari)
action: Release pension by DBT to Aadhaar-linked bank account each quarter
note: Direct Benefit Transfer, generally paid quarterly. Account must be Aadhaar-seeded. Status trackable on sspy-up.gov.in by application/registration number.

post_name: District Social Welfare Officer (DSWO) / CM Helpline 1076 / IGRS Jansunwai
action: Escalate a pending or rejected application via grievance channels
note: Escalation ladder: track on sspy-up.gov.in, then DSWO office, then DM grievance cell, CM Helpline 1076, and the IGRS/Jansunwai portal (jansunwai.up.nic.in).

post_name: Food Safety Officer / Designated Officer (FSSAI - state Food Safety Dept.)
action: For hygiene/adulteration/illness, lodge a food-safety complaint; officer inspects and can prosecute.
on_reject: Escalate to the Food Safety Commissioner of the state
note: Parallel track under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 where the issue is contamination, adulteration, or illness. If any child fell ill, also involve the Medical Officer (MO) / CMO immediately. Use only for food-safety-specific complaints.

action: Inspect the site: cut length/width, road surface (bituminous vs concrete), and feasibility.
note: Near-universal step; surface type drives the restoration cost. Post is the ward/zone Avar Abhiyanta of the engineering wing.

action: Compute road-restoration (reinstatement) charge plus permit fee from measured cut area and surface.
note: Charge is per the Corporation's schedule of rates/bye-laws; exact rates vary by city (low confidence on figures).

action: Applicant pays the restoration deposit and permit fee; challan/receipt generated.
note: Deposit is the core financial gate paid before digging; the Corporation (not the citizen) usually restores the road afterward. Keep the receipt.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Obtain traffic-police NOC if the cut affects a busy or main road.
note: City-specific; required only for high-traffic/arterial roads. Routed through the traffic police station, not the local SHO in every city.

action: Approve and issue the road-cutting permit for small cuts, specifying validity window and restoration condition.
on_reject: Escalate to Executive Engineer; then First Appellate Authority under the Janhit Guarantee / RTS Act.
note: Approving rank scales with cut size: minor cuts cleared by the ward Avar Abhiyanta.

post_name: High Court of Judicature (Allahabad, UP / Nainital, Uttarakhand)
action: Hear writ petition enforcing the Section 12(1)(c) right as last resort
note: RTE Section 12(1)(c) enforcement is well-litigated; a writ is the final remedy where administrative escalation fails.

action: Approve and sign the permit for larger or main-road cuts (or counter-sign the JE's approval).
on_reject: Escalate to City Engineer / Municipal Commissioner; then RTPS appellate chain.
note: Adhishasi Abhiyanta is the real designation; City Engineer (Mukhya Nagar Abhiyanta) signs off on the largest cuts. Not among the listed post names — official engineering-wing designation used.

action: Citizen executes the cut and lays pipe/cable within the window, through an approved contractor/licensed plumber; JE verifies.
note: Work often restricted to non-monsoon season and to empanelled contractors; notify the section on completion.

action: Corporation restores the road surface (or verifies contractor restoration) and reconciles/refunds the deposit balance.
note: Some cities let a licensed contractor restore and refund; restoration disputes are common, so retain the deposit receipt.

action: Escalate a stalled or wrongly-rejected application to the Commissioner's grievance cell / First Appellate Authority.
on_reject: Second Appellate Authority under U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 / Uttarakhand RTS Act 2011 (penalty Rs 500-5000) and the Jansunwai-Samadhan portal.
note: For notified services the RTPS chain (Designated Officer -> First -> Second Appellate Authority) applies; the road-cut permit itself may not be separately scheduled, but a bundled water connection usually is.

action: Publish the digitally issued certificate for download; applicant displays it at the establishment.
note: Certificate downloadable from Nivesh Mitra. Validity: five financial years; renew before expiry (subsequent renewal up to ten financial years).

action: Choose route: Beneficiary-Led Construction on own plot, AHP/ISSR unit, or loan interest subsidy.
note: Verticals: BLC (build on own land), AHP (buy partnership unit), ARH (rental), ISSR (slum), and Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS, the CLSS successor) via a home loan.

action: Submit online application via pmaymis.gov.in after Aadhaar validation, or through a CSC / ULB counter.
note: Apply at pmaymis.gov.in ('Apply for PMAY-U 2.0'). Process begins with Aadhaar verification. Common Service Centres (CSC) and the ULB assist offline applicants.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (PMAY cell, Nagar Nigam / ULB)
action: Scrutinise application, log documents, flag missing papers for correction.
on_reject: Applicant informed of deficiency to resubmit/correct documents.
note: PMAY / housing cell at the Municipal Corporation (Nagar Nigam) is the ground-level receiving office in urban UP.

action: Field-verify plot, ownership and dwelling; capture geo-tagged photos of the site.
on_reject: Ineligible plot/ownership returned with reasons; applicant may re-apply.
note: For BLC, site and land-title verification with geo-tagging is mandatory before sanction; geo-tag baseline anchors later installment stages.

post_name: Municipal Commissioner (Nagar Ayukt) / Executive Officer, ULB
action: Verify beneficiary eligibility and recommend the application upward to the district/state agency.
on_reject: Application rejected at ULB level with recorded reasons; applicant notified.
note: ULB is the verifier, not the final sanctioning authority. Nagar Ayukt heads a Municipal Corporation; smaller ULBs use the Executive Officer (Adhishasi Adhikari).

post_name: Project Officer, District Urban Development Agency (DUDA)
action: Consolidate verified ULB applications at district level and forward to the state agency.
on_reject: Discrepant cases sent back to ULB for re-verification.
note: In UP, DUDA is the district-level implementing arm feeding into SUDA. District Magistrate chairs district-level review of urban housing.

post_name: Additional Director / Mission Director, SUDA (State Level Nodal Agency)
action: Validate the demand, compile the state project and place it before the state sanctioning committee.
on_reject: Cases not meeting mission norms returned to DUDA/ULB.
note: SUDA (State Urban Development Agency), UP is the State Level Nodal Agency (SLNA) for PMAY-U.

post_name: State Level Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (SLSMC), chaired by Chief Secretary / Principal Secretary Urban Development
action: Appraise and approve the state project proposal and recommend to the central mission.
on_reject: Proposal returned to SLNA with observations for rework.
note: SLSMC is the standing state approving body for PMAY-U project proposals before central submission.

post_name: Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC), Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
action: Sanction central assistance and approve the beneficiary project for fund release.
on_reject: Proposal deferred/returned to the state for compliance.
note: CSMC is the final central sanctioning authority for PMAY-U BLC/AHP/ISSR project proposals.

post_name: Central Nodal Agency (for Interest Subsidy Scheme route only)
action: Process lender-forwarded subsidy claim and credit interest subsidy upfront to the loan account.
on_reject: Lender's grievance channel / CNA re-examines the claim.
note: ISS (CLSS successor): the bank/HFC forwards the claim via the Central Nodal Agency; subsidy is credited upfront, reducing principal and EMIs. Applies only to the loan route.

action: Release BLC grant in geo-tagged installments (foundation, lintel/roof, completion) to Aadhaar-linked account.
on_reject: Stage not verified by geo-tag halts the next installment until compliance.
note: For BLC, central+state assistance is paid direct-benefit-transfer in construction-stage installments, each released only after geo-tagged verification of the stage.

post_name: Junior Engineer (Avar Abhiyanta) / PMAY cell, ULB
action: Grievance and escalation: raise stuck cases via ULB PMAY cell, then SUDA and the portal helpline.
note: Escalation ladder: ULB PMAY cell -> DUDA -> SUDA (SLNA); for ISS use lender grievance channel + CNA; official PMAY-U grievance/helpline and city public-grievance system as backstop.

post_name: Junior Engineer (Avar Abhiyanta), Jal Kal Vibhag
action: Supervise tapping of the main, laying the service pipe, fitting the meter, connecting the drain to the sewer manhole; restore road.
note: Work done by the department or an empanelled licensed plumber under JE supervision; meter reading and billing then commence in the applicant's name.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (Jal Kal Vibhag, Nagar Nigam)
action: Confirm your service provider is the Nagar Nigam Jal Kal Vibhag (Jal Sansthan) for household connections in your city.
note: Under the U.P. Water Supply & Sewerage Act 1975, Jal Nigam lays trunk mains while the Jal Sansthan/Jal Kal Vibhag (merged into Nagar Nigam w.e.f. 01.04.2009) gives household connections. In a few cities Jal Nigam still handles connections directly — confirm at the counter or e-Nagarsewa portal.

post_name: Junior Engineer (Avar Abhiyanta), Jal Kal Vibhag
action: Check whether a distribution water main / public sewer already runs near your plot, or if only a new-line extension is possible.
note: The single biggest branch. A tap/sewer connection is sanctionable only where a main already passes; if no line is laid, it becomes a slower network-extension (often colony/group or developer-coordinated) request under the Act.

action: Gather sale deed/allotment letter, latest house-tax receipt/property ID, approved building plan, Aadhaar, photo.
note: Exact checklist varies per corporation; occupancy/completion certificate may also be asked. Confirm the current list on the e-Nagarsewa UP portal or the zonal Jal Kal office.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (Jal Kal Vibhag, Nagar Nigam)
action: Submit the water-connection (and sewer-connection) form with documents; pay the application/scrutiny fee.
on_reject: Resubmit with corrected documents; deficiency memo issued at counter.
note: File in person at the zonal Jal Kal office or online via the state e-Nagarsewa UP portal (e-nagarsewa.up.gov.in), where the corporation has enabled it. (Nivesh Mitra is for business approvals, not household connections.)

post_name: Registrar of Births and Deaths (Nagar Nikay / Gram Panchayat / Tehsil)
action: Register husband's death and issue the death certificate, the anchor document.
note: Under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. Issued by the municipal body, gram panchayat, or tehsil where the death occurred; prerequisite before applying.

action: Issue income certificate (below scheme ceiling) and residence/domicile certificate.
note: Obtained through the Uttarakhand e-District portal; income and domicile certificates are prerequisite supporting documents. Income ceiling is means-tested and revised by state budget - verify current figure.

action: Submit application online at ssp.uk.gov.in widow-pension form or on paper at DSWO/block office.
note: Official portal: ssp.uk.gov.in/OnlineRegistration/FrmWidowOnlineApplicationForm.aspx. Attach death certificate, Aadhaar, photo, domicile, income certificate, age proof, Aadhaar-linked bank passbook, widowhood declaration. Note the registration number.

action: Verify residence, widow status and income at village level; field check.
note: For rural applicants; urban applicants are verified by the municipal/ward-level welfare staff. This field-verification stage is where most delays occur.

action: Scrutinize verified file and supporting documents; forward recommendation to DSWO.
note: Block/tehsil-level welfare staff consolidate the field report and check document completeness before the file reaches the district officer.

action: Scrutinize the verified file and sanction the widow pension.
on_reject: If rejected, applicant is informed of the reason and may re-apply with corrected documents or appeal to the District Magistrate.
note: The DSWO is the district-level sanctioning authority; the case is recorded under the Collectorate's social-welfare wing. This is the decisive approval step.

action: Release pension by Direct Benefit Transfer into the Aadhaar-linked bank account.
note: Payment is DBT to the Aadhaar-seeded account (Aadhaar seeding is mandatory per department notifications); pension credited periodically (monthly/quarterly per current practice). Amount is budget-revised - verify current figure.

action: Follow up on a stalled file quoting the application/registration number.
note: First escalation: contact the DSWO office directly with the registration number. Helpline 1800-180-4236 / WhatsApp 63952 21188.

action: Receive written grievance if the DSWO line does not resolve the delay.
note: Second escalation up the Collectorate reporting line; also usable via the state grievance / CM Helpline (1905) portal.

post_name: Public Information Officer, Department of Social Welfare
action: File an RTI asking file status and reason for delay if file is complete but unmoved.
note: RTI under the Right to Information Act, 2005 is an effective forcing tool; if the service is notified under the Uttarakhand Right to Service Act, 2011, delay can also be escalated to the designated appellate officer.

post_name: Junior Engineer (Avar Abhiyanta), Jal Kal Vibhag
action: Inspect the site, confirm main proximity, fix pipe/ferrule/meter size, and prepare the demand note.
note: The JE (assisted where needed by the Assistant/Junior Engineer) records feasibility and specifications that drive the charge computation.

post_name: Assistant Engineer (Sahayak Abhiyanta), Jal Kal Vibhag
action: Assess and issue the demand: connection/tap fee, road-cutting/restoration charge, security deposit, meter cost, sewer charge.
note: Charges are levied under the U.P. Water Supply & Sewerage Act 1975 and the corporation's schedule; amounts are city-specific.

action: Deposit the assessed demand (tap fee, deposit, meter, road-cutting, sewer charge) at counter/treasury/online.
note: Retain the challan/receipt; sanction is issued only after full payment.

post_name: Executive Engineer (Adhishasi Abhiyanta), Jal Kal Vibhag
action: Sanction the connection and issue the work order authorising tapping of the main and sewer.
on_reject: Appeal to General Manager (Jal Kal) / Municipal Commissioner; then First Appellate Authority under U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011.
note: The zonal Executive Engineer is the competent sanctioning authority in the Jal Kal Vibhag (each of the department's zones is headed by an Executive Engineer).

post_name: General Manager (Jal Kal) / Municipal Commissioner (Nagar Ayukt)
action: Escalate delay/refusal to the GM Jal Kal, then the Municipal Commissioner, via the corporation grievance channel.
on_reject: CM Helpline 1076; IGRS jansunwai.up.nic.in.
note: First administrative escalation above the Executive Engineer within the Nagar Nigam.

post_name: First / Second Appellate Authority (U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011)
action: If a notified service-delivery timeline was breached, appeal to the designated First then Second Appellate Authority.
on_reject: State/District Consumer forum; or writ petition; Lokvani/IGRS grievance channels.
note: The Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 provides a designated officer + First/Second Appellate Authority and penalties for default. The specific guaranteed day-count for a water/sewer connection is not verified here — confirm the notified schedule locally.

action: Confirm child is in entry-age band and belongs to EWS or Disadvantaged Group category
note: Section 2(d)/2(e) RTE Act define disadvantaged group (SC/ST/OBC/disability/orphan etc.) and weaker section (below state income threshold, commonly cited ~Rs 1 lakh/yr in UP but year-specific). Residence in the school's notified neighbourhood/ward usually required.

action: Check eligibility: search family by mobile/Aadhaar/ration/family-ID on portal or Ayushman app.
on_reject: If not found in UP list, apply for state add-on / check 70+ Vay Vandana; in Uttarakhand all permanent residents qualify under AAUY.
note: PMJAY eligibility differs by state: UP uses SECC-2011 + state-added lists via SACHIS; Uttarakhand's AAUY is UNIVERSAL for all permanent residents regardless of income. Everyone aged 70+ is eligible nationwide under Ayushman Vay Vandana.

action: Gather Aadhaar of member being enrolled, registered mobile, ration/family-ID; Uttarakhand: residence proof.
note: Aadhaar of the person being enrolled is mandatory for eKYC. Exact accepted document list is set by the State Health Agency and can vary; confirm at the enrollment point.

post_name: Village Level Entrepreneur (VLE) - Common Service Centre / or self via Ayushman App
action: Go to a CSC, empanelled-hospital Arogya Mitra desk, or self-initiate on the Ayushman app.
on_reject: If CSC/VLE refuses or blocks, escalate to the CSC District Manager.
note: Enrollment points: CSC/VLE, Arogya Mitra kiosk at an empanelled hospital, designated government facility (PHC/CHC/district), or self-service via the Ayushman app (BIS 2.0) which still routes to an operator/auto-approver.

action: Operator searches family in beneficiary database and initiates eKYC for the member.
on_reject: If member not traceable, escalate to District Implementation Unit under the CMO/State Health Agency.
note: Arogya Mitra / Ayushman Mitra is the official PMJAY frontline enrolment-and-facilitation post at hospitals and camps.

action: Run Aadhaar eKYC (biometric/OTP or face auth), capture live photo, submit for approval.
on_reject: eKYC failure (Aadhaar mismatch): correct Aadhaar demographics at Aadhaar centre, then retry.
note: Under BIS 2.0, eKYC uses Aadhaar OTP/biometric/face authentication plus live photo; each family member is enrolled individually so eKYC repeats per member.

post_name: BIS 2.0 System / State Health Agency Verifier (SACHIS in UP; SHA in Uttarakhand)
action: System auto-approves exact matches above threshold; below-threshold records route to SHA verifier.
on_reject: Rejected/stuck record: escalate to the State Health Agency (SACHIS / Atal Ayushman SHA) grievance cell or District Implementation Unit under the CMO.
note: This is the decisive step. BIS 2.0 auto-approves high-confidence matches instantly; ambiguous ones go to a manual SHA verifier. No statutory SLA — turnaround ranges same-day to several days.

post_name: Self / Beneficiary or VLE / Arogya Mitra
action: Once approved, download or print the Ayushman card from app / bis.pmjay.gov.in self-print.
note: Card downloadable via Ayushman app, beneficiary portal, or self-print at bis.pmjay.gov.in. Card carries family cover up to Rs 5 lakh/year (amount/scope may differ under converged state schemes).

post_name: Ayushman Mitra (Arogya Mitra) at empanelled hospital
action: At admission, present card; Arogya Mitra raises pre-authorization to insurer/SHA/TPA for cashless care.
on_reject: If asked to pay at an empanelled hospital for a covered package, that is itself a grievance — escalate to hospital grievance nodal officer / helpline 14555.
note: Cashless ONLY at empanelled hospitals and ONLY for listed procedure packages; OPD and non-listed items generally excluded. Verify empanelment and package coverage before admission.

post_name: National Helpline 14555 / State Health Agency Grievance Cell / CMO District Implementation Unit
action: Escalate eligibility, enrolment, rejection, or treatment-refusal grievances.
note: National helpline 14555 (also 1800-111-565) for eligibility/enrolment/grievance. Rejected records -> SHA (SACHIS in UP; AAUY-SHA in Uttarakhand) grievance cell or CMO-led District Implementation Unit. Treatment-time refusal -> hospital grievance nodal officer.

action: Obtain death certificate and legal-heir/varasat certificate plus parivar register extract
note: Preliminary: heir gathers father's death certificate (from municipality/gram panchayat), a legal-heir (varasat/uttaradhikar) certificate via e-district or a succession certificate for disputed/large estates, the parivar register (family register) extract from the Gram Panchayat Adhikari, current khatauni/khasra copy, and Aadhaar. A will is submitted if one exists.

action: Applicant files mutation (namantaran/dakhil kharij) application on RCCMS/e-district or on paper at tehsil
note: Under Sec. 33-34 UPRC 2006 the heir applies to record succession. Filing is online through RCCMS (vaad.up.nic.in) / e-district, or on paper at the tehsil sadar. No court-fee for a succession mutation, though a nominal processing fee may apply.

action: Verifies land records and inspects possession on the ground; prepares report
note: The application is marked to the area Lekhpal, who checks the khatauni entry, confirms the death and heirship, verifies actual possession, and submits a report/recommendation. Rule 34 UP Revenue Code Rules 2016.

action: Reviews and countersigns the Lekhpal's report and record entries
note: The Supervisor/Registrar Kanungo scrutinises the Lekhpal's report for correctness against the revenue records before it goes to the deciding officer.

action: Parent reports to the allotted school within the deadline for final document verification
time_limit: within the reporting window on the allotment order
on_reject: non-reporting forfeits the seat; complaint to BEO/BSA
note: reporting step is by the parent at the allotted private school

action: If no objection, records succession and orders mutation of khatauni into heir's name
