on_reject: If an objection is filed the case is registered as a contested vaad (step 7); if the application itself is defective the applicant is asked to cure or it is rejected with reasons.
note: For an uncontested inheritance mutation the Tehsildar (or Naib Tehsildar) passes the order under Sec. 34 UPRC 2006 and directs correction of the record. This is the approval step for uncontested cases.

action: If contested, hears the mutation vaad as Assistant Collector and decides the succession entry
on_reject: Aggrieved party may appeal (step 9); genuine title disputes among heirs must be settled by a civil suit, not the mutation vaad.
note: Where an objection is filed the matter becomes a formal revenue case (vaad) before the SDM/Assistant Collector under the UPRC 2006; the record is corrected only after adjudication. Runs on the RCCMS platform.

post_name: Medical Officer (MO) / hospital in-charge (or head of household for a home birth)
action: Report the birth to the local Registrar within 21 days, keeping the reporting/discharge slip.
note: Section 8 RBD Act: institutions report institutional births; head of household reports home births. Reporting within 21 days is free.

action: File the birth-registration application at the Nagar Nigam registration section or via CRS / e-district portal.
note: In a city the Registrar sits within the Municipal Corporation (Nagar Nigam), usually its health / birth-death section; in towns/villages it is the Nagar Palika, Block PHC, or Gram Panchayat.

action: Check the application form, discharge slip, and parents' ID/address proof for completeness.
on_reject: Deficiency memo issued; applicant resubmits missing documents.
note: Documents: hospital slip, parents' Aadhaar/ID and address proof, marriage proof or affidavit if asked; child's name optional at this stage.

action: Verify the reported birth details against the hospital record or reporting form.
on_reject: Entry held pending clarification or corrected reporting form.
note: Under the CMO's / municipal health framework the reporting particulars are checked before the Registrar makes the entry.

post_name: Registrar of Births & Deaths (municipal official, e.g. under the Municipal Commissioner / Nagar Ayukt)
action: Approve and make the birth entry in the Civil Registration System register.
on_reject: Applicant informed of grounds; may cure defect or escalate to District Registrar.
note: The Registrar (Births & Deaths) is the statutory authority who registers the birth; in Nagar Nigam areas this function is placed under the municipal administration (Nagar Ayukt).

action: Sign and issue the birth certificate from the registered entry.
note: Certificate is issued by the Registrar; online-filed cases can be downloaded from the portal, else collected at the counter.

action: Collect/download the certificate; verify name, sex, date and parents' names immediately.
note: Corrections after issue are slower and may need an affidavit; check spelling at collection.

post_name: Registrar of Births & Deaths (late fee, 21-30 days)
action: For births reported after 21 but within 30 days, register on payment of the prescribed late fee.
on_reject: Applicant proceeds under the 30-day-to-1-year permission route.
note: Delayed-registration tier under RBD rules; only a nominal late fee, no external permission needed.

post_name: Additional District Registrar / Registrar (prescribed authority, 30 days-1 year)
action: For births 30 days to 1 year old, register on written permission of the prescribed authority plus fee and affidavit.
on_reject: Applicant must approach a magistrate under the over-one-year route.
note: Section 13(2) RBD Act: registration in this window requires written permission of the prescribed authority and a late fee.

post_name: Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) / Magistrate First Class (over 1 year)
action: For births over 1 year old, issue an order authorising registration after verification.
on_reject: Registration refused; applicant may seek review or provide further proof of birth.
note: Section 13(3) RBD Act: a birth not registered within one year is registered only on an order of a Magistrate of the first class / SDM, plus fee.

post_name: District Registrar (District Magistrate / CMO office) then Chief Registrar (state directorate)
action: Escalate delay, refusal, or errors through district and state registration grievance channels.
note: Escalation: Registrar to District Registrar to Chief Registrar of Births & Deaths; also UP Jansunwai/IGRS or Uttarakhand CM Helpline 1905, and Right-to-Service Act timelines.

action: Updates khatauni to record the heir as tenure-holder per the mutation order
note: On the final order the Lekhpal effects the entry in the khatauni; the updated record reflects on UP Bhulekh. Mutation is strong evidence of possession/revenue liability but not a conclusive title decree (Sec. 34(3)).

action: Escalate: appeal against mutation order lies upward — SDM, then Collector/DM, then Commissioner, then Board of Revenue
note: Statutory revenue appeal hierarchy under the UPRC 2006: first appeal upward through SDM → Collector/District Magistrate → Commissioner, with revision/reference ultimately to the Board of Revenue. For delay, use online status on RCCMS/e-district plus IGRS / CM Helpline 1076 / Jansunwai grievance.

action: Field-verify family income and residence particulars for the certificate
on_reject: Applicant re-submits corrected particulars or supporting proof
note: Village/ward revenue official conducts the ground verification that feeds the income and residence certificates applied for on the e-District portal.

post_name: State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (SCPCR)
action: Adjudicate RTE grievance and direct remedial action
on_reject: File writ petition in the High Court
note: SCPCR is the statutory RTE grievance-redress body (RTE Act Sections 31-32); the state RTE portal/helpline also accepts complaints.

action: Issue income certificate; caste certificate as applicable for DG claim
on_reject: Re-apply on e-District with corrected documents; appeal to SDM
note: Income/caste/residence certificates are issued via the e-District portal under the state Right to Public Service (Sewa Adhikar) Act, which sets a notified time limit for each service. Caste certificate needed only when claiming a Disadvantaged-Group seat.

action: Sign/countersign residence-domicile certificate or hear certificate appeal
on_reject: Escalate certificate refusal to District Magistrate under Sewa Adhikar appeal
note: SDM is the signing/appellate authority for residence-domicile and for appeals against a Tehsildar's certificate refusal.

action: Register and submit online RTE application with scanned documents, list preferred neighbourhood schools
note: UP: rte25.upsdc.gov.in (Basic Shiksha Vibhag). Uttarakhand: state RTE / Samagra Shiksha admission portal. Window is time-bound and often runs in multiple rounds early in the calendar year; parent may list several schools by preference within the ward/area.

action: Citizen submits mutation application with registered deed/succession papers at the Tehsil counter
on_reject: Application not accepted if documents incomplete; resubmit with corrections
note: Report of transfer is made to the Tehsildar under s.34

action: Registers/diarises the application, assigns a case number and issues a dated receipt
note: Diarising starts the statutory clock for disposal

post_name: Medical Officer in Charge (Hospital / Nursing Home)
action: Institution where birth occurred reports the event to the Registrar and gives parents the birth-report/discharge slip.
on_reject: If institution fails to report, the informant (parent/head of household) files the reporting form directly under s.8 RBD Act.
note: Under s.8-10 RBD Act the head of the institution is the informant for institutional births. Post-2023 amendment, the report is filed digitally on the CRS portal.

action: Create account on CRS portal (dc.crsorgi.gov.in) with parents' Aadhaar and file the birth-reporting form.
note: The Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2023 (in force 01-Oct-2023) made digital registration via CRS mandatory; Aadhaar of parents is captured. For home births the parent is the informant under s.8.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (Registrar of Births & Deaths, Nagar Nigam)
action: Receive the reporting form and documents; scrutinise for completeness and attach supporting proofs.
on_reject: Deficiency memo issued; informant re-submits missing documents.
note: Required documents: hospital birth-report/discharge summary, parents' Aadhaar/ID and address proof, and (some ULBs) marriage proof of parents. Registrar's office is the urban local body (Municipal Corporation).

post_name: Registrar of Births & Deaths (Nagar Nigam — designated Health Officer / Chief Medical Officer)
action: Verify the reported particulars against records and enter the event in the birth register.
on_reject: Objection recorded; informant asked to reconcile particulars or produce affidavit.
note: s.7 & s.12 RBD Act: the Registrar for an urban area is the officer designated by the Municipal Corporation (commonly the Health Officer / CMO or a designated corporation official).

action: Register the birth in the statutory register — this is the decisive registration act.
on_reject: If refused, escalate to the District Registrar of Births and Deaths.
note: s.12 RBD Act: on registration the Registrar shall give, free of charge, an extract of the prescribed particulars. Registration within 21 days carries no fee.

action: Generate and issue the QR-verified digital birth certificate to the informant.
on_reject: On non-delivery within the guaranteed period, invoke the State Right-to-Public-Services appeal (First Appellate Authority).
note: s.12/s.17 RBD Act read with 2023 amendment: the digital certificate carries a QR code and is the single proof of date of birth for those born on/after 01-Oct-2023. UP delivery guaranteed under the Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011.

action: For reporting after 21 but within 30 days, register on payment of the prescribed late fee.
on_reject: Escalate to District Registrar.
note: s.13(1) RBD Act. UP prescribed late fee at this tier is nominal (approx. Rs 2). This step applies only when the 21-day window was missed.

post_name: District Registrar of Births & Deaths / Additional District Magistrate
action: For reporting after 30 days but within one year, grant written permission to register on late fee plus notarised affidavit.
on_reject: Apply to a First Class / Executive Magistrate for an order (see next step).
note: s.13(2) RBD Act: requires written permission of the prescribed authority, prescribed fee (approx. Rs 5 in UP), and an affidavit before a notary public. Prescribed authority in UP is typically the District Registrar / ADM.

action: For births not registered within one year, pass a magisterial order directing registration on payment of fee.
on_reject: Revision before the District Magistrate; thereafter writ jurisdiction of the High Court.
note: s.13(3) RBD Act: registration after one year requires an order of a Magistrate of the First Class or Presidency Magistrate; in UP this is routed through the SDM / Executive Magistrate.

post_name: First Appellate Authority (designated officer, UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam)
action: On delay or refusal, hear the citizen's appeal and direct issuance within the guaranteed period.
on_reject: Second appeal to the Second Appellate Authority; parallel RTI to the CMO / District Registrar; complaint to State Chief Registrar (Births & Deaths) / Directorate.
note: UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 provides a tiered appeal with penalty on the defaulting designated officer. Grievance also lies to the District/Chief Registrar under the RBD Act.

action: Heir files mutation-on-inheritance application at the tehsil / Devbhoomi e-district portal with heirship proof.
note: Documents: father's death certificate, proof of relationship/legal-heir (or registered will if testate), current khatauni copy, and applicant ID. Intake is via the local Lekhpal/Patwari circle; exact online vs counter channel varies by tehsil (Devbhoomi/e-district Uttarakhand). Succession basis (intestate under applicable personal law vs will; ancestral vs self-acquired) governs which heirship proof is required.

action: Records the death and claimed succession and reports the change of possession for entry.
note: Section 34, U.P. Land Revenue Act 1901 (as adopted by Uttarakhand) obliges reporting of every succession/transfer of possession; the Lekhpal prepares the report and updates the khasra/field record accordingly.

action: Public notice / proclamation issued at the village level inviting objections from co-heirs and interested parties.
time_limit: typically 15–30 days notice window (not a confirmed statutory figure)
note: Because inheritance succession can be contested, the proposed mutation is notified and objections invited from other potential heirs/neighbours. If none is filed within the window, it proceeds as an uncontested (undisputed) mutation. The 15–30 day window is practice-reported, not confirmed from a named provision.

action: Naib Tehsildar / Tehsildar attests the undisputed inheritance entry and orders it mutated into the heir's name.
time_limit: no confirmed statutory day-count for rural revenue mutation; urban/municipal dakhil-kharij carries a 30-day Right-to-Service limit
on_reject: Appeal the revenue order upward: Tehsildar/SDM → Additional District Magistrate (Collector) → Commissioner → Board of Revenue (apex revenue authority, Uttarakhand).
note: For an undisputed succession, a Naib Tehsildar attests the entry; the Tehsildar-level revenue officer (under the SDM / District Collectorate) passes the order. This is the 'who decides' answer for the ordinary uncontested case. Municipal (Nagar Nikay) mutation of urban land is a separate track under the Uttarakhand Right to Service Act 2011 with a notified 30-day limit.

post_name: Block Education Officer (BEO / Khand Shiksha Adhikari)
action: Scrutinise application and verify uploaded documents at block level
on_reject: Application flagged for correction/resubmission before the round closes
note: BEO (Khand Shiksha Adhikari) is the block-level verifying authority in UP; in Uttarakhand the block-level education officer performs the equivalent scrutiny.

action: Dial 108 (toll-free, 24x7) from any mobile or landline
note: Free from any phone, no balance needed. 112 (national single emergency number) also routes medical calls to 108.

post_name: Emergency Response Centre Call-taker (ERC / EMRI dispatcher)
action: Answer call, record emergency type, patient condition, exact location, callback number
note: State Emergency Response Centre operated under PPP (GVK EMRI / Ziqitza / BVG by state and contract). Call handling typically ~1-2 minutes.

action: Assign nearest available GPS-located ambulance; no separate approval needed
note: Dispatch is the dispatcher's own decision within the same call. Ambulance may be Basic (BLS) or Advanced (ALS) Life Support.

action: Give pre-arrival first-aid instructions to caller over the phone
note: Tele-guidance (e.g. CPR, bleeding control, choking) while the ambulance is en route.

action: Drive to the caller's location using GPS/navigation
note: Reported average response ~14 min urban and ~31 min rural (NAS/EMRI averages, not a guaranteed SLA); actual time varies with traffic, distance, and fleet availability.

action: Provide on-scene pre-hospital care: oxygen, stabilization, protocol medication
note: EMT follows standard treatment protocols, with tele-guidance from an ERC doctor if needed.

action: Decide receiving hospital (usually nearest appropriate government facility)
note: Choice made with ERC tele-guidance; normally a government hospital, subject to case severity and patient/family input.

action: Alert (pre-notify) the receiving casualty/ER so it is ready
note: Crew may radio/call ahead for critical cases; not guaranteed for every trip.

action: Transport patient free of charge and hand over at hospital casualty
note: The 108 ride is free (state-funded). Hospital treatment cost is separate; government-hospital care may be free/subsidized.

action: Escalate if no ambulance arrives: re-call 108, quote case ID, ask ETA/supervisor
note: Backups: call 108 again, ask for the ERC supervisor, or dial 112; use a private/hospital ambulance if available. Service grievances go to the state health department / operator grievance line.

action: If any co-heir/third party objects, mutation is registered as a contested revenue case and heard as a mini-trial.
on_reject: Appeal the reasoned order: SDM → Additional District Magistrate/Collector → Commissioner → Board of Revenue.
note: Mutation proceedings are judicial; a disputed succession is decided by the Revenue Officer of Tehsildar rank in revenue-court capacity, with parties, evidence and a reasoned order after opportunity of hearing. No order on a disputed mutation without hearing the parties. Contested cases have no meaningful fixed time limit.

action: On approval, corrects the entry in the khatauni and the digitized (Devbhoomi) record.
note: The Lekhpal carries the ordered mutation into both the manual khatauni and the digital record. A common failure point is an order passed but the digital record not updated.

action: Heir obtains a fresh khatauni copy showing their name to confirm the mutation was carried through.
on_reject: If the record is not updated after the order, escalate to the SDM and then the District Collectorate / District Magistrate.
note: Verify via the Devbhoomi / e-district Uttarakhand portal or a certified tehsil copy. Reminder for the citizen: mutation updates the fiscal/possession record — it does NOT confer or prove title. If ownership itself is disputed among heirs, revenue authorities will not resolve title (that needs a civil suit / partition) and may decline to mutate until settled.

post_name: Chief Medical Officer (CMO) / District Immunization Officer (DIO)
action: If still unresolved, approach the District Immunization Officer in the CMO's District Health Office.
on_reject: State NHM Routine Immunization division; national health helpline 104/1075 can also route the grievance.
note: The District Immunization Officer (DIO), housed in the office of the Chief Medical Officer (the district-health lead office for this task), owns UIP delivery for the district - vaccine supply, session planning and grievances. A district health helpline or the national 104/1075 helpline can also route the complaint.

action: If the Lekhpal or Tehsildar delays or refuses, escalate to the SDM and up the revenue hierarchy.
on_reject: Full revenue appeal chain: Tehsildar → SDM → Additional District Magistrate/Collector → Commissioner → Board of Revenue; a Right-to-Service delay complaint for the municipal-track mutation goes to the designated first/second appellate authority under the Uttarakhand Right to Service Act, 2011.
note: Escalation ladder: SDM, then District Collectorate / District Magistrate for administrative delay, and the statutory revenue appeal chain for a passed order. Exact RTS appellate tiers apply to the notified municipal service and are jurisdiction-specific for the rural revenue track (unverified from a named provision).

post_name: Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA) [UP] / Chief Education Officer (CEO) [Uttarakhand]
action: Approve verified applications for inclusion in the allotment pool
on_reject: Applicant corrects documents and re-enters the next round; grievance to DM/Collectorate
note: District education head: BSA in UP, CEO / District Education Officer in Uttarakhand — the officer who validates the district's eligible pool before the lottery.

post_name: State RTE portal / District education office (lottery committee)
action: Run computerised lottery and allot each eligible child to a specific school
on_reject: Non-allotted applicants roll into subsequent rounds where seats remain
note: When applications exceed the 25% seats, allotment is by a computerised random draw/lottery, mapping the child to one school; allotment notified via SMS/portal. Often 2-4 rounds per cycle.

action: Report to allotted school with allotment letter and original documents within the deadline
on_reject: Missing the reporting window forfeits the seat; re-enter next round if available
note: Reporting deadline is short, commonly ~1-2 weeks after allotment. Carry originals of all certificates plus the allotment letter.

post_name: Principal / Head of the private unaided school
action: Verify originals and admit the child free of tuition; no screening or capitation fee
on_reject: School refusal is unlawful for a validly allotted seat — trigger escalation
note: Section 13 RTE Act bars screening procedure and capitation fee; the school admits the child free and claims reimbursement from the state under Section 12(2).

post_name: Block Education Officer (BEO) then Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA) / DEO
action: On complaint, direct the school to admit and enforce compliance
on_reject: Escalate to District Magistrate / Collectorate
note: First administrative escalation if a school refuses or delays a validly allotted RTE seat; ask the school in writing for the reason first.

action: Direct and compel the school's compliance; oversee district RTE implementation
on_reject: Approach SCPCR and/or High Court
note: The Collectorate is the higher administrative authority overseeing RTE implementation and the point where grievances against schools are enforced at district level.

action: At government delivery point, give BCG, OPV-0, Hep B birth dose before discharge; open MCP card.
time_limit: Hep B birth dose within 24 hours of birth
note: At a government hospital/CHC/PHC the ward nurse or ANM administers birth doses and issues the Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card. If born at a private facility or at home, birth doses/card may not have been given - proceed to step 2. UP runs a pilot (Sambhal/Jhansi) placing govt-supplied BCG/OPV-0/Hep B and U-WIN registration inside private delivery facilities.

post_name: Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA) / Auxiliary Nurse Midwife (ANM)
action: Ask your area's ASHA/ANM for the immunization session site, day and time for your address.
note: Free UIP vaccines are delivered at the nearest sub-centre, PHC/Urban PHC, Anganwadi centre and at Village Health & Nutrition Day (VHND) outreach sessions - in Uttarakhand/NHM these are held on Saturdays at the Anganwadi, Panchayat Bhawan or school. The ASHA maintains the due-list of children and mobilizes them; the ANM runs the session. They are the ground-truth source for the exact site/day.

action: Optionally self-register the child on the U-WIN Citizen app/web portal and book the nearest session.
on_reject: If self-registration fails, the ANM registers the child on-site at first visit.
note: U-WIN is the MoHFW national electronic immunization registry. Self-registration via the U-WIN Citizen mobile app or web portal lets you search centres by district/sub-district/PIN, book a slot, and later download a QR e-Vaccination Certificate and generate the child's ABHA. Optional - a walk-in without prior registration is fully allowed; the ANM can register you at the session.

action: At the session, register the child in U-WIN, issue/update the MCP card, record dose and next due-date.
note: No referral, income proof or prior appointment is required - free routine immunization is a walk-in entitlement. Bring the child and, if available, the birth certificate/hospital discharge slip or any ID. The MCP card (paper) plus the U-WIN digital record together form the immunization record you present at every later visit and for school admission.

action: Verify the child's age/eligibility and vaccinate free per the National Immunization Schedule.
note: National Immunization Schedule primary series: OPV/Pentavalent/Rota/PCV/fIPV at 6, 10 and 14 weeks; MR-1 & JE-1 (in endemic districts) and PCV booster at 9-12 months; DPT booster 1, OPV booster, MR-2 and JE-2 at 16-24 months. All 12-disease UIP vaccines are free at government points.

action: Track the due-list and remind you of each next dose; U-WIN sends SMS reminders 3 days prior.
note: Being late does not disqualify the child - catch-up is available and decided by the vaccinator per national guidelines. The MCP card prints due-dates and U-WIN sends automated SMS reminders three days before each due dose.

action: If turned away or a card/dose is refused, raise it with the PHC Medical Officer.
on_reject: If unresolved, escalate to the District Immunization Officer / CMO (step 8).
note: The Medical Officer in charge of the PHC/Urban PHC supervises the ANM/ASHA and the routine-immunization sessions in the block and can direct issuance of the card or the due vaccine.

action: Attach ID proof, premises ownership/occupancy proof, address proof, photo; pay processing fee
note: Ownership/occupancy = registry/sale deed, or rent agreement + owner NOC. Exact document list per UPCL new-connection schedule - confirm on portal.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Commercial Clerk, UPCL sub-division
action: Register application, scrutinise documents for completeness, generate service-request number
on_reject: Application returned to applicant for missing/incorrect documents before registration
note: Real designation at sub-division: commercial/dealing assistant; front-office intake. Not the sanctioning officer.

action: Conduct site inspection to verify premises, feasibility, sanctioned load and metering point
on_reject: Infeasible site or load mismatch reported back; applicant advised on required infrastructure/revised load
note: Field verification by JE/lineman; feeds the demand-note and sanction decision.

post_name: Assistant Engineer / Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO), UPCL sub-division
action: Sanction the connection and issue demand note for security deposit and service-line charges
on_reject: Applicant may revise load/route or escalate; larger loads/new infra escalate to Executive Engineer at division
note: AE/SDO sanctions routine domestic loads on existing network. This is the decisive approval step. EE (division) handles larger loads or new transformer/line extension.

action: Pay security deposit and service-line/development charges per the demand note
note: Security deposit scales with sanctioned load; amounts per UPCL schedule of charges - verify current figures.

post_name: Junior Engineer / Meter Reader, UPCL field
action: Install meter and service line at the premises after dues clearance
note: Metering and service-line drop by UPCL field staff once demand note cleared.

action: Energise the connection and open the consumer billing account
time_limit: Routine connection where network exists: approx. 7-15 working days from complete application (UERC SoP)
note: Energisation completes supply under Electricity Act 2003 s.43 duty to supply. SoP time limit is provision-based but exact days vary by current UERC schedule.

post_name: Executive Engineer / Superintending Engineer, UPCL division
action: First escalation: represent delay or refusal to the division office
note: Internal utility escalation above the sub-division AE/SDO. Also UPCL consumer grievance cell / toll-free helpline.

action: Contact area ASHA; she registers newborn, links to session site, tracks due doses
note: ASHA is the frontline anchor for your address; she mobilizes families and maintains the due-list. No form, no fee, no eligibility test.

action: Issue Mother & Child Protection (MCP) card; register child on U-WIN registry
on_reject: If no card at birth, ANM issues one at first contact.
note: MCP card records the schedule and every dose; U-WIN is the national digital immunization registry (successor to paper-only tracking). Aadhaar may be requested for records but is NOT a precondition for vaccination.

post_name: Medical Officer (MO), delivery facility / government hospital
action: Administer birth doses (BCG, OPV-0, Hepatitis B) before discharge for institutional deliveries
on_reject: For home births, get birth doses at nearest Sub-Centre/PHC as early as possible.
note: Ask before leaving the hospital. Birth doses are given within the first days of life.

action: Run immunization session at Sub-Centre/HWC, PHC, or VHSND at Anganwadi; give due vaccines
on_reject: If a session is missed, catch-up doses are given at the next session - no restart.
note: Village Health, Sanitation & Nutrition Day (VHSND) is held at the Anganwadi centre, typically on a fixed weekday (often Wed/Sat - confirm locally). Urban areas hold equivalent urban-PHC sessions.

action: Give primary series at 6, 10, 14 weeks: Pentavalent, OPV, Rotavirus, fIPV, PCV
note: Pentavalent = DPT + HepB + Hib. PCV and Rotavirus are the sub-nationally introduced vaccines now rolled out across UP and Uttarakhand. All free.

action: Give 9-12 month doses: Measles-Rubella 1, PCV booster, JE-1 (endemic districts), Vitamin A
note: Japanese Encephalitis (JE) vaccine is given only in JE-endemic districts (several in eastern UP and the Terai belt of Uttarakhand) - a district-specific add-on.

action: Give 16-24 month boosters: DPT booster-1, OPV booster, MR-2, JE-2 (endemic districts)
note: Completes the infant/toddler course. Further boosters: DPT booster-2 at 5-6 yr; Td at 10 and 16 yr.

action: Supervise session schedule; resolve stock, session-timing, or refusal-of-service complaints
on_reject: If unresolved, escalate to district level (next step).
note: First escalation point if you are turned away, a session is not held, or a fee is demanded. Any charge for a UIP vaccine at a government facility is impermissible.

post_name: District Immunization Officer (DIO) / Chief Medical Officer (CMO)
action: Own routine immunization at district level; act on written complaint of denial or charging
on_reject: If still unresolved, use CM Helpline / grievance portal (next step).
note: This is the district-health office class that runs the programme. The CMO office houses the DIO. Put demands-for-payment or denial-of-service complaints in writing here.

action: Call health helpline 104; lodge grievance on CM Helpline UP 1076 / Uttarakhand 1905 or Jansunwai portal
note: 104 = state health helpline. UP grievances: CM Helpline 1076 / jansunwai.up.nic.in. Uttarakhand: CM Helpline 1905. 108 is emergency ambulance, NOT for immunization queries. National immunization/health helpline 1800-180-1104 (verify - helpline numbers change).

action: File grievance with CGRF if the utility does not resolve within its standards
on_reject: If unsatisfied with CGRF order, appeal to the Electricity Ombudsman
note: CGRF constituted under Electricity Act 2003 s.42(5). Named statutory forum.

action: Final utility-side appeal against the CGRF decision
note: Ombudsman appointed by UERC under Electricity Act 2003 s.42(6). Final internal-sector appeal; further recourse is judicial.

post_name: Appellate Authority (Labour Commissioner's office), UP Shops & Establishments Act
action: On rejection or stalled application, hear the applicant's appeal against the Chief Inspector's order.
on_reject: Writ petition to the Allahabad High Court under Article 226 as the ultimate structural remedy.
note: Appeal lies to the designated appellate authority (senior Labour Department officer / Labour Commissioner). Nivesh Mitra also carries a grievance/Jansunwai escalation tracker. Exact appeal window not asserted - verify in the 1963 Rules.

action: Hear appeal against refusal or conditions; confirm, modify, or set aside the order
on_reject: Further remedy: writ petition in the High Court; and RTI to obtain reasons/status on a stuck file.
note: Appeal lies to the authority prescribed under the Act (Collector/DFO tier). Also use the state Right-to-Service / grievance portal for time-bound delivery where the service is notified.

action: Hear appeal against delay, wrongful rejection, or refusal to transfer.
time_limit: Appeal generally within 30 days of the order
on_reject: Further remedy: State Transport Appellate Tribunal / High Court writ; seller-won't-release-RC is a civil/consumer dispute, not for the RTO
note: Grievance first via Vahan/Parivahan portal or the RTO citing the application reference, then appeal to the Transport Commissioner under MV Act s.50/appeal provisions. A seller refusing to hand over the RC is a contractual dispute for consumer/civil forum.

action: Issue income certificate and domicile/residence certificate, applied through e-District / CSC.
time_limit: Income certificate and domicile certificate are notified services under the U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (commonly 15 working days).
on_reject: First Appellate Officer (SDM) then Second Appellate Officer under U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011.
note: Lekhpal conducts the field verification feeding the Tehsildar's certificate. Time limits set by the RTS notification schedule.

action: Register on sspy-up.gov.in, fill the Nirashrit Mahila (widow) pension form, upload documents, submit.
on_reject: Correct and resubmit; contact the DPO helpline 1800-419-0001.
note: Documents: husband's death certificate, Aadhaar, domicile, age proof, income certificate/BPL, Aadhaar-linked bank passbook, photo. Print form and submit hard copy to the office within ~1 month.

action: Verifies residence/income/land records in rural areas, corroborates the SI report
on_reject: discrepancy noted in report
note: revenue-side field verification (rural cases)

action: Countersigns/validates the revenue verification and income-residence certification
on_reject: returns for re-verification
note: revenue authority attesting eligibility inputs

action: Scrutinises eligibility against NFSA priority-household / AAY exclusion criteria
on_reject: recommends rejection with reasons
note: eligibility scrutiny before forwarding to the sanctioning officer

action: Approves eligible applications at sub-division level within delegated authority
on_reject: rejection recorded with reasons
note: sanctioning authority where power is delegated to SDM/tehsil level

action: Issue Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD) for the deceased
note: For institutional/hospital deaths the attending Medical Officer issues MCCD under s.10(3) RBD Act; for home deaths a registered medical practitioner who attended may issue it.

action: For unnatural death, order post-mortem and record cause via forensic report
note: Accident/suicide/homicide/unexplained deaths require post-mortem; the mortuary/CMO's forensic wing supplies the cause-of-death report used in place of a routine MCCD.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Register FIR/inquest and issue police clearance / NOC for unnatural deaths
note: Under CrPC inquest (s.174) the SHO conducts inquest; police NOC / no-objection required before registration proceeds for unnatural deaths only.

action: Submit death report Form 2 with MCCD and IDs to the Registrar
note: s.8/s.10 RBD Act and Rule 5: report within 21 days of the death; for institutional deaths the institution's officer-in-charge is the reporting person.

action: Scrutinise Form 2, MCCD and proofs; check window and enter details
on_reject: Return for missing MCCD, ID, or proof of date/place of death
note: Registration wing clerk in the Nagar Nigam records the entry in the CRS software before Registrar approval.

action: Register the death in the municipal register and approve the entry
on_reject: Registration refused if documents incomplete or death not within jurisdiction
note: s.7/s.12 RBD Act: the Registrar (a designated municipal officer of the Nagar Nigam) makes the register entry; registration within 21 days is free of fee.

action: Permit delayed registration between 30 days and one year on affidavit and late fee
on_reject: Refuse if affidavit/late fee absent or cause unverifiable
note: s.13(2) RBD Act: after 30 days and within one year, registration needs written permission of the District Registrar plus prescribed late fee and affidavit.

action: Order registration of a death reported after one year
on_reject: No registration without a magistrate's order once one year has elapsed
note: s.13(3) RBD Act: a death not registered within one year is registered only on the order of a magistrate of the first class / executive magistrate and payment of late fee.

action: Issue certified death certificate (extract) on registration
note: s.12/s.17 RBD Act: extract of the register issued free once on registration; further certified copies on application and fee, downloadable from CRS / e-district.

action: Hear grievance / escalation against delay or refusal by the Registrar
note: In a Nagar Nigam the Municipal Commissioner heads the registration establishment; grievance also lies to the District/Chief Registrar and via the UP Right-to-Service appellate authority.

action: Confirm eligibility/category and that no member holds an existing ration card anywhere
note: Categories: AAY (poorest) / Priority Household / State non-subsidized. Eligibility criteria are state-NFSA-specific; verify locally.

action: Obtain surrender/deletion certificate if splitting name from a prior household card
note: A person may appear on only one card; deletion from the old card (a separate FCS transaction) is commonly required before a fresh card. Requirement varies by district.

action: File new-card application with documents via e-district / URCMS portal or CSC kiosk
note: UP: fcs.up.gov.in / edistrict.up.gov.in (Rural/Urban/Migrant form). Uttarakhand: URCMS uk.smartpds.nic.in or offline at DSO. Docs: Aadhaar of all members, residence proof, HoH photo, bank/LPG details; income declaration if category requires.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (DSO office / Tehsil Supply)
action: Scrutinize application, check documents and completeness, forward for verification
on_reject: Deficiency memo; applicant resubmits corrected form
note: Data-entry/dealing clerk at the Tehsil Supply Office / District Supply Office is the intake point in the e-district workflow.

post_name: Supply Inspector / Food Supply Inspector (Ration/Food Inspector)
action: Conduct field verification of residence and household composition, submit report
on_reject: Adverse report; application returned to clerk with reasons
note: The FSI/Supply Inspector physical verification is the usual source of delay. In rural areas the Lekhpal / Patwari may co-verify residence.

action: Review verification report and recommend the case for sanction
on_reject: Returns case for re-verification or rejection with reasons
note: Intermediate approval tier in the e-district routing (data operator -> FSI -> Assistant DSO -> DSO). Title varies by district; some districts route sanction through the Tehsildar / SDM as designated officer.

action: Sanction the ration card and digitally sign / approve issuance
time_limit: ~15 days (UP Janhit Guarantee ration-card window); 15-30 working days (Uttarakhand)
on_reject: Rejection order stating reasons; appealable under state Right-to-Service / Janhit Guarantee Act
note: DSO (a district-collectorate food-wing officer) is the sanctioning/digital-sign-off authority. In some UP districts the Tehsildar/SDM is the notified designated officer for this service.

action: Generate the NFSA card, link it to a Fair Price Shop, release e-ration card
note: Card downloadable from the state portal (e-ration card) and mapped to an FPS for grain drawal; name added to the NFSA eligibility list.

post_name: First Appeal Officer (Janhit Guarantee) / Additional District Magistrate
action: Hear appeal if service not delivered within the notified time or rejected
time_limit: File within 30 days of rejection/expiry (UP JGA Sec. 6)
on_reject: Second appeal to the next designated appellate officer under the Act
note: UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 gives a time-bound first-appeal remedy; Uttarakhand equivalent under its Right to Service Act 2011.

action: Escalate PDS grievance under NFSA if statutory remedies exhausted
on_reject: Onward to State Food Commission under NFSA Sec. 15
note: NFSA 2013 Sec. 14-15: DGRO then State Food Commission is the food-specific redressal track, parallel to the Right-to-Service appeal.

action: Identify the public authority (department) that holds the record sought.
note: RTI can only be filed with the public authority holding the record; misdirection is the top cause of delay. Which department holds a given record is a factual lookup, not structural.

action: Issue Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 4/4A) to the family.
note: RBD Act s.10 + Rules: attending doctor/hospital certifies cause of death on Form 4 (institution) or Form 4A (non-institutional). In Uttarakhand urban areas the CMO is a designated District Registrar for deaths.

action: Report the death and submit the death report (Form 2) within 21 days.
time_limit: 21 days from date of death (RBD Act s.10 + Rules)
note: RBD Act ss.8-9 fix the informant: for a house death, the head of household or nearest relative; for a hospital/institution, the medical officer in charge; for cremation/burial ground, the person in charge.

post_name: Registrar of Births and Deaths (Municipal Health Officer / designated ward-zone Registrar)
action: Receive Form 2, medical cause-of-death certificate, and ID/address proofs at counter or e-district portal.
note: In a municipal-corporation area the Registrar function sits in the corporation Health Dept (a designated Registrar/Sub-Registrar). Documents: Form 2, Form 4/4A, proof of identity of deceased (Aaadhaar), informant ID and address proof, cremation/burial receipt. Apply via UP eDistrict (edistrict.up.gov.in) or Uttarakhand eServices / CRS portal.

action: Verify documents against Form 4/4A and informant particulars for completeness.
on_reject: Return application for missing/discrepant documents; informant re-submits.
note: Registrar checks the report against the medical certificate; if reported within 21 days registration is normal and no fee is charged for entry.

post_name: Prescribed Authority (Additional District Registrar / District Registrar)
action: For delay of 30 days to 1 year, grant written permission on affidavit plus prescribed late fee.
time_limit: Applies only when reported after 30 days and within 1 year (RBD Act s.13(2))
on_reject: Escalate to District Registrar; ultimately magistrate route under s.13(3).
note: RBD Act s.13: 21-30 days = small prescribed late fee only; 30 days-1 year = registered only with written permission of the prescribed authority + affidavit before a notary + prescribed fee. Skip this step if reported within 21 days.

action: For delay beyond 1 year, pass an order authorising registration after verifying correctness.
time_limit: Applies only when reported after 1 year (RBD Act s.13(3))
on_reject: Revision/representation to District Magistrate.
note: RBD Act s.13(3): a death not registered within one year is registered only on an order of a Magistrate of the First Class / Executive Magistrate after verifying correctness, on payment of the prescribed fee. Skip if within 1 year.

action: Examine person in-person; order tests (audiometry, X-ray, psych/IQ) as needed by disability type
note: Relevant specialist per disability: orthopaedic, ENT/audiologist, ophthalmologist, psychiatrist, etc.

action: Enter the death in the register and record it on the national CRS portal.
on_reject: Refusal to register is appealable to the District Registrar / Chief Registrar under RBD Act s.25.
note: This is the operative decision that completes registration. Post-2023 Amendment (in force 1 Oct 2023) registration on the Centre's Civil Registration System (crsorgi.gov.in) is mandatory and data is shared with the Registrar General of India.

action: Issue the death certificate (digital or physical) free of charge to the informant.
time_limit: Within 7 days of completing registration (RBD Act s.17)
note: RBD Act s.17 (as amended 2023): Registrar gives, free of charge and not later than 7 days, a certificate to the person who gave information under s.8/s.9, electronically or otherwise. Additional/duplicate copies carry a small prescribed fee.

action: Issue additional certified copies on request against the prescribed per-copy fee.
time_limit: State RTS schedule where notified (UP Janhit Guarantee / Uttarakhand RTS)
on_reject: First appeal (see step 11) if copy not delivered within the RTS time limit.
note: Extra copies are searched and issued under RBD Act s.17; digitally certified copies are downloadable from the UP eDistrict / Uttarakhand eServices portal.

action: Process corrections/cancellations of entries on written application with proof.
on_reject: Refusal appealable to District Registrar under RBD Act s.25.
note: RBD Act s.15 + Rules: clerical/material errors (name, date, spelling) are corrected or cancelled by the Registrar with a margin entry on documentary proof; not by erasing the original entry.

post_name: First Appellate Officer (Additional District Magistrate / designated officer under state RTS)
action: Hear appeal where service is refused or exceeds the RTS time limit; direct delivery.
time_limit: File within 30 days of rejection or expiry of the stipulated time limit (UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011, s.5-6)
on_reject: Second appeal to the Second Appellate Authority within 60 days.
note: Under the UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (and the Uttarakhand Right to Service Act), the First Appellate Officer may order the designated officer to deliver within a fixed period; a second appeal lies within 60 days.

post_name: Second Appellate Authority (Commissioner / senior officer under state RTS)
action: Decide second appeal and may impose penalty on the defaulting designated officer.
time_limit: File within 60 days of the first-appeal decision (UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011)
on_reject: Parallel remedy: RBD Act s.25 appeal to Chief Registrar; or writ/RTI.
note: The RTS statute empowers the second appellate authority to penalise the designated officer for unjustified delay/refusal, closing the accountability loop.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (Jal Kal Vibhag, Nagar Nigam / Jal Sansthan)
action: Confirm your provider: Nagar Nigam Jal Kal Vibhag (UP corporation cities) or Uttarakhand Jal Sansthan.
note: Under the U.P. Water Supply & Sewerage Act 1975, Jal Nigam lays trunk mains while the Jal Sansthan / Jal Kal Vibhag gives household connections (merged into UP Nagar Nigams w.e.f. 01.04.2009; a standalone Jal Sansthan in Uttarakhand). In a few towns Jal Nigam still connects directly — confirm at the counter or the e-Nagarsewa / ujsbill portal.

post_name: Junior Engineer (Avar Abhiyanta), Jal Kal Vibhag / Jal Sansthan
action: Check whether a distribution water main already runs near your plot, or only a new-line extension is possible.
note: The single biggest branch: a tap-connection is sanctionable only where a main already passes; if no line is laid it becomes a slower network-extension (often colony/group or developer-coordinated) request under the Act.

action: Gather sale deed / allotment letter, latest house-tax receipt or property ID, approved building plan, Aadhaar, photo.
note: Exact checklist varies per corporation / Jal Sansthan; occupancy/completion certificate may also be asked. Confirm the current list on e-Nagarsewa UP (e-nagarsewa.up.gov.in) or ujsbill.uk.gov.in, or at the zonal office.

action: Write request describing information sought; attach Rs 10 fee; no reason required.
note: Section 6 RTI Act: request in writing in English, Hindi, or the official language of the area; no reason or form mandated. Fee Rs 10 per UP/Uttarakhand RTI Rules; BPL applicants exempt on proof (Section 7(5)). Payment mode (IPO/DD/court fee stamp/online) is state-specific.

post_name: Attestation Officer, CPV Division, Ministry of External Affairs (MEA)
action: Verify state authentication and issuing-authority genuineness on the document
on_reject: Document returned for missing/invalid state attestation
note: Via e-Sanad the issuing authority verifies digitally before MEA acts; MEA is the sole Competent Authority for apostille in India.

post_name: Competent Authority (Apostille), CPV Division, Ministry of External Affairs (MEA)
action: Affix MEA Apostille sticker for Hague-member destination countries
on_reject: For non-Hague countries proceed to embassy attestation instead of apostille
note: Apostille fee approx Rs 50 per document (+ postal ~Rs 40 via e-Sanad); apostille alone suffices for Hague Apostille Convention member states (India in force 14 Jul 2005).

post_name: Consular / Attestation Officer, Destination-Country Embassy or Consulate in India
action: Attest the MEA-authenticated certificate for non-Hague destination countries
on_reject: Correct MEA-attestation defects; recheck embassy document checklist
note: Only for countries NOT party to the Apostille Convention; such states need MEA attestation followed by destination-embassy legalisation (apostille does not apply).

post_name: Credential Evaluation Body (e.g. WES / destination university admissions / employer)
action: Submit apostilled/attested degree for foreign credential evaluation if required
on_reject: Provide additional transcripts sent directly by the university
note: Some universities/employers require a separate credential evaluation (e.g. WES for Canada/US) or accept transcripts sent directly; requirement is institution-specific, not a government step.

post_name: Grievance Officer / CPGRAMS (Public Grievance) + MEA Apostille Helpdesk
action: Escalate delays at university, state department, or MEA/apostille stage
note: University delay: Registrar then Vice-Chancellor. State delay: department grievance officer / state PG portal (UP Jansunwai / Uttarakhand). MEA/apostille delay: MEA apostille helpdesk, service-provider escalation line, and CPGRAMS.

action: Route application to the district Medical Authority and schedule a Medical Board assessment date
note: CMO/Civil Surgeon is the notified Medical Authority under RPwD Rule 17; convenes the Board. Appointment notified by SMS/portal.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (Jal Kal Vibhag, Nagar Nigam / Jal Sansthan)
action: Submit the new-water-connection form with documents; pay the application / scrutiny fee.
on_reject: Resubmit with corrected documents; a deficiency memo is issued at the counter.
note: File in person at the zonal office or online (UP: e-nagarsewa.up.gov.in 'Apply for New Water Connection'; Uttarakhand: ujsbill.uk.gov.in 'Apply For New Connection'). Nivesh Mitra is for business approvals, not household connections.

action: Register applicant on national UDID portal (swavlambancard.gov.in) or via e-District UP; select disability type, upload Aadhaar/photo.
note: UP applicants may also route through divyangjanUP / e-District CSC counters; application is federated to the national UDID system. 2024 amendment allows applying at any hospital (not only government).

post_name: Chief Medical Officer (CMO) office / Medical Authority
action: Receive online application, verify applicant data and documents, forward to the concerned district hospital for assessment.
on_reject: Deficiency memo to applicant via portal for correction/resubmission.
note: CMO office is the designated medical authority node that controls the district hospital assessment queue in the UDID workflow.

post_name: Chief Medical Officer (CMO) office / Medical Authority
action: Assign the relevant specialist(s) and schedule an assessment slot or refer to a periodic disability assessment camp.
note: Walk-in vs. appointment vs. camp-only varies by district and disability type; multi-disability cases may need several specialists on different days.

post_name: Medical Officer (MO) / Specialist (orthopaedic, ENT, ophthalmic, psychiatrist etc.)
action: Clinically examine the person in-person; run required diagnostics (audiometry, X-ray, vision, IQ) for the claimed disability.
note: In-person presence of the person with disability is required; assessment is clinical, not documentary. Specialist matched to disability category.

action: Determine disability type and assess percentage against the national gazetted assessment guidelines; record opinion on portal.
note: Percentage assessed per the Ministry's notified 'Guidelines for assessment of the extent of specified disability' under the RPwD Act.

post_name: Medical Board (chaired by CMO / Medical Superintendent + specialists)
action: Review the specialist finding, confirm disability type and final percentage; decide certificate eligibility.
on_reject: Rejection reasons conveyed to applicant via Form VIII within one month; appeal within 90 days (see step 9).
note: Board is the standard approving body; a single specialist may suffice for straightforward categories, but the Medical Board is the deciding authority.

action: Authenticate the assessment on the UDID portal; digitally sign and generate the Disability Certificate (Form V).
note: Certificate becomes downloadable once the CMO/medical authority authenticates it in the portal; integrated with DigiLocker in UP e-District.

action: Generate the UDID number and print the UDID card (Form VI / colour-coded Form VII); dispatch centrally, usually by post.
time_limit: Certificate + UDID card within 3 months of application (Rule 18, as amended 2024)
note: Colour band by severity: White (<40%), Yellow (40-79%), Blue (80%+). Physical card dispatch may lag certificate download by additional weeks.

post_name: State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities / notified Appellate Authority
action: Hear appeal against rejection or disputed percentage; order re-assessment or revision.
time_limit: Appeal within 90 days of rejection (Form VIII)
on_reject: Further remedy before the State/Chief Commissioner for PwD (s.75/s.80 RPwD Act) or the courts.
note: Rejection notified via Form VIII within one month; appeal filed under s.59(1) RPwD Act, 2016. First-stop grievance desk may be the District Disability office / DM; portal-technical issues route to the national UDID helpdesk.

post_name: Junior Engineer (Avar Abhiyanta), Jal Kal Vibhag / Jal Sansthan
action: Inspect the site, confirm main proximity, fix ferrule / pipe / meter size, and prepare the demand note.
note: The JE records feasibility and specifications that drive the charge computation, and (for road tapping) the road-cutting requirement.

post_name: Assistant Engineer (Sahayak Abhiyanta), Jal Kal Vibhag / Jal Sansthan
action: Assess and issue the demand: connection / ferrule fee, road-cutting-restoration charge, security deposit, meter cost.
note: Charges are levied under the U.P. Water Supply & Sewerage Act 1975 and the local schedule; exact amounts are city-specific and not quoted here — expect a fee, deposit and meter cost.

action: Deposit the assessed demand (connection fee, security deposit, meter, road-cutting) at counter / treasury / online.
note: Retain the challan / receipt — the sanction and work order are issued only after full payment.

post_name: Executive Engineer (Adhishasi Abhiyanta), Jal Kal Vibhag / Jal Sansthan
action: Sanction the connection and issue the work order authorising tapping of the distribution main.
on_reject: Appeal to General Manager (Jal Kal) / Municipal Commissioner (UP) or the General Manager, Jal Sansthan (UK); then the First Appellate Authority under the state Right-to-Service Act.
note: The zonal Executive Engineer is the competent sanctioning authority in the Jal Kal Vibhag / Jal Sansthan (each operational zone is headed by an Executive Engineer).

post_name: Junior Engineer (Avar Abhiyanta), Jal Kal Vibhag / Jal Sansthan
action: Obtain road-cutting NOC (PWD / Nagar Nigam roads dept) if the main lies across a public road.
note: Required where tapping needs excavation of a public carriageway; the restoration charge is already collected in the demand at step 6.

post_name: Junior Engineer (Avar Abhiyanta), Jal Kal Vibhag / Jal Sansthan
action: Supervise tapping the main, laying the service pipe, fitting the meter, commissioning supply; restore the road.
note: Work is done by the department or an empanelled licensed plumber under JE supervision; meter reading and billing then commence in the applicant's name.

post_name: General Manager (Jal Kal) / Municipal Commissioner (Nagar Ayukt)
action: Escalate delay or refusal to the GM Jal Kal / GM Jal Sansthan, then the Municipal Commissioner, via the grievance channel.
on_reject: CM Helpline (UP 1076 / UK 1905); IGRS jansunwai.up.nic.in; Jal Sansthan customer care 1800-180-4100 / 1916.
note: First administrative escalation above the Executive Engineer within the Nagar Nigam / Jal Sansthan.

action: If a notified service-delivery timeline was breached, appeal to the designated First then Second Appellate Authority.
on_reject: State / District Consumer forum; writ petition; Lokvani / IGRS grievance channels.
note: The U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 / Uttarakhand Right to Service Act 2011 provide a designated officer plus First/Second Appellate Authority and penalties for default. The specific guaranteed day-count for a new water connection is not verified here — confirm the notified schedule locally.

action: Receive and forward the application to the PIO where filed at sub-office.
note: Section 5(2) RTI Act: APIO (common at sub-district level, tehsil, and post offices) only receives and forwards; adds 5 days to the disposal clock (proviso to Section 7(1)). Skip this step if filed directly with the PIO or via the state online portal.

post_name: Applicant / Citizen (self, or via Jan Seva Kendra CSC operator)
action: Register on UDID portal swavlambancard.gov.in; fill personal, disability and address details.
note: Free. In UP the assisted route is the Jan Seva Kendra / CSC or e-District. An enrolment number is issued to track status. Portal is run by DEPwD. Confidence high on portal/route.

action: Upload identity proof, address proof, photograph, and any existing medical/disability records; select district hospital/CMO.
note: Aadhaar, photo, address proof and prior medical records. Applicant selects the designated assessing hospital / CMO office in their district. Grounded in DEPwD UDID application flow.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (UDID cell, District Hospital / CMO office)
action: Receive and scrutinise application on portal; verify documents; assign a medical assessment date.
on_reject: Application returned on portal for correction/resubmission of documents.
note: The application lands with the designated medical authority selected in Step 2. RPwD Rules 2017 Rule 18(1): medical authority verifies information before assessment.

post_name: Medical Officer (MO) / Specialist (orthopaedic, ophthalmologist, ENT, psychiatrist as per disability)
action: Examine applicant on assigned date; measure impairment and quantify disability percentage per notified guidelines.
note: Assessment per Gazette Notification S.O. 76(E), 04.01.2018. Single specialist for some categories (e.g. locomotor); a full Medical Board for multiple/intellectual/mental disability. Applicant brings originals.

post_name: Medical Board (chaired by Chief Medical Officer (CMO) / Civil Surgeon)
action: Deliberate on assessment, fix disability category and percentage, and decide eligibility for certification.
time_limit: Within one month of receipt of application (RPwD Rules 2017, Rule 18(3))
on_reject: If found ineligible, reasons conveyed in Form VIII within one month; appeal under RPwD Act s.59 within 90 days of rejection (Rule 18(4)).
note: The decisive step. CMO chairs the district Medical Board. Certificate issues only if the person is a person with a specified disability (benefits generally require >=40%). Confidence high (statutory).

post_name: Chief Medical Officer (CMO) / Medical Superintendent (competent medical authority)
action: Generate the disability certificate in Form V / VI / VII and digitally sign it on the portal.
time_limit: Within one month of receipt (RPwD Rules 2017, Rule 18(3))
note: Form VII for a single disability; Form V/VI for multiple disabilities. Certificate is valid across the country (RPwD Act s.58(3)). Digitally signed by the competent medical authority.

post_name: UDID Cell, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD, Central)
action: Generate the UDID number and card centrally after certificate approval; enable e-card download.
note: UDID card carries a unique ID, disability type and percentage; single nationally-valid credential. E-card downloadable immediately; generated centrally by DEPwD after the CMO approves. Confidence high on structure.

action: Dispatch the physical PVC UDID card to the applicant's address by post; e-card remains downloadable.
time_limit: Physical card typically 30-60 days (administrative, not statutory)
note: The downloadable e-card is the operative credential; the PVC card follows by post. Turnaround for the physical card is administrative, not a statutory day-count. Confidence high on route, medium on exact turnaround.

post_name: Applicant / Citizen (via portal track-status or Jan Seva Kendra)
action: Track status by enrolment number; if stalled beyond one month, escalate to the CMO / designated hospital.
note: Rule 18(3) fixes one month for issuance; delay beyond it is escalable to the CMO/Medical Superintendent, then the portal grievance channel. Confidence high on the one-month peg.

post_name: Appellate Authority designated by State Government (Directorate of Medical & Health Services / State Medical Board)
action: Hear appeal against rejection or wrongly-assessed percentage; re-decide the certification.
time_limit: Appeal within 90 days of rejection (RPwD Rules 2017, Rule 18(4) read with Act s.59)
on_reject: Further complaint of denial of rights lies with the State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (RPwD Act, ss.79-80); UP: cmsdivyangjan.up.gov.in.
note: Section 59 vests appeal in a State-designated appellate authority; the 90-day window is fixed by Rule 18(4). Exact appellate body name varies by state notification (UP: State Medical Board / DGMH). Confidence high on provision, medium on exact body.

post_name: State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (statutory)
action: Hear complaints of deprivation of rights or non-implementation; direct remedial action on the certificate/benefits.
on_reject: Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities at the Centre (RPwD Act, ss.74-75).
note: Statutory grievance forum under RPwD Act ss.79-80 for denial of rights (distinct from the medical-percentage appeal). UP court: cmsdivyangjan.up.gov.in. Confidence high (statutory).

action: Register person with disability on swavlambancard.gov.in; fill UDID application, upload photo, Aadhaar, medical records
note: Offline alternative: apply at district hospital/CMO office or via state e-district (UP: edistrict.up.gov.in; Uttarakhand e-district); staff enter same portal.

action: Receive and register application, verify uploaded documents and identity/address proofs for completeness
on_reject: Deficiency memo issued; applicant asked to re-upload or resubmit missing documents.
note: CMO office is the receiving/dealing point for the notified Medical Authority.

post_name: Medical Board (chaired by CMO / Civil Surgeon)
action: Assess and quantify disability as a percentage per gazette assessment guidelines
on_reject: Below-benchmark cases may still get a certificate stating percentage; re-assessment can be sought.
note: 40% is the benchmark ('benchmark disability') for most reservations/benefits under the RPwD Act.

action: Approve and digitally sign the Disability Certificate; push it to the UDID portal
time_limit: Within one month of application (RPwD Rules 2017, r.18)
note: Certificate is digitally signed; permanent vs temporary/re-assessment date noted per condition.

action: Generate UDID centrally; make e-UDID available for download and dispatch physical card
note: e-UDID downloadable soon after certification; physical card by post takes weeks to months.

post_name: District Disability Welfare Officer / District Social Welfare Officer
action: Sanction the pension and enrol the beneficiary on the pension roll.
on_reject: Rejection is appealable to the next-higher authority (Director/Deputy Director, Divyangjan Sashaktikaran / Samaj Kalyan) and via the portal grievance cell.
note: This is the decision step. Sanctioning authority is the designated district welfare officer; some districts route final approval through the District Magistrate/Collector-level committee.

action: Set up and credit recurring monthly pension to the Aadhaar-linked bank account by DBT.
note: UP Rs 1,000/month paid quarterly (Rs 3,000/quarter); Uttarakhand Rs 1,200-1,500/month. Direct Benefit Transfer, no intermediary; may include arrears from sanction date.

post_name: District Disability Welfare Officer / District Social Welfare Officer
action: Conduct periodic re-verification (annual continued-eligibility/life check) to keep pension active.
on_reject: Payment paused pending re-verification; beneficiary completes eKYC/life certificate to reinstate.
note: Annual re-confirmation of eligibility is required; portals support eKYC for continuation.

post_name: Appellate authority (Right to Public Services / Sewa Adhikar)
action: Hear appeal on delay past service deadline or on rejection; direct sanction if due.
on_reject: Further appeal to second appellate authority / ombudsman (Lokayukt) or the High Court.
note: UP: escalation under the Uttar Pradesh Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 where the service is notified. Grievance/status functions exist on both state pension portals. Whether pension sanction is a notified guaranteed service should be confirmed locally.

post_name: Protection Officer (District, appointed under Section 8 PWDVA)
action: Aggrieved woman reports abuse; Protection Officer records Domestic Incident Report (Form I) and informs her of rights
on_reject: May approach a registered service provider, police, or file directly with the Magistrate - PO route is optional (Section 4)
note: Section 4/9 & Rule 5: any person may inform the Protection Officer; woman may also go direct to court. DIR is Form I under Rule 5.

post_name: Protection Officer / Station House Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Forward the Domestic Incident Report to the Magistrate and to the local police station; assist woman in getting legal aid
on_reject: Woman/counsel may file the application directly without waiting for the DIR
note: Section 9 & Rule 8/10: PO forwards copies of DIR to Magistrate and police officer in charge; ensures free legal aid under Legal Services Authorities Act.

post_name: Aggrieved Person / Protection Officer (applicant to court)
action: File application for protection order to the Magistrate in Form II under Section 12, seeking reliefs sought
note: Section 12 & Rule 6: application in Form II may be filed by the aggrieved person, a Protection Officer, or any other person on her behalf. No court fee.

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate
action: Fix the first date of hearing on the application after receiving it
time_limit: Within 3 days of receipt of the application (Section 12(4))
note: Section 27: JMFC/Metropolitan Magistrate within whose jurisdiction the woman resides/works, respondent resides, or cause of action arose, has jurisdiction.

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate
action: Consider Domestic Incident Report; grant interim or ex parte protection order if satisfied prima facie of violence
time_limit: May be granted at first hearing / same day (Section 23)
on_reject: Aggrieved person may lead further evidence at the full hearing; final order can still grant relief
note: Section 23: Magistrate may pass interim orders and, on an affidavit (Form III), ex parte orders under ss.18-22 before the respondent is heard.

action: Serve notice of the hearing (and any interim order) on the respondent as directed by the Magistrate
time_limit: Within a maximum of 2 days, or further time allowed by the Magistrate (Section 13 & Rule 12)
on_reject: Substituted service may be ordered by the Magistrate if the respondent evades service
note: Section 13 & Rule 12: notice served by Protection Officer; a declaration of service by the PO is proof of service.

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate
action: Hold hearing; both parties appear, evidence and counter-affidavit considered; respondent may contest
time_limit: Endeavour to dispose of the application within 60 days of the first hearing (Section 12(5))
note: Section 12(5): Magistrate shall endeavour to dispose of every application within 60 days of the first hearing. May direct counselling (Section 14) or welfare expert (Section 15).

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate
action: Decide the application and, if satisfied domestic violence occurred, pass the Protection Order under Section 18
on_reject: Appeal to the Court of Session within 30 days from service of the order (Section 29)
note: Section 18 protection order prohibits further violence, contact, entry, etc. Magistrate may also pass residence (19), monetary relief (20), custody (21), compensation (22) orders.

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate
action: Sign the order; supply free certified copies to the aggrieved person and respondent
note: Section 24: copies given free of cost to parties, Protection Officer, and the police station in charge of the area. Protection order remains in force until aggrieved person applies for discharge (Section 25).

post_name: Protection Officer / Station House Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Serve/enforce the order; on breach, register cognizable offence and arrest respondent
note: Section 31: breach of a protection order is a cognizable, non-bailable offence - up to 1 year imprisonment and/or fine up to Rs.20,000. Copy sent to SHO under Section 24.

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate
action: On application, modify, alter or revoke the order on change of circumstances
on_reject: Appeal to Court of Session within 30 days (Section 29)
note: Section 25(2): either party may apply for alteration/modification/revocation on change in circumstances. Protection order continues until discharged.

action: Hear appeal against the Magistrate's order and confirm, modify or set it aside
time_limit: Appeal to be filed within 30 days of service of the order (Section 29)
on_reject: Further remedy by revision/writ before the High Court (outside PWDVA)
note: Section 29: appeal lies to the Court of Session within 30 days from the date the order is served on the aggrieved person or the respondent, whichever is later.

action: Assist applicant, and if delayed or denied, follow up on pending assessment or reprocessing
note: District Disability Rehabilitation Centre (DDRC) often facilitates camps and the process.

post_name: State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities
action: Adjudicate grievance/appeal against delay, denial, or disputed assessment percentage
note: Statutory grievance authority under RPwD Act s.79-80. Also portal grievance/helpdesk and state Right-to-Service appeal (UP Janhit Guarantee / Uttarakhand RTS designated appellate officer).

action: Register application; if misdirected, transfer to the correct authority.
note: Section 6(3) RTI Act: PIO transfers a misdirected application (or the relevant part) to the correct public authority within 5 days and informs the applicant.

action: Notify affected third party where record involves third-party information.
time_limit: 5 days to notify; third party 10 days to object
note: Section 11 RTI Act: PIO gives third party written notice within 5 days; third party has 10 days to represent. Total disposal in such cases extends to 40 days. Applies only when third-party info is implicated.

action: Gather the information and furnish it, or refuse with reasons.
time_limit: 30 days (35 via APIO; 48 hours if life/liberty; 40 with third party)
on_reject: First appeal to the First Appellate Authority under Section 19(1)
note: Section 7 RTI Act: disposal within 30 days of receipt (35 if via APIO). Life/liberty cases: 48 hours (Section 7(1) proviso). Failure to respond in time = deemed refusal (Section 7(2)); no additional fee then chargeable. Refusals must cite exempt provisions (Sections 8/9) and state appeal rights.

action: Hear first appeal on no reply, unsatisfactory reply, or refusal; decide.
time_limit: File within 30 days; FAA decides in 30 days (extendable to 45)
on_reject: Second appeal to the State Information Commission under Section 19(3)
note: Section 19(1) RTI Act: FAA is an officer senior in rank to the PIO within the same department. Applicant files within 30 days of the deadline or response (condonable for cause). FAA decides within 30 days, extendable to 45 with reasons (Section 19(6)).

action: Gather residence, identity and age proofs plus a self-declaration affidavit; confirm the state's residence-duration threshold.
note: UP typically expects proof of roughly 3 years' residence; exact document set and duration rule are state-specific and can change (uncertain) - verify on the portal or at the tehsil.

post_name: Applicant (Citizen) / Common Service Centre (Jan Seva Kendra) operator
action: Submit application online via the state e-District portal or a Jan Seva Kendra; pay the statutory fee.
note: UP: edistrict.up.gov.in / e-Sathi (esathi.up.gov.in). Uttarakhand: Apuni Sarkar / edistrict.uk.gov.in. Fee is small (~Rs.15 in UP). An acknowledgement / tracking number is issued.

action: Scrutinise the application and attachments for completeness; forward down to the field revenue officer for verification.
on_reject: Application returned to the applicant for correction and resubmission via the same portal.
note: Tehsil counter / e-District back-office triage before field verification.

action: Conduct field/neighbourhood check that the applicant actually resides at the stated address for the required period; file report.
on_reject: Adverse verification report can lead to rejection; applicant may re-apply with stronger residence proof.
note: Village/ward-level revenue officer (Lekhpal in UP/Uttarakhand). Normally the longest, most variable stage.

action: Review the Lekhpal's field report, countersign/endorse it, and forward it up to the Tehsildar.
note: Kanungo / Revenue Inspector is the supervisory revenue tier between Lekhpal and Tehsildar. Not a decision point.

action: Review the verified report and approve issuance of the Nivas Praman Patra.
on_reject: Rejection order must state a reason; appeal lies to the First Appellate Officer (SDM) under the state service-guarantee Act.
note: Tehsildar is the designated issuing authority for UP/Uttarakhand domicile certificates, acting under the DM/Collectorate. The time limit runs under the UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 / Uttarakhand Sewa Ka Adhikar Adhiniyam 2011.

action: Digitally sign the certificate and release it (with QR/verification ID) for download from the e-District portal.
note: UP domicile certificate is lifetime-valid; some certificate types elsewhere require renewal (state-specific, uncertain).

action: Download the digitally signed certificate from the portal using the tracking number; verify the QR/authentication.
note: Offline alternative: collect from the Tehsil / Jan Seva Kendra counter. Acceptance for a specific job/college depends on that institution's own rules.

action: On delay past the statutory limit or wrongful rejection, hear the first appeal and direct issuance.
on_reject: Second appeal to the District Magistrate / designated Second Appellate Officer; grievance via CM Helpline (1076) / IGRS. A wrongful rejection can ultimately be challenged before the Collector or by writ.
note: First Appellate Officer under the UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 / Uttarakhand Sewa Ka Adhikar Adhiniyam 2011, which carry a penalty on the defaulting officer for unjustified delay.

action: Confirm eligibility: age 60+, state resident, income below ceiling / BPL, not drawing another pension.
note: UP SSPY income ceiling: Rs 46,080/yr rural, Rs 56,460/yr urban. Uttarakhand: income up to Rs 4,000/month from all sources or BPL. Age threshold is firmly 60+ (draft's 65 is incorrect for the state scheme). 'No regular income' qualifies but must be evidenced by an income certificate or BPL card.

action: Assemble documents: age proof, residence/domicile, income certificate or BPL, Aadhaar, bank passbook, photo.
note: Bank account must be Aadhaar-linked for DBT. In Uttarakhand a family register (rural, issued by VPDO) or ration card (urban) is required. Income certificate is itself an e-district/RTPS service if not already held.

action: Issue income certificate through e-District if applicant lacks one; establishes the below-ceiling income fact.
on_reject: Re-apply with supporting income evidence; income-certificate refusal is itself appealable under the state RTPS/Janhit Guarantee schedule.
note: Prerequisite, not part of the pension sanction chain. The income certificate is the key gating document confirming 'no regular income'. Handled by the Tehsil revenue chain (Lekhpal -> Tehsildar/SDM).

action: Submit online application on state Integrated Pension Portal (sspy-up.gov.in / ssp.uk.gov.in) or via CSC.
note: Corrects draft: intake is the online state portal (or Common Service Centre / Apuni Sarkar e-services in Uttarakhand), NOT the Collectorate counter or the Gram Panchayat form. Applicant selects 'Old Age Pension' -> 'Apply Online', fills personal/bank/income fields, uploads documents, submits. UMANG and myScheme also route here.

action: Field-verify residence and income at village level; in Uttarakhand list is placed before open Gram Sabha.
on_reject: Discrepancy returned to applicant for correction/resubmission before higher forwarding.
note: Uttarakhand rural chain: Gram Panchayat Development Officer (VPDO) -> Assistant Social Welfare Officer recommend; beneficiaries are selected in an open Gram Sabha meeting. This is the local-verification layer the draft was unsure about.

action: Verify rural applications via official login and forward recommended cases to the sanctioning officer.
on_reject: Returned to lower level / applicant if particulars fail verification.
note: On SSPY, the BDO verifies rural applications with a login ID and forwards to the District Social Welfare Officer. In Uttarakhand the BDO recommends onward to the DSWO.

action: Verify urban applications (SDM / Sub-District Officer login) and forward recommended cases for sanction.
on_reject: Returned for correction if urban residence/income particulars fail verification.
note: SSPY urban verification is done by SDM / SDO (in Uttarakhand, Assistant Social Welfare Officer + Sub-District Magistrate). Parallel to step 6 depending on rural vs urban applicant; only one of steps 5-7's paths applies.

post_name: District Social Welfare Officer / District Probation Officer (DPO)
action: Scrutinise the verified case and sanction the pension; approval initiates DBT enrolment.
time_limit: Approx. 30-60 days from complete application (per state RTPS / Janhit Guarantee service window)
on_reject: Applicant may seek review by the District Magistrate / Collector and file a statutory appeal under the UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 / Uttarakhand Right to Service Act if the time limit lapses or the case is wrongly rejected.
note: This is the actual sanctioning authority, correcting the draft's uncertainty: the District Social Welfare Officer (in UP the District Probation Officer / DPO handles pension sanction) signs, NOT the District Magistrate case-by-case.
