The DM/Collector is supervisory and appellate. Post-name uses the real official designations.

action: Gather residence, identity, age proofs and self-declaration affidavit; confirm state's residence-duration threshold.
note: UP typically requires proof of at least ~3 years' residence; exact document set and residence-duration rule are state-specific (uncertain).

post_name: Applicant (Citizen) / Common Service Centre (Jan Seva Kendra) operator
action: Submit application online via state e-District portal or a Jan Seva Kendra; pay statutory fee.
note: UP: edistrict.up.gov.in / e-Sathi (esathi.up.gov.in); Uttarakhand: edistrict.uk.gov.in. Fee ~Rs.15 in UP. An acknowledgement / tracking number is issued.

action: Scrutinise application and attachments for completeness; forward down to field revenue officer for verification.
on_reject: Application returned to applicant for correction/resubmission via the same portal.
note: Tehsil counter / e-district back-office triage before field verification.

action: Verify applicant actually resides at stated address for the required period; conduct field/neighbourhood check.
on_reject: Adverse verification report can lead to rejection; applicant may re-apply with stronger residence proof.
note: Village/ward-level revenue officer (Lekhpal in UP/Uttarakhand). Normally the longest, most variable stage.

action: Review the Lekhpal's field report, countersign/endorse, and forward up to the Tehsildar.
note: Kanungo / Revenue Inspector is the supervisory revenue tier between Lekhpal and Tehsildar.

action: Review verified report and approve issuance of the Nivas Praman Patra.
on_reject: Rejection order stated with reason; appeal to First Appellate Authority (SDM) under the Janhit Guarantee / Sewa Ka Adhikar Act.
note: Tehsildar is the designated issuing authority for UP/Uttarakhand domicile certificates (acting under the DM/Collectorate). Time limit runs under the state service-guarantee act.

action: Digitally sign the certificate; make it downloadable from the e-District portal.
note: UP domicile certificate is lifetime-valid. Some states/certificate types require renewal (state-specific, uncertain).

action: Download digitally signed certificate from portal using tracking number; verify QR/authentication.
note: Offline alternative: collect from Tehsil / Jan Seva Kendra counter.

post_name: Protection Officer (District Protection Officer, notified u/s 8 PWDVA)
action: Record the Domestic Incident Report (DIR) in Form I with details of abuse and reliefs needed.
note: PO duty under s. 9 and Rule 5; DIR is Form I of the 2006 Rules. In UP the PO is usually the District Probation/Protection Officer under WCD. A service provider (s. 10) may also record it.

action: On delay past the statutory limit or wrongful rejection, hear the first appeal and direct issuance.
on_reject: Second appeal to the District Magistrate / designated senior appellate authority; grievance via CM Helpline (1076) / IGRS.
note: First Appellate Authority under the UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 / Uttarakhand Sewa Ka Adhikar Adhiniyam, 2011. A wrongful rejection can ultimately be challenged before the Collector or by writ petition (rarely needed).

post_name: District Social Welfare Officer / District Probation Officer (DPO)
action: Release sanctioned pension in quarterly installments via NEFT/DBT to the Aadhaar-linked account.
note: Corrects draft: payment is quarterly (four installments/year) by NEFT/DBT once funds are released by the state directorate (HQ Lucknow in UP), not monthly cash/money order. Nominal monthly rate: UP ~Rs 1,000, Uttarakhand Rs 1,500.

action: Hear appeals against rejection/delay and enforce time-bound delivery under the state Right-to-Service Act.
time_limit: Statutory appeal window under UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 / Uttarakhand Right to Service Act
on_reject: Second appeal to the designated appellate authority under the RTPS Act; parallel grievance via CM Helpline (1076) / state social-welfare grievance portal.
note: Escalation ladder, grounded: (1) review by District Social Welfare Officer / DPO; (2) District Magistrate / Collector; (3) statutory RTPS appeal under the Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam if the service window lapses; (4) CM Helpline / department grievance portal. Confirms the Collectorate's real role here is supervisory/appellate, as the draft suspected.

action: Hear second appeal; order disclosure and impose penalty on defaulting PIO.
time_limit: File within 90 days of FAA decision
on_reject: Writ petition to the High Court under Article 226 (no civil suit; Section 23 bars courts)
note: Section 19(3) RTI Act: second appeal to the State Information Commission (UP: UP State Information Commission; Uttarakhand: Uttarakhand Information Commission). Central bodies go to the CIC instead. Final adjudicator; can order disclosure and impose penalty of Rs 250/day up to Rs 25,000 on the PIO (Section 20). Burden of justifying denial is on the PIO (Section 19(5)).

action: Register on state police CCTNS citizen portal, fill Tenant/PG Verification form, upload tenant ID/photo.
note: Landlord (not the tenant) is the applicant. UP: CCTNS citizen portal 'Tenant/PG Verification'. Offline route: submit filled form at the local police station. Post-title is applicant, not an official designation.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (Police Station reception / CCTNS operator)
action: Receive request, check completeness of form and attachments, generate acknowledgement/reference number.
on_reject: Incomplete file returned to applicant for missing tenant ID/address proof/photo.
note: Attach: tenant govt photo ID and address proof, tenant photograph, landlord ID/ownership or rent-agreement proof; a registered rent agreement strengthens the file.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Register the verification request at the police station and assign it to the jurisdictional beat officer.
note: The police station with jurisdiction over the property address is the operational host, not the revenue collectorate.

action: Verify tenant identity, address and antecedents; physically confirm occupancy at the property.
note: Beat officer conducts the actual field verification. Real designation: beat/local constable under the SHO.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: If tenant is from another district/state, forward a query to the tenant's home police jurisdiction.
note: Interstate/inter-district tenants require a home-jurisdiction antecedents check, which lengthens processing.

action: Compile findings (clear / adverse antecedents) and submit the verification report to the SHO.
note: Report records whether any adverse criminal record was found.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Review the beat report and decide the outcome: no adverse record (clear) or adverse report.
on_reject: Adverse report recorded; landlord may seek review via the Circle Officer/ACP or SP grievance channel.
note: The SHO records the verification outcome. This is the decisive step for the request.

action: Identify area DISCOM and apply online via Jhatpat portal (upenergy.in) declaring sanctioned load in kW.
note: In UP the licensee is a UPPCL DISCOM for the applicant's zone (PVVNL Meerut, MVVNL Lucknow, PuVVNL Varanasi, DVVNL Agra, KESCO Kanpur) or a private licensee (NPCL/Torrent); in Uttarakhand it is UPCL. Application also accepted at Jan Suvidha / e-Suvidha centres or the sub-division office. Domestic (DS) load selectable 1 kW to 500 kW.

action: Upload ID proof, ownership/occupancy proof, photograph; pay application fee (Rs 100 APL / Rs 10 BPL).
note: Ownership proof per Supply Code: registered sale deed / partition deed / succession or heir (vasiyat) certificate; occupant may use rent agreement + owner NOC. Fee amounts are the Jhatpat scheme rates; the refundable security deposit and line/service charges come later via the demand note, not at application.

action: Register application, verify documents for completeness, generate application/registration number.
on_reject: Deficiency memo issued; applicant re-submits missing documents; deemed-registration on completeness.
note: Scrutiny/registration at the DISCOM sub-division (Vidyut Vitran Khand) serving the address. Incomplete applications are returned with a checklist rather than rejected outright.

action: Conduct site/feasibility inspection: confirm load, nearest distribution pole/point, and technical feasibility.
on_reject: Infeasibility recorded with reasons; applicant may contest via CGRF (step 10).
note: Applicant suggests up to three preferred inspection dates on the portal. The DISCOM JE (Avar Abhiyanta) is the field officer; assesses whether existing mains suffice or a line extension/transformer augmentation is needed - this determines the release timeline.

action: Prepare and file the Section 12 application in Form II before the Magistrate, listing reliefs sought.
note: Application u/s 12 in Form II (Rule 6). Reliefs: protection order (s.18), residence (s.19), monetary relief (s.20), custody (s.21), compensation (s.22). Filed in the local court complex.

post_name: Sub-Divisional Officer / Assistant Engineer (SDO/AE, Upkhand Adhikari)
action: Prepare cost estimate and issue the demand note specifying charges and security deposit.
on_reject: Dispute estimate before Executive Engineer or CGRF; excess/erroneous charges refundable.
note: Demand note (Supply Code cl. 4.x) itemizes processing/registration fee, refundable security deposit, and any service-line / system-loading (development) charges. The statutory release clock in step 8 runs from the applicant's compliance with this demand note.

action: Pay demand-note charges and security deposit online or at the sub-division cash counter.
note: Payment (compliance of the demand note) is the trigger event for the statutory release timeline in step 8.

post_name: Executive Engineer (Adhishasi Abhiyanta / XEN, Vidyut Vitran Khand)
action: Sanction the connection and authorize meter installation at the approved load.
on_reject: Appeal refusal/improper conditions to CGRF, then Electricity Ombudsman.
note: This is the decisional approval: the Executive Engineer (or delegated SDO for small DS loads) sanctions supply under the DISCOM's duty to supply (Electricity Act s.43). Sanctioning authority varies with load slab per DISCOM delegation.

action: Install meter and energize the connection within the regulated release period.
time_limit: 7 days (DS, no mains extension) / 15 days (minor extension) from demand-note compliance; longer where new infrastructure needed
on_reject: Delay beyond the standard entitles the applicant to compensation under Standards of Performance / Rights of Consumers Rules 2020; escalate via steps 9-11.
note: UP Electricity Supply Code 2005 cl. 4.15/4.16: supply within 7 days for DS/NRS where no augmentation/erection/extension of distribution mains is required, 15 days where minor extension needed. Uttarakhand (UERC Supply Code) allows up to ~90 days for fresh connections needing infrastructure. Jhatpat scheme markets ~10 days end-to-end.

post_name: Executive Engineer (Adhishasi Abhiyanta / XEN, Vidyut Vitran Khand)
action: First-level grievance: register delay/refusal complaint via 1912 or the sub-division/circle grievance cell.
on_reject: If unresolved, approach the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum (step 10).
note: Internal DISCOM redressal (toll-free 1912 / 1800-180-8752) is the first tier before the statutory forum. Not a separate statute; part of the DISCOM's consumer-service obligations.

action: Adjudicate the grievance if internal redressal fails or times out.
time_limit: Resolution generally within the period set by CGRF Regulations 2022; ~90 days outer limit
on_reject: Approach the Electricity Ombudsman (Vidyut Lokpal) within 30 days of the CGRF order or expiry of the resolution period.
note: Constituted under UPERC (Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum & Electricity Ombudsman) Regulations, 2022 (notified 21-07-2022), at circle and company level. In Uttarakhand the equivalent CGRF operates under UERC regulations.

action: Final statutory appeal: hear representation against the CGRF order or unresolved grievance.
time_limit: File within 30 days of CGRF order or expiry of its resolution period
on_reject: Order binding on the licensee; further recourse only via writ jurisdiction of the High Court.
note: Electricity Ombudsman appointed by UPERC under Electricity Act 2003 s.42(6) and the 2022 Regulations. Delay compensation under the Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020 / Standards of Performance may also be claimed here.

action: Locate your Property ID / House Tax No. on any earlier bill or receipt; if none, proceed to get the property assessed.
note: The PID is the key to the whole transaction. On e-NagarSewa UP it may also be searched by owner name / address / old bill number. A property never assessed has no PID until steps 2-4 create one.

action: For a new/unassessed property, request assessment; the inspector surveys the property and records area, use and location.
note: Ward-level revenue field officer of the Nagar Nigam Kar Vibhag. Records the built-up area, usage (residential/commercial) and location factors that drive the annual value. Skip if the property already has a Property ID.

action: Assess the annual value, fix the annual house-tax demand, approve the assessment and generate the Property ID.
on_reject: File an objection/appeal against the assessment before the assessing authority under the U.P. Municipal Corporation Act 1959 taxation rules.
note: The Kar Adhikshak verifies the Revenue Inspector's assessment list and is the competent assessing/approving officer in the corporation's Revenue Department. Only relevant for first-time assessment or reassessment; routine payment needs no such approval.

action: Enter your Property ID on the e-NagarSewa UP portal (or ask at the counter) to view the current-year demand plus arrears/penalty.
note: UP: e-nagarsewaup.gov.in -> Property Tax -> search by PID. Uttarakhand: the Nagar Nigam's own property-tax portal or serviceonline.gov.in/uttarakhand. Confirm any early-payment rebate window or self-occupied/senior-citizen discount before paying.

action: Check eligibility via beneficiary.nha.gov.in, Ayushman App, or helpline 14555 using mobile/Aadhaar/ration details
note: Eligibility is pre-determined from the SECC 2011 deprivation database plus state-added categories, not by applying. A central 'not found' is not final where the state runs a converged/expanded scheme (UP: SACHIS lists; Uttarakhand: Atal Ayushman covers all domiciled residents) — recheck at district level.

post_name: Ayushman Mitra / CSC Village Level Entrepreneur (VLE)
action: Assist the family to locate the beneficiary record and initiate registration at hospital kiosk or CSC
note: Alternative to self-service: an Ayushman Mitra at an empanelled hospital or a CSC VLE searches the beneficiary list and starts the registration. CSC self-download is free; historically a small nominal fee (~Rs. 30) was charged at some CSCs — treat as approximate and confirm locally.

action: Complete Aadhaar e-KYC via OTP or face authentication and capture the beneficiary photo
note: e-KYC matches the applicant to the SECC/beneficiary record. Aadhaar is the standard KYC; ration card / family ID helps match the household. Self-service e-KYC is now available directly in the Ayushman App / beneficiary portal via Aadhaar OTP or face auth — a major shift from the old operator-only flow.

post_name: State Health Agency system (SACHIS / State Health Authority)
action: Auto-authenticate the e-KYC against the beneficiary database and approve straightforward cases
on_reject: Ambiguous or mismatched cases are routed to the District Implementation Unit under the CMO for manual review; the applicant is asked to submit corrected documents or apply for a name addition.
note: Approval is largely automated once e-KYC matches. This is the decisive step: a matched record yields an approved (authenticated) card the same visit.

post_name: Chief Medical Officer (CMO) / District Implementation Unit
action: Review flagged, mismatched, or name-addition cases at district level and authorize the record
on_reject: Applicant is informed of the deficiency and may resubmit; unresolved disputes escalate to the SHA and then central CGRMS grievance redressal.
note: The District Implementation Unit sits under the Chief Medical Officer's office (the district-health office owning local PM-JAY implementation). Exact unit title varies by state — the function is district-level beneficiary verification/addition. Flagged cases can take a few days to ~2 weeks.

action: Download or print the authenticated Ayushman card (golden card) from the app, portal, or kiosk
note: Once approved the card is downloadable free from the Ayushman App / beneficiary.nha.gov.in, or printable by the operator. Physical 'golden cards' have largely been replaced by the digital Ayushman card; the 'golden card' term persists colloquially.

action: Escalate if not found, rejected, or stuck: call 14555, then district CMO/DIU, then SHA, then central CGRMS
note: Escalation ladder: (1) helpline 14555 / 1800-111-565; (2) District Implementation Unit / district hospital Ayushman Mitra desk under the CMO; (3) State Health Agency (UP: SACHIS; Uttarakhand: State Health Authority) via the state grievance portal; (4) central CGRMS at cgrms.pmjay.gov.in. Helpline numbers and portal URLs are from general memory and should be reconfirmed against the live portal.

action: Pay the shown amount online by UPI / net-banking / card, or in cash / cheque / card at the Nagar Nigam counter or CSC.
on_reject: If the online payment is debited but not credited, retain the transaction reference and raise it via steps 8-9 for reconciliation.
note: Online is self-service (no official approval). In person, payment is taken by the ward Bill Collector / counter cashier (Lipik) at the Citizen Service Centre. Cheques clear before the receipt finalises.

action: At the counter, record the payment in the collection register and hand over a stamped, signed physical receipt.
note: For counter payments only. Collections are later reconciled/verified by the accounts wing and the Tax Superintendent against the demand-and-collection register. Online payments skip this step (system issues the receipt directly).

action: Download/print the e-receipt generated instantly against the Property ID; keep it as proof of payment.
note: The e-receipt is proof for mutation, sale, loan and No-Dues certificate. If a gateway lag delays it, it reflects within 24-48 hours; re-download from the portal against the PID/transaction ID.

post_name: Revenue Inspector / Ward Revenue Office (Rajasva Nirikshak)
action: If the amount is wrong, payment is uncredited, or no receipt issues, raise it first at the ward revenue office / helpline.
on_reject: If unresolved, escalate to the Zonal Officer / Municipal Commissioner's office.
note: First point of contact for a routine correction or a credited-but-no-receipt case. Corporation helpline / grievance cell is the parallel channel.

post_name: Zonal Officer (Kshetriya Adhikari) / Municipal Commissioner (Nagar Ayukt)
action: Escalate an unresolved payment/receipt or reconciliation dispute to the zonal office, then the Commissioner's grievance cell.
on_reject: If still unresolved, use the state grievance portal (IGRS Jansunwai / CM Helpline 1076 UP; CM Helpline 1905 Uttarakhand).
note: Administrative escalation ladder inside the Nagar Nigam above the ward revenue office. In smaller towns the counterpart head is the Adhishasi Adhikari (Executive Officer) of the Nagar Palika.

post_name: Designated / First Appellate Authority under the Right-to-Service Act
action: For a formal assessment dispute or a breached notified timeline, appeal to the assessing authority / First Appellate Authority.
on_reject: Second Appellate Authority; then IGRS/Jansunwai or a writ petition.
note: Assessment disputes follow the objection/appeal route under the U.P. Municipal Corporation Act 1959 taxation rules. Service-timeline breaches invoke the U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 / Uttarakhand Right to Service Act 2011 (designated officer + First/Second Appellate Authority). The specific guaranteed day-count for this service is not verified here.

action: Register the complaint on e-NagarSewa UP portal/app or the ULB helpline; note the complaint number.
note: Portal: e-nagarsewaup.gov.in ('Apply Public Grievance'). Ticket number is your proof and escalation lever. Route garbage to Sanitation/Health wing, drain to Engineering wing. Uttarakhand equivalent: file via Nagar Nigam / serviceonline.gov.in/uttarakhand.

action: Receive and verify the garbage complaint; identify the ward and collection gap.
note: Ward-level sanitation official under the Nagar Swasthya Adhikari (City Health Officer). Field-level dispatch; no senior sign-off for routine lifting.

action: Update portal status and issue verification acknowledgement/status to the landlord.
note: Most CCTNS portals show a downloadable acknowledgement/'no adverse report' status rather than a formal certificate.

action: Constitute entity; obtain PAN, GST, bank account; confirm worker headcount and power load cross Factories Act threshold
note: Prerequisite, not part of the licence. Factories Act Sec. 2(m) 'factory' trigger: 10+ workers with power or 20+ without power; below this the factory licence may not be required.

post_name: Local Development Authority / SIDCUL Estate Office (Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) where gram-panchayat/revenue land is involved)
action: Confirm industrial land use / zoning and obtain building-plan approval for the site
on_reject: Reapply after re-zoning / land-use change; land-use appeal to the development authority
note: Approving body depends on whether the plot sits inside a SIDCUL/State Industrial Development Corporation estate, a municipal area, or gram-panchayat/revenue land. SDM named where revenue-land conversion is needed.

post_name: Member Secretary, Uttarakhand Environment Protection & Pollution Control Board (UEPPCB)
action: Apply for Consent to Establish (CTE) under Water Act Sec.25 and Air Act Sec.21 before construction
time_limit: Statutory limit set by state RTS notification; commonly 30-120 days by category (not confirmed this session)
on_reject: Appeal to the Uttarakhand Appellate Authority under the Water/Air Acts; then National Green Tribunal
note: Red/Orange/Green/White categorisation drives documents and timeline. CTE must precede the Factories-Act licence; White-category units are often exempt/self-declared.

post_name: Chief Inspector of Factories, Directorate of Factories, Boilers, Labour & Employment (Uttarakhand)
action: Submit factory building plans and layout for prior approval before constructing the manufacturing area
time_limit: As notified under Uttarakhand Right to Service Act, 2011 (exact days not confirmed this session)
on_reject: Resubmit corrected plans; appeal within Directorate, then State Government / RTS appellate route
note: Factories Act Sec. 6 and Uttarakhand Factories Rules require prior approval of plans/layout (state plan-approval form) before construction.

action: File Sec.7 occupier notice and the application for registration and licence with prescribed fee
note: Application on Form No. 2 (Model/most state rules); occupier notice under Sec. 7. Fee scaled by worker count and installed HP/kW per the Uttarakhand Factories Rules fee schedule (exact form numbers/fees are state-rule specific).

post_name: Inspector of Factories, Directorate of Factories (Uttarakhand)
action: Scrutinise application, occupier/manager particulars and approved plan; inspect premises for compliance
on_reject: Comply with deficiency notice and re-submit
note: Verification of safety, health and welfare provisions and consistency with the approved layout before the licence is granted.

post_name: Chief Inspector of Factories, Directorate of Factories (Uttarakhand)
action: Register the factory and grant the licence to operate under the Factories Act, 1948
time_limit: As notified under Uttarakhand Right to Service Act, 2011 (exact days not confirmed this session)
on_reject: Appeal under Factories Act Sec. 6(2)/state rules to the State Government within the prescribed period; RTS appeal for delay
note: This is the core decision. Licence typically issued on Form No. 4 (Model/most state rules), renewable; the registration number is allotted here. This step is the actual grant of the factory licence.

post_name: Regional Officer, Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) and Regional PF Commissioner, EPFO
action: Register the establishment for ESI and EPF once employee thresholds are crossed
time_limit: ESI/EPF registration is time-bound from the date coverage is attracted
on_reject: Rectify and re-register; appeal under ESI Act / EPF & MP Act to the respective appellate forum
note: ESI Act 1948 applies at 10+ employees (in covered areas); EPF & MP Act 1952 at 20+ employees. Registration via the unified Shram Suvidha portal.

post_name: Registering Officer, Contract Labour (Labour Department, Uttarakhand)
action: Register the principal employer under the Contract Labour Act if using contractor-supplied workers
on_reject: Appeal to the appellate officer under the Contract Labour (R&A) Act, 1970
note: Only if contract workers engaged (threshold 20+ contract workers per the Central Act, subject to state amendment). Also register under Shops & Establishments / labour-welfare rules as applicable.

post_name: Chief Fire Officer, Uttarakhand Fire & Emergency Service (and Director of Boilers where a boiler is run)
action: Obtain Fire NOC and boiler registration/certification only where the process triggers them
on_reject: Rectify fire-safety/boiler deficiencies and reapply; departmental appeal
note: Triggered clearances only: Fire NOC; boiler registration under the Boilers Act 1923; plus Legal Metrology, FSSAI/Drug/explosives/hazardous-chemical licences depending on the product. Skip those that do not apply.

post_name: Member Secretary, Uttarakhand Environment Protection & Pollution Control Board (UEPPCB)
action: After construction and installation, obtain Consent to Operate (CTO) before starting production
time_limit: As notified under Uttarakhand Right to Service Act, 2011 (exact days not confirmed this session)
on_reject: Appeal to the Uttarakhand Appellate Authority under Water/Air Acts; then National Green Tribunal
note: CTO under Water Act Sec.25 / Air Act Sec.21 is distinct from the CTE taken at Step 3. CTE is not permission to run production - CTO is the final environmental go-live gate.

post_name: Designated Officer / Nodal Officer, Single Window Facilitation (Invest Uttarakhand) and Right to Service appellate authorities
action: Escalate any approval that exceeds its notified time limit through single-window then RTS appeal
on_reject: First appeal to the designated first appellate authority, then the Uttarakhand Right to Service Commission; ultimately a writ petition in the Uttarakhand High Court for unreasonable delay
note: Front the whole flow through the Invest Uttarakhand single-window portal. Delay remedy runs under the Uttarakhand Right to Service (Sewa Ka Adhikar) Act, 2011: designated officer -> first appellate authority -> RTS Commission (exact named authorities not confirmed this session).

action: Confirm whether family's name is already on the Gram Panchayat's PMAY-G Permanent Wait List (SECC/Awaas+).
on_reject: If name absent, proceed to Awaas+ 2024 self-survey (step 2) to seek fresh inclusion.
note: PWL is drawn from SECC 2011 deprivation data plus Awaas+ returns, displayed at Gram Sabha. Being on the list, not filing a form, is the gate. Check status at pmayg.nic.in.

post_name: Head of Family (self-survey applicant) / Awaas+ enumerator
action: Register the household via the AwaasPlus 2024 app: self-survey with Aadhaar OTP/face auth, or assisted survey by enumerator.
on_reject: If self-survey not possible (no smartphone), request assisted survey by the Panchayat enumerator/Sachiv.
note: Awaas+ 2024 survey (launched 17 Sept 2024; app self-survey from Jan 2025) enrols families left out of SECC 2011. Eligibility (Aug 2024): kachcha house of 0-2 rooms, household income <= Rs. 15,000/month, Aadhaar-seeded bank account, no prior housing benefit; two-wheeler/refrigerator no longer disqualify. Survey window is periodically extended - confirm current deadline locally.

post_name: Aggrieved Person / Complainant (or on her behalf)
action: Approach a Protection Officer, registered service provider (NGO), police, or the Magistrate directly.
note: Under s. 4/s. 12 PWDVA the aggrieved woman, or any person on her behalf, may initiate. No lawyer or fee is mandatory to begin.

post_name: Jansunwai (Samadhan) / Directorate of Local Bodies, UP
action: Lodge a state-level grievance escalating the unresolved municipal complaint.
note: jansunwai.up.nic.in; Directorate of Local Bodies, Lucknow (ph. 0522-2838128/29). Uttarakhand: Chief Minister Helpline 1905 / CM Helpline portal.

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate
action: Take cognizance and fix the first date of hearing within three days of receiving the application.
note: Jurisdiction fixed by s. 27; time limit u/s 12(4). The JMFC (in UP districts) sits within the district judiciary; despite the PO route the order is a court order.

post_name: Court / Magistrate (through Protection Officer or process server)
action: Issue notice of the date of hearing to the respondent and Protection Officer for service.
note: Notice served by the Protection Officer under Rule 12 within two days (or as directed); s. 13. Governed by CrPC procedure (s. 28).

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate
action: On urgency, grant an interim or ex-parte protection order on the first hearing.
note: Interim / ex-parte relief u/s 23 where prima facie domestic violence is shown, before hearing the respondent.

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate
action: Hold hearing; consider DIR, affidavits, and both parties; may direct counselling or welfare-expert assistance.
note: Magistrate may direct counselling (s. 14) or assistance of a welfare expert (s. 15); proceedings may be held in camera (s. 16).

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate
action: Pass the final Protection Order and any residence/monetary/custody/compensation orders; endeavour to dispose within 60 days.
note: Protection order u/s 18; associated orders ss. 19-22. Disposal endeavour u/s 12(5). Order remains in force till the aggrieved person applies for discharge (s. 25).

action: Supply certified copies of the order free of cost to parties, police in-charge, and Protection Officer.
note: Free copies to aggrieved person, respondent, PO and officer-in-charge of the police station within jurisdiction under s. 24.

action: Monitor compliance and assist enforcement of the protection order.
note: PO enforcement duties under s. 9 and Rules 8/10; PO acts under the Magistrate's control.

action: On complaint of breach, register and act on the cognizable, non-bailable offence and arrest respondent.
note: Breach of a protection order is an offence u/s 31 (up to 1 year imprisonment and/or fine) — cognizable and non-bailable; triable by the same Magistrate.

action: Hear appeal by either party aggrieved by the order, filed within thirty days.
note: Appeal to the Court of Session u/s 29 within 30 days from the date the order is served on the aggrieved person or respondent, whichever is later.

action: Capture four-side geo-tagged photos of the existing kachcha house and submit family, income, asset, and bank details.
on_reject: Poor GPS/photo failures require retaking geo-tagged photos before submission.
note: Form captures Aadhaar of head + all members, house specs, toilet status, income, land holding, Aadhaar-linked bank account. Applicant receives a registration/application number by SMS on submission.

action: Conduct field verification: fresh geo-tagged photos and cross-check of self-declared income, assets, and house condition.
on_reject: If details fail verification, applicant may correct/re-submit or raise the matter at Gram Sabha (step 6).
note: Tier-1 (Panchayat) verification, typically ~30-60 days. Data recorded in AwaasSoft MIS. Time limit is a programmatic target, not statutory.

action: Scrutinise Panchayat-endorsed list; run duplicate and automatic-exclusion checks against AwaasSoft MIS.
on_reject: Wrongful exclusion at block level can be contested at Gram Sabha (step 6) and escalated to Project Director, DRDA.
note: Tier-2 (Block) verification. BDO validates against the modified exclusion criteria before the district finalises.

action: Publicly present eligible list for objections; ratify additions/corrections by resolution and set priority ranking.
on_reject: An omitted-but-eligible family raises an appeal-against-exclusion here; the Gram Sabha resolution feeds back to Block/District.
note: Gram Sabha ratification is the mandated social-audit step. Automated priority scoring weights kachcha-house severity and SC/ST/widow/disabled/minority vulnerability. This is the key escalation route for genuinely eligible but omitted BPL families.

post_name: Project Director, District Rural Development Agency (DRDA)
action: Finalise the verified list and update the Permanent Wait List (PWL) on AwaasSoft MIS.
on_reject: Fund-release or finalisation delays are escalated to the CDO (Chief Development Officer), who heads the DRDA at district level.
note: Tier-3 (District) finalisation. DRDA is chaired by the CDO in UP; the Project Director runs day-to-day PMAY-G administration. Post title 'Project Director, DRDA' is the real UP designation (outside the supplied post list).

action: Generate the sanction order as funds reach the block and the family moves up the PWL; notify by SMS.
on_reject: If sanction is stuck despite PWL inclusion, escalate BDO -> Project Director DRDA -> PMAY-G helpline 1800-11-6446 / CPGRAMS / UP CM Helpline 1076.
note: This is the decisive approval: sanction authorises the first installment. Sanction depends on annual state target allocation, so an on-list family may wait for its turn in the priority queue.

action: Receive Installment 1 (~Rs. 30,000) via DBT and begin construction at foundation/plinth stage.
on_reject: Non-credit despite sanction: verify Aadhaar-bank seeding, then escalate via AwaasSoft grievance module / helpline.
note: Plain-area UP unit assistance is Rs. 1.20 lakh total, released in 4 installments (approx 30k/45k/30k/15k) tied to construction stages via DBT to the Aadhaar-linked account. Beneficiary is owner-builder. Installment split figures are indicative and may vary by state order.

action: Register on state police CCTNS e-FIR portal with mobile OTP; select unknown-accused case type
note: UP: cctnsup.gov.in/eFIR (linked from uppolice.gov.in); e-FIR restricted to cognizable cases with unknown accused, which covers vehicle theft and lost articles. Uttarakhand: analogous state CCTNS e-FIR / lost-article service.

action: Fill complaint form; upload ID, RC/chassis-engine no. (vehicle) or IMEI + bill (mobile); state place/time
note: Distinguish lost article report vs cognizable theft e-FIR. Vehicle theft is a cognizable offence (IPC 379 / BNS 303). Rough time 15-30 min. Lost article report auto-generates a downloadable acknowledgement immediately.

post_name: CCTNS e-FIR System / Station House Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Route e-FIR to jurisdictional police station; register electronically under BNSS s.173(1) proviso
note: BNSS s.173(1) proviso permits registration of information given electronically. Zero-FIR provision means jurisdiction is not a barrier at intake. e-FIR must be signed by the giver within 3 days.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Verify submission and formally register FIR; assign FIR number and investigating officer
time_limit: e-FIR sign window 3 days (BNSS s.173); verification typically 24-72 hrs
on_reject: If registration refused, escalate under BNSS s.173(4) to SP; or apply to Magistrate under s.175(3).
note: For vehicle theft, SHO or an assigned Investigating Officer (usually Sub-Inspector rank) verifies before formal FIR registration and number allotment.

action: Take up investigation; for vehicle, verify RC/insurance details and jurisdiction
note: Rank is typical, not statutorily fixed per state. Investigation follows BNSS provisions after registration.

action: Obtain duplicate SIM from telecom operator using the police report copy
note: CEIR requires a police report first and a duplicate SIM of the lost number. SMS on re-issued SIM enabled after 24 hrs.

action: Submit IMEI-blocking request on CEIR / Sanchar Saathi portal (ceir.gov.in) with report + ID
note: Purchase invoice optional. A Request ID is issued for tracking and future unblocking.

action: Block IMEI nationwide across all networks; phone unusable on any Indian network
note: Blocking does not prevent police tracking. Acts automatically via CEIR + operators once request accepted.

action: Download PDF acknowledgement / e-FIR copy with reference or FIR number
note: Used for insurance claim (vehicle), SIM re-issue, and new-phone verification.

action: For untraced vehicle, file untraced/final report enabling insurance settlement
note: Untraced-vehicle report timing is portal/state practice, not a universal statutory figure.

action: On refusal to register a cognizable offence, direct registration/investigation
note: BNSS s.173(4): SP route on refusal (successor to CrPC s.154(3)). Magistrate under BNSS s.175(3) (successor to CrPC s.156(3)). Also state police grievance portal / 112 helpline.

action: Verify each construction milestone via geo-tagged AwaasApp photo (lintel, roof-cast) to unlock the next installment.
on_reject: If a completed stage is not verified/photo not uploaded, escalate to BDO then Project Director, DRDA.
note: Installments 2-4 release only after stage verification. Milestone photo upload to AwaasSoft is the trigger; delays here are the most common practical bottleneck.

action: Complete the house; claim ~90-95 days MGNREGA wage labour and Rs. 12,000 SBM-G toilet grant via convergence.
on_reject: MGNREGA wage or toilet-grant denial: raise with Panchayat Sachiv/BDO; MGNREGA has its own grievance and social-audit channel.
note: Convergence: 90 unskilled MGNREGA person-days (95 in hilly areas) to the household head for self-construction, paid separately at state wage; SBM-G toilet grant Rs. 12,000 by separate DBT on completion. Person-day/rupee figures per MoRD convergence norms.

post_name: Project Director, DRDA / CPGRAMS / UP CM Helpline (1076)
action: Escalate any stalled stage (no name on PWL, sanction delay, unpaid installment) up the grievance ladder.
note: Ladder: Panchayat Sachiv -> BDO -> Project Director DRDA -> State RD. Cross-cutting: AwaasSoft grievance module, PMAY-G helpline 1800-11-6446 (8am-8pm Mon-Sat), CPGRAMS (pgportal.gov.in), UP CM Helpline 1076. BPL cardholders may file RTI free under RTI Act 2005 s.6(1) for file-movement/fund-release records.

action: Inspect the overflowing drain; confirm stormwater-drain vs sewer jurisdiction.
note: Corporation Engineering wing handles stormwater/nala de-silting; a separate Jal Sansthan/sewerage board may handle trunk sewers in some cities.

action: Assign crews: safai gang lifts garbage, de-silting gang clears the drain.
on_reject: If not resolved in the charter window, escalate (first appeal) to the Zonal Officer.
note: Stage-1 owner in the e-NagarSewa escalation matrix. Charter SLAs: 24 hrs drain/road cleaning, 1 day garbage pickup/disposal.

action: Flag persistent non-collection politically to push the department.
note: Elected representative; parallel political lever, not a statutory approver. Optional but effective.

action: Re-open the unresolved ticket as first appeal; direct field action.
on_reject: If still unresolved, escalate to City Health Officer / Additional Municipal Commissioner.
note: Stage-2 authority in the e-NagarSewa three-stage escalation.

post_name: Nagar Swasthya Adhikari (City Health Officer) / Additional Municipal Commissioner (Apar Nagar Ayukt)
action: Take up the final internal appeal; order compliance and fix accountability.
on_reject: If unresolved, escalate to the Municipal Commissioner / public grievance cell.
note: Stage-3 authority in the e-NagarSewa escalation matrix.

action: Direct resolution through the corporation's public grievance cell.
on_reject: If still unresolved, escalate to the state portal (Jansunwai / Samadhan).
note: Administrative head of the Nagar Nigam. In smaller towns the counterpart is the Adhishasi Adhikari (Executive Officer) of the Nagar Palika/Panchayat.

post_name: Superintendent of Police (SP) / Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP)
action: If satisfied a cognizable offence is disclosed, investigate personally or direct an officer to register and investigate.
on_reject: If SP declines, move the Judicial Magistrate under BNSS S.175(3) (Step 6).
note: BNSS S.173(4): on being satisfied that a cognizable offence is disclosed, the SP shall either investigate the case or direct a subordinate to do so, which includes registering the FIR.

action: File a written application before the jurisdictional Magistrate to order police to register the FIR and investigate.
on_reject: If application is not entertained, file a private complaint under BNSS S.223 (Step 8) or a High Court writ.
note: BNSS S.175(3): a Magistrate empowered under S.210 may, after enquiry and considering the S.173(4) submission to the SP, order investigation - i.e. direct registration of the FIR. This is the core court remedy; office class = district court. Designation is Judicial Magistrate First Class (not in the standard revenue-post list).

action: Order the officer in charge to register the FIR and investigate; require an action-taken report.
note: Under BNSS S.175(3) the Magistrate directs the police to register and investigate; this compels the refusing station to act.

action: Alternatively, take the matter as a private complaint - record complainant and witness statements and proceed.
note: BNSS S.223 (formerly CrPC S.200): the Magistrate may take cognizance of the offence on complaint, examine the complainant on oath, and proceed without police - an alternative route if S.175(3) registration is not sought.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Parallel option: file e-FIR / online complaint via UP Police CCTNS citizen portal or dial 112.
on_reject: If the online portal only logs a 'complaint' (not an FIR), still pursue Steps 1-7.
note: UP Police CCTNS Citizen Portal (cctnsup.gov.in) offers e-FIR for specified categories (e.g. unknown-accused / vehicle theft) and complaint registration; emergency number is 112. e-FIR availability and whether it counts as a formal FIR varies by category and state - not a substitute for the statutory route above.

post_name: Superintendent of Police (SP) / Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP)
action: For misconduct by the refusing officer, complain to Police Complaints Authority / SHRC / Jansunwai (IGRS).
on_reject: High Court writ (mandamus) as last resort to compel registration.
note: Refusal to register an FIR for a cognizable offence is itself an actionable dereliction. UP grievance route: Jansunwai/IGRS portal; State Human Rights Commission; State Police Complaints Authority. Designation for oversight body is outside the standard revenue-post list.

post_name: Circle Officer / Assistant Commissioner of Police (CO/ACP)
action: On delay or dispute, escalate with the reference number to the sub-divisional police officer.
note: First escalation tier above the police station (CO in districts / ACP in commissionerates).

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC), jurisdictional court
action: File an affidavit-supported application asking the Magistrate to direct police to register and investigate
on_reject: If the Magistrate declines, pursue a private complaint under s.223 (step 8) or revision/High Court under Article 226/482
note: s.175(3) BNSS: the Magistrate empowered under s.210 may, after considering the affidavit under s.173(4) and the police's submission on their refusal, order investigation. Attach the SHO complaint, the SP (s.173(4)) complaint and proof of both (Priyanka Srivastava v. State of U.P. (2015) requires the supporting affidavit). Exhausting the SP remedy is a precondition.

action: Consider the application and police submission and decide whether to order FIR registration and investigation
on_reject: Criminal revision, or writ under Article 226 / s.528 BNSS (High Court inherent power)
note: This is the decisive step of the escalation: under s.175(3) the Magistrate must now also weigh the police's explanation for refusal before directing investigation. An order here compels the station to register the FIR and investigate.

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) — private complaint bench
action: As an alternative, file a private complaint; Magistrate examines complainant on oath and may take cognizance directly
on_reject: Dismissal is appealable/revisable; can be pursued alongside the s.175(3) route
note: s.223 BNSS (successor to s.200 CrPC): the Magistrate examines the complainant and witnesses on oath and may take cognizance directly, bypassing the police entirely. New proviso to s.223(1): the proposed accused must be given an opportunity of being heard before cognizance. Distinct from the s.175(3) direct-to-police route.

post_name: Director General of Police (DGP) office / UP Police online grievance portal (UPCOP / e-FIR cell)
action: In parallel, lodge an online/e-FIR or written grievance for eligible offence types
on_reject: Portal non-action feeds the Janhit Guarantee appeal (step 5) and the SP complaint (step 4)
note: s.173(1) BNSS recognises information by electronic communication, valid once signed within 3 days. UP Police run online reporting (UPCOP/e-FIR) but scope is generally limited offence types (e.g. vehicle/property theft, cyber crime), not all serious bodily offences — verify offence-eligibility on uppolice.gov.in. A parallel channel, not a substitute for the s.173(4)/s.175(3) chain.

action: Where refusal involves a rights violation or police misconduct, file a separate complaint of police inaction
on_reject: Independent forum; does not compel FIR registration but records misconduct
note: A real but adjunct route for police inaction implicating rights; it addresses misconduct rather than compelling registration, which remains the function of s.175(3). Use alongside, not instead of, the core chain.

action: Register on NSP or state portal; complete One-Time Registration (OTR) / KYC with Aadhaar
note: Entry point: National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in) or state portal (UP: scholarship.up.gov.in). OTR de-duplicates and Aadhaar-authenticates the applicant. Renewals log in instead of re-registering.

action: Fill scholarship form; upload income, caste/category or EWS certificate, marksheet, fee receipt, bank passbook
note: Bank account must be in the applicant's own name and Aadhaar-seeded (DBT-enabled). Category routing differs: SC and OBC often under different schemes/departments than EWS; confirm the correct scheme.

action: Review FSO and Food Analyst reports; decide enforcement route (notice, adjudication, or prosecution)
note: DO sanctions prosecution under FSSA 2006 s.42; substandard/misbranding cases go to civil adjudication, unsafe-food cases to court.

action: Verify enrolment, course, fees and documents at institute level (Level 1)
on_reject: Returns as 'defective' to applicant with query for correction and resubmission
note: First verification tier on NSP. Nothing progresses until the institute forwards/verifies the application.

post_name: District Social Welfare Officer (SC) / District Backward Classes Welfare Officer (OBC)
action: Second-level (district) verification of eligibility, certificates and institute forwarding
on_reject: Sends back to institute/applicant as defective for correction
note: District verifying officer designation depends on category and state (Social Welfare Officer for SC; Backward Classes / Pichhara Varg Welfare Officer for OBC; Minority Welfare Officer for minority-EWS variants).

post_name: Deputy Director / Assistant Director, District Social Welfare (as delegated)
action: Cross-check district merit/quota list and consolidate verified applications for the state
note: Intermediate district-level consolidation before state sanction; delegation varies by state and category.

post_name: Director / Secretary, Social Welfare (or Backward Classes Welfare) Department
action: Sanction the scholarship at state level (Level 3) and pass for payment
on_reject: Application rejected/returned with reason; applicant may re-apply in a later window or grieve
note: The secretariat department (Social Welfare / Backward Classes Welfare) is the sanctioning authority. This is the decisive approval step.

action: Generate DBT payment (Fund Transfer Order) via PFMS to Aadhaar-linked account
on_reject: Payment fails on account/Aadhaar-seeding mismatch; returned for correction
note: Disbursement is Direct Benefit Transfer routed through PFMS (pfms.nic.in). Most 'sanctioned but unpaid' delay sits here.

action: Track status on portal (Know Your Status) and payment on PFMS; confirm bank credit
note: Use application ID for portal status; PFMS 'Know Your Payment' with bank/reference number; bank SMS/passbook confirms final credit.

post_name: NSP / State Portal Helpdesk; then Social Welfare Dept grievance cell / CM Helpline (1076)
action: Escalate stalled or unpaid application at the blocking level (institute/district/state)
note: First identify the stuck level via status. Portal helpdesk for technical/OTP; District then State welfare grievance cell; Uttarakhand SW helpline 1800-180-4236; CM Helpline 1076 for unresolved cases.

post_name: Designated Officer / Appellate Authority under Right-to-Service Act
action: Invoke the statutory time-guarantee if the service is a notified Right-to-Service item.
note: UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 / Uttarakhand Right to Service Act 2011 penalize designated officers for missing notified deadlines. Applies only to services actually notified in each state's schedule; sanitation-specific notification varies by city, so treat as conditional.

post_name: Superintendent of Police / Commissioner of Police (SP/CP)
action: Final district escalation; also address via state police public-grievance portal or helpline.
note: District SP (or CP in commissionerate cities) heads the police grievance chain. The District Magistrate/collectorate issues the underlying BNSS §163 verification order but does not process individual files.

post_name: Regional/Deputy Transport Commissioner then State Transport Commissioner
action: Escalate delay/refusal; then grievance via UP CM Helpline (1076) / Parivahan grievance
on_reject: Persistent inaction challengeable in writ before the High Court.
note: Administrative appeal lies with the Transport Commissioner; service also covered by UP Right-to-Public-Services grievance channels.

post_name: Registrar of Births & Deaths (Municipality / Gram Panchayat via Panchayat Secretary)
action: Register husband's death and issue the death certificate, the core prerequisite document.
time_limit: Certificate issued within notified days once registration is complete (per Registration of Births & Deaths Act, 1969; state RTS schedule).
on_reject: Appeal to the District Registrar (Births & Deaths); invoke U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam appeal if time limit breached.
note: Death within 21 days is free registration; late registration needs an order. This certificate is mandatory and most confident item.

action: Receive the application, order field verification of widow status, residence and income.
on_reject: Applicant notified; re-verification or correction; escalate to District Probation Officer.
note: Rural applications route through the BDO, urban through the SDM. Grounded in SSPY process pages.

action: Gather evidence: bill, packaging with batch/expiry, photos, FBO name/address, symptoms
note: Evidence strengthens sampling and any prosecution under FSSA 2006. Batch/lot and expiry are key for expired-product claims.

action: Lodge complaint via Food Safety Connect portal/app, national helpline 1800-112-100, or district FSDA office
note: FSSAI Food Safety Connect (foscos.fssai.gov.in/consumergrievance) routes to the State/UT Food Safety Commissioner; helpline 1800-112-100. Anonymous complaints accepted but limit follow-up.

post_name: Food Safety Connect / State Grievance Cell
action: Register complaint, issue reference number, route to concerned district Designated Officer
note: Complaint is triaged and forwarded to the district under the State Food Safety Commissioner. Reference number enables tracking.

action: Assess complaint and assign a Food Safety Officer to inspect the FBO
note: Under FSSA 2006 s.36/37 one Designated Officer per district oversees licensing and enforcement; in UP/UK this sits within the district health/CMO administration (FSDA wing).

action: Draw food samples in four parts, seal, and pay/tender the FBO where adulteration suspected
note: Sampling procedure under FSSA 2006 s.47 and FSS Rules 2011; one part to Food Analyst, others retained for the Designated Officer / possible re-analysis.

action: Analyse the sample and issue a report on adulteration/substandard/unsafe status
note: Analysis at a laboratory recognised under FSSA 2006 s.43; Food Analyst report under s.46 is the evidentiary basis for action.

action: Track FIR/complaint status online using the reference or FIR number.
note: Status tracking via portal/UP-COP app.

action: Adjudicate civil penalty for misbranding/substandard/unsafe food and impose fine
note: Adjudication of penalties under FSSA 2006 ss.68-70 by an officer not below Additional District Magistrate; serious unsafe-food offences go to the designated court.

action: Communicate outcome and enforcement action to the complainant against the reference number
note: Outcome (penalty, licence suspension/cancellation, closure, or closure of complaint) is recorded on the grievance portal.

action: Escalate here if no acknowledgement or action; then approach State Consumer Commission / FSSAI
note: Grievance escalation under FSSA 2006 s.89; packaged-product/expired-goods matters may also go to the consumer helpline (1915) or a Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.

action: Confirm SC caste certificate, current admission, and family income below Rs 2,50,000/year before applying
note: SC/ST income ceiling is Rs 2,50,000/year; student must be a UP resident enrolled in a recognized post-matric (Class 11 onward, incl. college) course. Outside not-official designation: the citizen, noted as such.

action: Generate mandatory One-Time Registration (OTR) on scholarship.up.gov.in using Aadhaar e-KYC
on_reject: Correct Aadhaar name/DOB mismatch and redo e-KYC; update Aadhaar-linked mobile via NPCI if needed
note: OTR (14-digit ID) is mandatory for fresh and renewal applicants from 2025-26; requires Aadhaar-linked mobile. Portal is UP's Samaj Kalyan (Social Welfare) department channel, not NSP for in-state UP applicants.

action: Seed the student's own bank account to Aadhaar via NPCI for DBT before final submission
on_reject: Re-seed the correct account with the bank/NPCI; a wrong or unseeded account blocks disbursal
note: Disbursal is DBT through PFMS to the student's Aadhaar-seeded account, so NPCI seeding is a hard prerequisite.

action: File the post-matric (Dashmottar) application online within the announced window and upload documents
time_limit: Annual window (~2 weeks); e.g. 2026-27 fresh Class 11-12 window announced 11-25 Aug 2026
on_reject: Portal rejects mismatched marksheet/Aadhaar details; correct and resubmit within the window
note: Documents: SC caste certificate, income certificate, previous marksheet, admission/fee proof, Aadhaar, bank details. Name/DOB must match the High School certificate exactly or the application is rejected.

action: Print the submitted form and hand the signed hard copy plus documents to the institution
note: Physical submission to the college is required; the online form alone does not advance the application.

action: Verify enrollment, attendance and fees online and forward the application to the district
on_reject: If status stays 'Pending at Institute', escalate to the institution's nodal scholarship officer
note: Mandatory gate; unverified applications do not proceed. Status: Verified by Institute. Real designation: institution nodal/scholarship officer (outside the listed post set).

post_name: District Social Welfare Officer (Jila Samaj Kalyan Adhikari)
action: Scrutinize the forwarded application at district level and verify eligibility and documents
on_reject: Objection returned to student/institution for correction; contact the District Welfare Officer to resolve
note: District Social Welfare Officer / District Welfare Officer (DWO) is the district-level verifying authority. Status: Verified by District. Real designation (outside the listed rural/revenue post set).

post_name: Director, Social Welfare (SC Welfare Directorate, Samaj Kalyan Nirdeshalaya)
action: Scrutinize district-verified cases at state level and sanction the scholarship
on_reject: Appeal/representation to the Social Welfare Directorate; NSP/portal technical issues via the grievance module
note: State Social Welfare Directorate under the Secretariat's Social Welfare department is the sanctioning authority (Status: Verified by State -> Approved). This is the decisive approval step.

action: Release maintenance allowance and reimbursed fees by DBT to the student's account
on_reject: Failed credit (account/NPCI error) is flagged for re-seeding and reprocessing
note: Payment processed by DBT through PFMS. Maintenance goes to the student; compulsory-fee reimbursement follows the scheme's fee rules. Status: Payment Processed.

action: Open uppolice.gov.in citizen services or UP-COP app; register/log in via mobile number and OTP.
note: One-time account creation. Portal reachability and exact app version not live-verified.

action: Select correct service: e-FIR (vehicle theft / unknown-accused property theft) or online complaint for other offences.
note: Self-service e-FIR is limited to notified categories; wrong menu choice is the main failure point. Menu labels not verified.

action: Enter incident details, vehicle/document numbers, attach documents; submit and receive acknowledgement/reference number.
note: Reference number issued immediately in same session.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Receive the e-FIR/complaint routed to jurisdictional police station; verify particulars against records.
on_reject: For an ineligible offence, complainant is directed to the station or the complaint proceeds as a report; escalation under step 8+ applies if registration refused.
note: e-FIR verification commonly targeted within 24-72 hours for vehicle theft; exact SLA not verified.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Register the FIR under relevant BNS sections and assign FIR number for an eligible cognizable offence.
on_reject: If SHO refuses a cognizable-offence FIR, escalate to Superintendent under Sec. 173(4) BNSS and Magistrate under Sec. 175(3) BNSS.
note: Registration is mandatory for cognizable offences per Sec. 173 BNSS and Lalita Kumari (2014); the officer registers, not exercises discretion to refuse.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Assign an investigating officer and commence investigation.
note: Investigation follows registration under BNSS Chapter XIII.

action: Download/receive a free copy of the registered FIR from the portal or station.
note: Free FIR copy is the complainant's right under Sec. 173 BNSS.

post_name: Superintendent of Police / Senior Superintendent of Police (SP/SSP)
action: On non-registration, send written complaint to SP under Sec. 173(4) BNSS; SP may order registration/investigation.
on_reject: If SP does not act, approach the Magistrate under Sec. 175(3) BNSS.
note: Sec. 173(4) BNSS (formerly Sec. 154(3) CrPC). Circle Officer (CO)/DCP is an intermediate written-grievance option.

action: Approach Magistrate under Sec. 175(3) BNSS to direct police to register and investigate.
note: Sec. 175(3) BNSS (formerly Sec. 156(3) CrPC). Parallel routes: UP Jansunwai/IGRS, 112 emergency, 1090 women helpline.

action: If stalled, escalate through institute nodal officer, then DWO, then Directorate, then portal grievance
note: Escalation ladder: (1) institution nodal officer, (2) District Social Welfare Officer, (3) state Social Welfare Directorate, (4) portal/NSP grievance module and Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment grievance.

action: Submit written TC application to the school Head, giving child's name, class, admission no., destination.
note: Plain written request or the school's TC application form. For RTE-age children the school cannot demand the TC be routed through the receiving school; a direct request to the Head suffices.

post_name: Head Teacher / Principal (Pradhanadhyapak / Prabhari) of the school
action: Receive and acknowledge the application; record it in the school inward register.
note: The Head is the issuing authority for a routine TC; no higher office is needed for a normal transfer. Ask for a dated acknowledgement.

action: Run no-dues / property check: library books, ID card, any dues (usually nil in free govt schools).
on_reject: Clear the pending item, then re-request; withholding TC for dues cannot delay the child's admission elsewhere (RTE s.5(3)).
note: Government elementary schooling is free (RTE s.3), so dues are typically nil; the no-dues gate is structural, not financial.

action: Prepare the TC from the scholar/admission register: name, DOB, admission & leaving dates, class, conduct.
note: Accuracy depends on the admission register; small schools may have no clerk, in which case the Head fills the form directly.

action: Sign the TC and apply the school seal — the act of issuance; deliver to the parent.
time_limit: RTE-age (Class 1-8): immediately (RTE s.5). Higher classes: ~3-7 working days (administrative norm).
on_reject: If refused/delayed, escalate to the Block Education Officer (Khand Shiksha Adhikari) — step 7.
note: This is the decision that grants the request. For an RTE-age child the Head is statutorily bound to issue it immediately and free; delay is a disciplinary lapse (RTE s.5).

post_name: Block Education Officer (Khand Shiksha Adhikari, BEO) — for inter-district / inter-state moves only
action: Countersign / validate the TC where required for out-of-district or out-of-state transfer.
note: Countersignature is not needed for a local move; it is commonly required only for inter-district/inter-state transfers or for record migration. Real UP designation: Khand Shiksha Adhikari (BEO).

action: Verify the TC against records (may seek confirmation from issuing school), then admit the child.
on_reject: For an RTE-age child, admission cannot be denied/delayed for want of a TC (RTE s.5(3)); insist on provisional admission and file a grievance if refused.
note: RTE s.5(3) bars using absence/delay of a TC to deny or delay a child's admission.

post_name: Block Education Officer (Khand Shiksha Adhikari, BEO)
action: Escalation 1: written complaint; BEO directs the school Head to issue the TC.
on_reject: Escalate to the Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA / District Basic Education Officer) — step 9.
note: First administrative escalation if the Head refuses or delays. In UP the block-level officer is the Khand Shiksha Adhikari.

post_name: Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA) / District Basic Education Officer
action: Escalation 2: district-level order directing issuance; can initiate disciplinary action against the Head.
on_reject: File a grievance on the state portal (UP IGRS / CM Helpline 1076; Uttarakhand CM Helpline 1905 / Sewa Ka Adhikar appeal) or approach the Right to Service appellate authority.
note: District head of Basic Education in UP. For secondary schools the parallel office is the District Inspector of Schools (DIOS). Delay in issuing TC is a service lapse actionable here under RTE s.5.

action: Log complaint on official channel with location, ward, photo; note the ticket ID
note: Channels: municipal sanitation helpline/app, national Swachhata app, jansunwai.up.nic.in (UP) or CM Helpline 1905 / Sewa portal (Uttarakhand), or written application at the ward office. The ticket ID is what enables tracking and escalation.

action: Register the complaint, generate ticket ID, route to the concerned ward/zone sanitation wing
note: The corporation grievance cell / call centre records and forwards the ticket; auto-routing on the app or jansunwai portal performs this step electronically.

action: Inspect the reported spot, confirm garbage / choked drain / unclean area and its scale
on_reject: Complaint marked non-actionable/duplicate with reason; citizen may re-open or escalate to the Health Officer
note: The Sanitary Inspector is the ground-level sanitation authority under SWM Rules 2016; naming varies (Sanitary Inspector / Chief Sanitary Inspector / Health Assistant) by city.

action: Dispatch safai karmchari crew or contracted agency to lift garbage / clear drain / clean area
note: Routine work is dispatched directly without senior approval; this is the operative decision that resolves most complaints.

post_name: Ward Health Officer / Zonal Health Officer
action: Sanction machinery, extra crew, or dump-site clearance for larger jobs beyond routine crew
on_reject: Job deferred/queued; citizen escalates to Zonal or Deputy Commissioner (Health)
note: Only for non-routine work (chronically blocked drain needing suction machine, dump-site to be cleared, engineering-wing involvement). Designation varies: Health Officer / Chief Medical & Health Officer of the corporation.

action: Carry out the lifting, drain clearing, or cleaning at the reported location
note: Execution on ground; for garbage/spot-cleaning commonly within 1-3 days of a logged ticket, drain clearing a few days to ~2 weeks by severity.

action: Verify completion, upload after-photo, mark the ticket resolved
on_reject: Ticket kept open; citizen can reject the closure on the app/portal and it reopens for re-action
note: Swachhata app and jansunwai allow the citizen to rate/close; a citizen rejection reopens the complaint.

action: Follow up quoting ticket ID after the promised window; reject closure if not actually done
note: Re-open on the same ticket rather than filing fresh, so the escalation clock and audit trail stay attached.

action: Escalate the stalled ticket; corporator's office pushes the department to act
note: The elected ward councillor is the political representative and can move stalled complaints; not a statutory decider but an effective escalation lever.

action: Review the escalated complaint and direct the ward wing to resolve
on_reject: Escalate to the Municipal Commissioner's public-grievance cell
note: Escalation chain: Sanitary Inspector to Health Officer to Zonal/Deputy Commissioner (Health) to Municipal Commissioner. Designation naming varies by corporation.

action: Take up unresolved grievance via the commissioner's public-grievance cell and order compliance
on_reject: Pursue statutory Right-to-Service appeal (step 12) or state grievance portal
note: Head of the corporation administration; the commissioner's grievance cell is the internal apex for sanitation complaints.

post_name: First Appellate Authority (under UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam / Uttarakhand Right to Service Act)
action: Hear appeal where a notified time-bound sanitation service was not delivered; direct action and may impose penalty
on_reject: File second appeal before the Second Appellate Authority under the same Act
note: Applies only where the specific service is notified under the state Right-to-Service schedule with a fixed window; the Act provides designated officer, first and second appellate authority and penalty for default. Confirm your service is on the notified schedule.

action: Issue caste (SC/ST/OBC) certificate and family income certificate for the applicant family.
on_reject: Apply to Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) / District Magistrate for review of certificate refusal.
note: Prerequisite documents. Income certificate must be within the scheme ceiling; caste certificate must match the claimed category. Both are Tehsildar/SDM-issued via e-district.

action: Complete One-Time Registration and create login on the correct portal (NSP or state).
on_reject: Correct registration details or reset via portal helpdesk.
note: Uttarakhand: National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in) with NSP OTR. Uttar Pradesh: state portal scholarship.up.gov.in registration. Confirm which portal applies for the child's category and class band before proceeding.

action: Fill scholarship form, select scheme, upload caste/income/bonafide/marksheet and bank/Aadhaar details.
on_reject: Re-open draft within the application window and resubmit corrected form/documents.
note: Class band determines the sub-scheme (pre-matric usually classes I-VIII or IX-X depending on scheme). Bank account should be student/guardian Aadhaar-seeded for DBT.

action: Verify enrollment, class and application details; forward (Level-1 institute verification).
on_reject: School returns application to applicant for correction; escalate to District Social Welfare Officer if wrongly held.
note: Mandatory institute-level (L1) gate on NSP; application cannot proceed without school forwarding. School confirms bonafide status and that the student is on rolls.

post_name: District Social Welfare Officer (Jila Samaj Kalyan Adhikari) / District Backward Classes Welfare Officer
action: Verify caste/income eligibility and documents at district level (Level-2 verification).
on_reject: Application returned with reason; applicant corrects and resubmits, or represents to the officer/District Magistrate.
note: District welfare office checks scheme eligibility and certificate validity. SC handled by Social Welfare, OBC/EBC by Backward Classes Welfare, ST by Tribal Welfare where a separate directorate exists (varies by state).

post_name: State Directorate of Social Welfare / State Nodal Officer
action: Sanction the scholarship at state level (Level-3 verification) after budget/quota check.
on_reject: State-level rejection is communicated on portal with reason; grievance to State Nodal Officer, then Secretary/Director, Social Welfare.
note: This is the deciding step: the state directorate finalizes sanction against the centrally-sponsored scheme allocation. This is where the request is granted or refused.

action: Gather evidence: FBO name/address, bill, wrapper, retained food sample, photos, date and time.
note: Physical sample and bill materially support later formal sampling and any Section 40 self-analysis right.

action: Lodge complaint on FSSAI Food Safety Connect portal or app; receive unique concern number.
note: foscos.fssai.gov.in/consumergrievance or the Food Safety Connect mobile app; routes to state Designated Officer/FSO. Concern number enables tracking.

action: Receive and register complaint; assign it to the jurisdictional Food Safety Officer for action.
on_reject: Escalate to Commissioner of Food Safety, Uttar Pradesh (FSDA HQ).
note: DO heads district food-safety administration under the state Commissioner of Food Safety; the district-health office the citizen resolves to.

action: Inspect the shop/restaurant premises and verify the complaint on the ground.
note: FSO is the frontline enforcement officer under Section 38, FSS Act, 2006.

action: Lift a food sample under prescribed procedure; divide into parts and seal per Section 47.
note: Sampling and division of sample under Sections 41-47, FSS Act and Rule 2.4, FSS Rules, 2011; one part sent to Food Analyst.

post_name: Food Analyst, notified food laboratory (FSDA lab)
action: Analyse the sample and issue a report on whether food is substandard, misbranded, or unsafe.
on_reject: Analyst informs DO and Commissioner with reasons if 14-day window cannot be met.
note: Rule 2.4 (FSS Rules 2011): analysis within 14 days. Allahabad HC (Kewal Dairy v. State of UP, 2024) treats analyst-report date as the date of offence.

action: Review Food Analyst report; decide whether to adjudicate, prosecute, or drop.
on_reject: FBO/complainant may seek re-analysis by referral to the Central Food Laboratory under Section 46.
note: DO decides the enforcement route on the analyst report; sanction/consent to prosecute rests with DO under the FSS Act.

action: Adjudicate lesser offences (substandard, misbranded) and impose monetary penalty.
on_reject: Appeal to the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal under Section 70, FSS Act.
note: Adjudication of penalties under Section 68, FSS Act, 2006; Adjudicating Officer is of ADM rank (state-notified).

action: Try serious offences (unsafe food, injurious adulteration) on prosecution filed by the DO.
on_reject: Appeal to the High Court per the criminal-appeal procedure.
note: Serious offences under Sections 48-59 tried by Special Court under Section 69/section on special courts; prosecution requires DO consent.

post_name: Commissioner of Food Safety, Uttar Pradesh (FSDA)
action: On inaction, escalate; Commissioner supervises DO/FSO and may direct action or transfer.
on_reject: Further escalation to FSSAI central grievance mechanism; District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission for compensation; RTI on action taken.
note: Commissioner of Food Safety is the state head under Section 30, FSS Act; parallel consumer-forum and RTI routes available.

post_name: State Directorate of Social Welfare (Treasury / DBT)
action: Release sanctioned amount via Direct Benefit Transfer to the Aadhaar-linked bank account.
on_reject: If DBT fails (account/Aadhaar mismatch), correct bank/Aadhaar seeding and re-trigger payment via portal/PFMS grievance.
note: Disbursement is via DBT/PFMS. Pre-matric covers a maintenance allowance and, per scheme, book/tuition components. Payment failures are usually Aadhaar-seeding issues, not re-sanction.

post_name: State Nodal Officer / Portal Grievance Helpdesk
action: Escalate stalled, wrongly-rejected, or technical cases through the portal grievance module.
on_reject: Written grievance to Secretary/Director, Social Welfare Department; state public-grievance system (e.g. UP Jansunwai / CM Helpline) and central CPGRAMS.
note: First chase the level where it is stuck (school for L1, District Officer for L2). NSP has a state nodal officer and grievance/helpdesk; state portals have equivalents. Uttarakhand helpline 1800-180-4236.

post_name: Right to Service Appellate Authority / State Grievance (IGRS / CM Helpline / RTE grievance officer)
action: Escalation 3: formal grievance/appeal compelling issuance and penalising delay.
note: UP: Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam appellate route / IGRS jansunwai / CM Helpline 1076. Uttarakhand: Right to Service Act, 2011 appellate authority / CM Helpline 1905. RTE grievance also lies with the Block/District Grievance Redressal.

action: File felling application with ownership proof, revenue record, site sketch, species and count
note: Submit to the notified Tree Officer via the Revenue office (Tehsil) or e-District portal; where the state assigns felling to Forest, submit to the territorial Forest Range Office.

action: Register application, check documents complete, issue receipt/acknowledgement number
on_reject: Return for missing documents (ownership proof, khasra, site sketch) before registration.
note: Front-desk completeness check at the Tehsil/Range office or e-District intake.

action: Verify land ownership and that trees stand on private non-forest land against revenue records
on_reject: If ownership unclear or land is forest/community land, application stalls pending resolution.
note: Revenue field verification of title and land classification; most common source of delay.

action: Inspect site; confirm tree species, count, girth; classify as exempt or regulated
note: Species classification is the key branch: notified exempt species (e.g. eucalyptus, poplar, agroforestry species) need no permission; scheduled/protected species are tightly regulated.

action: If species is on the exempted list, issue exemption confirmation - no felling permission required
on_reject: If species is not exempt, route to Tree Officer for regulated-felling decision (step 6).
note: Exempt-species branch terminates here for felling; a transit pass may still be needed to move timber (step 8).

post_name: Tree Officer (notified Revenue officer - SDM / Tehsildar tier)
action: Examine verification and inspection reports; decide grant or refusal of felling permission
on_reject: Refusal must state reasons; applicant may appeal to the prescribed appellate authority (step 9).
note: Under the U.P. Protection of Trees Act 1976 the Tree Officer is the competent authority for felling on non-forest land; exact notified designation varies by district.

post_name: Tree Officer (notified Revenue officer - SDM / Tehsildar tier)
action: Sign and issue the felling permission order specifying trees and conditions
note: Permission typically conditional (number of trees, replanting condition where imposed).

action: Identify which PCC is needed: Passport-route for visa/immigration, or state route for domestic job.
note: Visa/immigration and overseas employment require the MEA/RPO-issued PCC in a specific format; a domestic employer usually accepts the state e-district Character Certificate. Confirm the requesting authority's exact requirement first.

action: Apply online: Passport Seva Portal for PCC, or UP/Uttarakhand e-district portal for Character Certificate.
note: Passport route: register on passportindia.gov.in, select 'Police Clearance Certificate', fill form. State route: apply on edistrict.up.gov.in / edistrict.uk.gov.in for the Character Certificate service.

action: Scrutinize application, check documents complete, issue acknowledgement/receipt number
on_reject: Return to applicant with deficiency memo to cure documents
note: Application forwarded into the supply office workflow; acknowledgement number is the status-tracking key

action: Pay the prescribed fee online and, for the passport route, book a Passport Seva Kendra appointment.
note: MEA PCC fee is a fixed statutory fee paid on the portal; state e-district charges a small notified service fee. Upload address proof, ID, passport (passport route), and photograph.

post_name: Passport Seva Kendra Officer (Regional Passport Office / MEA)
action: Verify documents and capture biometrics at the Passport Seva Kendra (passport route only).
on_reject: Deficient documents sent back to applicant for correction/resubmission.
note: Document check by Granting, Verification and Printing counters. For the state route this step is a dealing-clerk document scrutiny at the tehsil/police office instead.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (District Police / SP Office)
action: Route the verification request to the police station covering the applicant's address.
