note: Application/verification request forwarded from the Regional Passport Office (or e-district) to the jurisdictional District Superintendent of Police, then to the local Station House Officer.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Assign the address verification to the beat officer / local investigating staff.
note: The SHO of the police station having territorial jurisdiction over the applicant's residence is responsible for the character/antecedent verification.

post_name: Beat Constable / Sub-Inspector (Local Police, verification staff)
action: Physically verify identity and residence and check local records for any criminal antecedents.
on_reject: Adverse antecedents recorded and reported; may lead to refusal/hold of the certificate.
note: Field verification at the stated address plus a records check for any FIR/case against the applicant.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Compile and sign the verification report and forward it up the chain.
note: SHO certifies the field report ('no adverse record found' / details of any record) and returns it to the SP office / passport office.

post_name: Superintendent of Police / Senior Superintendent of Police (SP/SSP, District)
action: Review the police verification report and, for the state route, approve issuance of the Character Certificate.
on_reject: Adverse report; certificate refused or held with reasons; applicant may represent/appeal.
note: For the state e-district Character Certificate the SP/SSP office is the deciding/issuing authority. For the passport route the SP's verification report is the input to the RPO's decision.

action: Decide the PCC on the cleared police verification and grant the certificate (passport route).
on_reject: Adverse police report; PCC withheld/refused; applicant notified with reasons.
note: The RPO is the statutory issuing authority for the PCC used for visas/immigration/overseas employment under the Passports Act, 1967. Where address records are already current, the RPO may grant on the spot without fresh field verification.

action: Print/generate and deliver the certificate to the applicant.
note: Passport route: PCC booklet/sticker printed and dispatched or handed over at the PSK. State route: digitally signed Character Certificate downloadable from the e-district portal.

action: If stalled on police verification, escalate via the portal grievance system or in person.
note: Escalation paths: Passport Seva grievance / national call centre and the RPO; state route via the Right-to-Service designated appellate officer (UP Janhit Guarantee / Uttarakhand Sewa Ka Adhikar), CPGRAMS, and follow-up with the SHO/SP office. RTI can surface a delayed verification's status.

action: Verify seller's title: pull mother deed, khatauni/record of rights, and Encumbrance Certificate before committing.
note: Record of rights in UP is the khatauni (upbhulekh.gov.in); Lekhpal/Patwari maintains it. EC and chain-of-title confirm the seller can convey clear title. Due-diligence, not a statutory step.

action: Draft the sale deed: parties, property schedule, consideration, and terms; agreement-to-sell optional.
note: Agreement to sell is customary/protective, not mandatory for conveyance. The registrable instrument is the sale deed itself. Confirmed: registration of the transfer is compulsory under Registration Act 1908 §17.

action: Compute and pay stamp duty on higher of consideration or circle rate, plus registration fee.
note: UP stamp duty ~7% of market/circle-rate value (rebates for female buyers; only ₹5,000 for blood-relative transfers). Registration fee 1%, capped at ₹30,000. Paid via igrsup.gov.in e-stamp. Percentages are state-notified rates, subject to change.

action: If consideration ≥ ₹50 lakh, deduct 1% TDS and deposit via Form 26QB before registration.
note: TDS obligation is on the buyer under Income-tax Act 1961 §194-IA for transactions of ₹50 lakh or more. PAN of both parties (or Form 60) is required at registration.

post_name: Buyer via IGRSUP online slot booking
action: Book an online appointment/token at the Sub-Registrar of Assurances for the property's jurisdiction.
note: Registration Act 1908 §23 requires presentation within four months of the deed's execution. UP uses igrsup.gov.in for slot booking. Jurisdiction is the Sub-Registrar covering the property's location.

action: Verify identities of buyer, seller, and two witnesses appearing in person; capture biometrics/photos.
on_reject: Appeal to District Registrar (Registration Act §72) if refused
note: Registration Act 1908 §34 requires the executants to appear before the registering officer within the presentation window. Aadhaar/PAN, photos and biometrics of parties and two witnesses are taken. The Sub-Registrar (not the District Collector) is the registering authority.

action: Submit written TC application or school TC form to Principal/Head
note: State child's name, class, admission number, reason for leaving and intended date; keep an acknowledgement copy.

action: Apply online via UP e-district / CSC or offline at tehsil supply office for new ration card, listing all members
note: UP: apply through edistrict.up.gov.in or a Jan Seva Kendra (CSC); attach Aadhaar of every member, residence proof, and no-duplicate declaration

action: Field-verify household composition, residence, and eligibility category; confirm no member double-listed elsewhere
on_reject: Adverse verification report; application liable to rejection
note: The Purti/Supply Inspector is the standard UP field verifier; de-duplication against existing cards is done via Aadhaar seeding

action: Verify residence and income/eligibility details in revenue records where required for category classification
on_reject: Adverse report on residence or income feeds rejection
note: Revenue-side residence/income check supporting NFSA priority (BPL/AAY) vs non-priority classification

action: Review verification reports; recommend/counter-sign eligibility category at tehsil/sub-division level
on_reject: Recommend rejection back to DSO with reasons
note: Revenue chain confirms NFSA priority classification; in some UP tehsils issuance is sanctioned here, but final PDS sanction sits with DSO

action: Decide eligibility and sanction issuance of the new NFSA ration card
on_reject: Speaking rejection order; applicant may appeal under Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam / to DGRO
note: DSO is the district approving authority for ration cards under the Food & Civil Supplies dept, under the District Magistrate/Collectorate; NFSA coverage cap governs priority slots

action: Generate Aadhaar-seeded digital ration card and map household to a linked fair price shop
note: e-ration card downloadable from e-district; entitlement drawn monthly at the linked FPS for all listed members

action: If stalled or wrongly rejected, hear grievance; direct issuance/correction
on_reject: Escalate to State Food Commission
note: NFSA s.15 mandates a DGRO in every district; s.16 State Food Commission can impose penalty (s.33) for non-compliance; parallel appeal lies under UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011

action: Confirm stamp duty/fee paid, admit execution, and register the sale deed in the record.
on_reject: Appeal to District Registrar / Registrar of the district under Registration Act §72 (except where refusal is on denial of execution)
note: This is the decisive step: registration conveys ownership. Registration Act 1908 §72 gives the appeal against a Sub-Registrar's refusal to the District Registrar. Denial-of-execution refusals go to civil suit under §77 instead.

action: Return the registered original sale deed to the buyer after scanning and indexing.
time_limit: Immediately or within a few days
note: Endorsed/indexed original returned to the buyer. Certified copies remain available from the Sub-Registrar's record thereafter.

action: Send intimation of the registered transfer to the Tehsildar to initiate mutation of the record of rights.
note: UP Revenue Code 2006 §34: on registration of a document creating/extinguishing title to land, the registering authority must send intimation to the Tehsildar in whose jurisdiction the land lies — the statutory bridge from registration to mutation.

action: File a dakhil kharij (namantaran) mutation application with the registered deed and prior khatauni.
note: Registration transfers ownership but not the revenue record; the buyer should still apply for mutation (dakhil kharij / namantaran) online at upbhulekh.gov.in or e-District so the record of rights and property-tax records are updated. Distinct from registration.

action: Conduct field verification, issue public notice, and report on the mutation application to the Tehsildar.
time_limit: Within the Tehsildar's overall mutation timeline
note: The Lekhpal (Patwari) performs the ground-level verification and objection-notice step feeding the Tehsildar's order. An objection window allows interested parties to contest before the order is passed.

action: Decide the mutation and update the khatauni/record of rights into the buyer's name.
time_limit: ~30-45 days (undisputed); specific limit notified under Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 §3
on_reject: Appeal to Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) / Sub-Divisional Officer under UP Revenue Code 2006 §35; then revision to Commissioner under §210. For service delay, first appeal within 30 days under Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 §6.
note: Tehsildar is the mutation authority under UP Revenue Code 2006 (§34 read with the mutation provisions). This is where the collectorate/revenue side (the stated office class) actually comes in. Undisputed cases run ~30-45 days; contested mutations become a revenue proceeding.

action: If registration refused or mutation delayed/denied, pursue the statutory appeal for that stage.
time_limit: Mutation service appeal within 30 days of rejection/expiry (Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam §6)
on_reject: Registration refusal: District Registrar (Registration Act §72), then civil court. Mutation: SDM (UP Revenue Code §35) → Commissioner revision (§210). Service delay: First Appellate Officer then Second Appellate Authority (Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam §6). Fraud/impersonation: police + civil court.
note: Two separate ladders: the registration-refusal ladder under the Registration Act 1908 and the mutation/revenue ladder under the UP Revenue Code 2006, plus the Janhit Guarantee service-delay ladder. Title/valuation disputes proceed as revenue/civil litigation.

action: Verify enrolment and check pending fees, library and property dues
note: Dues clearance is the common precondition; under RTE s.5 dues cannot be used to indefinitely withhold a child's transfer/admission.

action: Cross-check TC against admission and scholar registers
note: Confirms register serial, exam results and category details before the head signs.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (Street-Vending / Urban-Livelihood 'DUDA' cell, Nagar Nigam)
action: Submit CoV application with ID, photos, residence proof and vending-spot/goods details at corporation cell or portal
on_reject: Incomplete forms returned for cure; refile with missing documents
note: No single national form; exact form, fee and checklist are set by state rules and the local corporation. Many corporations accept applications online via the state e-district / municipal portal or during a vendor survey camp.

post_name: Survey Enumerator (Town Vending Committee survey team / appointed agency)
action: Record applicant in the street-vendor survey and issue a survey token/ID
on_reject: Un-surveyed applicants may still apply; placement then depends on vending zones and caps in the Street Vending Plan
note: Section 3 requires a survey of all existing vendors (repeated at least every five years); a surveyed vendor cannot be evicted before a certificate is issued and has a certificate as of right under s.4.

post_name: Lekhpal / Ward Revenue Inspector (field verification, as engaged by the corporation)
action: Verify applicant identity, residence and actual occupation of the claimed vending spot
on_reject: Discrepancies flagged to the TVC; applicant given chance to clarify
note: Field/spot verification is a local-procedure step (post varies by corporation — ward inspector, revenue official or survey agency); not named in the central Act.

post_name: Town Vending Committee (chaired by the Municipal Commissioner / Nagar Ayukt)
action: Verify application against survey and vending plan; confirm spot lies in a designated vending zone
on_reject: If spot is in a no-vending zone, applicant offered an alternative zone/spot per the plan
note: TVC is constituted under the Act, chaired by the Municipal Commissioner, with at least 40% members being street vendors elected by vendors; it screens applications against the Street Vending Plan (s.6/s.7).

post_name: Town Vending Committee (chaired by the Municipal Commissioner / Nagar Ayukt)
action: Recommend issuance of the certificate of vending, fixing zone, category and timings
on_reject: Refusal must be reasoned; surveyed vendors are entitled as of right, making non-issuance contestable
note: The TVC is the body that recommends who gets a certificate; surveyed vendors are to be issued one as of right under s.4.

action: Issue and sign the Certificate of Vending on the TVC recommendation
on_reject: Reasoned refusal appealable; vendor may seek redress via the s.22 committee
note: The municipal corporation formally issues the CoV under s.4, specifying zone/spot, category (stationary/mobile), permitted days and timings, and conditions.

action: Accept certificate conditions, give the personal-vending undertaking and pay the vending fee
on_reject: Certificate is non-transferable; breach of conditions can lead to cancellation after a hearing
note: Section 5 requires an undertaking to vend personally or through family and bars transfer/rental of the certificate; a nominal fee and periodic renewal apply per the local scheme.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (Nagar Nigam), or PM SVANidhi nodal officer
action: Deliver the issued CoV to the vendor and, if opted, forward it as basis for a PM SVANidhi loan
note: A Certificate/Letter of Recommendation of Vending is the eligibility document for a PM SVANidhi working-capital loan.

post_name: Municipal Commissioner (Nagar Ayukt) / RTI Public Information Officer, Nagar Nigam
action: If stalled, file a written grievance / RTI to obtain application status
on_reject: No response escalates to the first appellate authority under the RTI Act
note: First recourse for delay: written status request or RTI to the corporation; non-issuance to a surveyed vendor is directly contestable under s.4.

post_name: Committee for Dispute Redressal (chaired by a former Civil Judge / Judicial Magistrate) under s.22
action: Hear the vendor's written application against non-issuance or cancellation and direct relief
on_reject: Adverse order may be challenged by writ petition in the High Court
note: Section 22 requires the government to constitute a dispute-redressal committee chaired by a person who has been a civil judge or judicial magistrate plus two professionals — the designated appeal route for certificate disputes.

action: Entertain a writ petition to enforce the vendor's statutory protections if lower remedies fail
note: Ultimate recourse; High Courts have repeatedly enforced vendor protections and directed constitution of TVCs, surveys and certificate issuance under the 2014 Act.

action: Register on state labour single-window (UP Nivesh Mitra / Uttarakhand LAMS) and open Shops & Establishment service
note: State Shops & Establishment registration is a state law; UP uses Nivesh Mitra, Uttarakhand uses the Labour Act Management System (LAMS).

action: Fill establishment particulars: trade name, address, nature, employee count, date of commencement, weekly holiday
note: Notice of establishment is required under s.30 of the 1962 Act; apply within 30 days of commencing business.

action: Upload documents (owner ID, premises proof, photo, PAN, employee details) and pay employee-count-based fee
note: Fee scales by number of employees; confirm the current fee schedule on the state labour portal (figures change frequently).

action: Scrutinise application and documents for completeness; flag deficiencies for correction
on_reject: Application returned to applicant for correction of deficiencies before re-submission
note: Real designation: labour-office dealing clerk; not part of the revenue/panchayat post roster supplied.

post_name: Inspector under the Shops & Establishment Act (Labour Enforcement Officer)
action: Verify particulars; where required, conduct premises inspection of the establishment
on_reject: Adverse inspection findings communicated; applicant given opportunity to remedy or explain
note: Real designation: Inspector/Labour Enforcement Officer appointed under the Act; many states now defer physical verification to post-registration.

post_name: Chief Inspector of Shops & Establishments / District Labour Officer (Registering Authority)
action: Decide the application and register the establishment (or reject with reasons)
on_reject: Rejection with reasons; applicant may re-apply after cure or appeal to the appellate authority under the Act
note: Registering/approving authority under the Act; deemed/auto-approval on complete submission is common in current online flows.

post_name: Chief Inspector of Shops & Establishments / District Labour Officer (Registering Authority)
action: Sign and issue the Registration Certificate (labour identification/registration number)
note: Certificate must be displayed at the premises; the same authority signs it.

action: Approve, sign and affix school seal on the Transfer Certificate
note: The TC is valid as an official record only when signed by the head with the institutional seal.

action: Apply to Nagar Nigam for trade licence online (Nivesh Mitra / e-Nagar Sewa) or at zonal office
note: Application states trade category and premises; correct classification (general trade vs dangerous & offensive trade) determines the approval track.

action: Register application, scrutinise documents for completeness, raise deficiency query if papers missing
on_reject: Deficiency memo issued; applicant resubmits missing documents before processing continues.
note: Zonal / ward licensing desk of the Nagar Nigam does the first-cut completeness check.

action: Confirm premises is assessed to house/property tax and no tax dues are outstanding
on_reject: Applicant clears property-tax arrears before licence proceeds.
note: A trade licence is routinely gated on a clear property-tax account for the premises; designation varies by corporation.

action: Inspect premises for hygiene, safety, zoning and trade suitability; file inspection report
on_reject: Adverse report; applicant remedies premises defects and seeks re-inspection.
note: Physical site inspection by the Health Department's sanitary/food inspector; central for eateries and D&O trades.

post_name: Designated Officer, FSSAI (Food Safety) / District Food Safety Officer
action: Grant FSSAI registration/licence where the business handles food (prerequisite clearance)
on_reject: Food business cannot be licensed until FSSAI clearance is obtained.
note: Applies only to food businesses; issued under the FSS Act 2006, separate from the municipal file. Skip for non-food trades.

post_name: Fire Officer / Chief Fire Officer (State Fire Service)
action: Issue Fire NOC where premises size/occupancy triggers fire-safety clearance
on_reject: Applicant installs required fire-safety measures and re-applies for NOC.
note: Prerequisite for larger/assembly premises; not required for small ordinary shops.

post_name: Regional Officer, UP/Uttarakhand Pollution Control Board
action: Grant Consent to Establish/Operate for polluting or hazardous trades
on_reject: Trade cannot operate without CTE/CTO; applicant meets effluent/emission norms.
note: Under Water Act 1974 & Air Act 1981; applies only to red/orange-category trades. Skip for benign shops.

post_name: Health Officer / Chief Medical Officer (Nagar Nigam Health Dept)
action: Review inspection report and clearances; recommend grant of trade / D&O licence
on_reject: Recommends refusal with reasons; file returns to applicant for cure.
note: The Nagar Nigam Health Officer (or CMO where health-linked) is the substantive vetting authority before the sanctioning officer signs.

post_name: Zonal Officer / Additional Municipal Commissioner (Nagar Nigam)
action: Decide the application and sanction the trade licence on the recommended file
on_reject: Rejection order with reasons; appeal lies to the Municipal Commissioner and under the Right-to-Service Act.
note: Sanctioning power is delegated by the Municipal Commissioner to the zonal/additional officer for routine trades under the UP Municipal Corporation Act 1959.

action: Assess and collect the annual trade-licence fee per trade category and premises size
on_reject: Licence not released until fee paid; challan re-issued.
note: Fee is category-and-area based and is an annual charge; paid via portal or corporation counter.

action: Sign/issue the trade licence in the Nagar Nigam's name for the licence year
note: Issued under the Commissioner's authority; licence carries conditions and is renewable annually.

action: Deliver the trade licence (digital/printed) to the applicant; record for annual renewal
note: Licence downloadable from the e-Nagar Sewa / Nivesh Mitra account; renewal due each licence year.

post_name: Designated Appellate Officer (Right to Service) / Municipal Commissioner
action: Hear appeal and direct time-bound disposal if the licence is delayed or wrongly refused
on_reject: Further appeal to the second appellate authority under the Right-to-Service Act; grievance on the state CM portal.
note: Escalation under the UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 / Uttarakhand Right to Service Act 2011 where the service is notified as time-bound.

post_name: State labour single-window portal (Nivesh Mitra / LAMS)
action: Deliver the digitally-signed Registration Certificate for download to the applicant
note: Time-bound delivery is notified under the state Right to Service / Sewa Ka Adhikar Act; renewal falls due per the state cycle.

post_name: Appellate Authority under the Act / Deputy Labour Commissioner (grievance & appeal)
action: Hear grievance or appeal on rejection or delay; direct registration or remedy as due
note: Escalation path: portal grievance module, then Deputy Labour Commissioner, then State Labour Commissioner; delay is separately actionable under the Right to Service Act's designated/appellate officer.

post_name: Khand Shiksha Adhikari (Block Education Officer, BEO)
action: Countersign TC for inter-block/inter-district government-school transfers
note: Situational, not universal - required by many Basic Shiksha rules for government/aided schools moving across jurisdictions.

post_name: Basic Shiksha Adhikari (District Basic Education Officer, BSA)
action: Countersign / attest TC for inter-district or inter-state moves where required
note: District-level attestation applies chiefly to government/aided schools; private-board schools may not need it. Verify locally.

action: Collect signed TC; retain a photocopy for records
Accept TC and admit child into the new school
note: Under RTE s.5, delay in producing the TC shall not be a ground to delay or deny admission; the new school helps obtain it if needed.

post_name: Designated Officer, UP/UK Right to Service (or Khand/Basic Shiksha Adhikari)
action: Escalate written complaint if the school delays or refuses the TC
note: First seek reason and date in writing from the school; then complain to the block/district education officer or the notified Right-to-Service designated officer; RTI can compel a response where TC issuance is a listed service.

action: Auto-issue permanent Udyam Registration Number and e-certificate with dynamic QR code.
note: No officer sign-off; issuance is machine-driven and automatic on successful validation. This is the outcome step, not a human approval.

action: Issue timber transit pass (TP) for moving felled timber of regulated species
on_reject: Movement without a TP is seizable; apply again with felling order attached.
note: Felling permission and transit pass are separate approvals under the state Timber Transit Rules; TP not needed for transit-exempt species.

action: Execute sale; seller endorses/hands over Registration Certificate; both sign Forms 29 and 30.
note: India is single-document: the RC is the ownership record - there is no separate title. Form 29 = seller's notice of transfer; Form 30 = buyer's application. Seller also gives a delivery/sale note.

action: Confirm the trade needs a corporation licence and its category; identify required extra clearances.
note: At the Nagar Nigam trade-licence / health section or Nagrik Suvidha Kendra. Fee slab and clearances (fire/health/pollution) depend on trade category.

action: Assemble ID/address proof, premises proof + owner NOC, property-tax/holding number, category NOCs.
note: Category NOCs may include Fire NOC, FSSAI food licence, UPPCB consent for polluting trades. Exact checklist varies by corporation.

action: File the trade-licence application online with documents and prescribed fee; get application number.
note: Via UP e-Nagar Sewa portal (e-nagarsewaup.gov.in) or the corporation office / Nagrik Suvidha Kendra counter. Intake only.

post_name: Licence Inspector (real designation; corporation licence/tax inspector)
action: Scrutinise the file and record any objection or demand for additional documents.
on_reject: Applicant cures objections / resubmits.
note: Post is a corporation-specific designation outside the standard list (Licence/Tax Inspector under the trade-licence or health section).

action: Inspect premises to confirm trade matches declaration and meets health/safety norms.
on_reject: Adverse report returned to applicant with reasons.
note: For dangerous & offensive / food & health trades, the corporation health wing (CMO office / MO / sanitary inspector) inspects under the 1959 Act licensing provisions.

post_name: Licence Superintendent / Zonal Officer (real designation; corporation delegated officer)
action: Recommend grant or rejection on the inspection and scrutiny reports.
on_reject: Recommendation of rejection escalates to sanctioning officer for order.
note: Delegated recommending officer varies by corporation (Zonal/Additional/Deputy Commissioner or Licence Superintendent). Designation outside standard list.

action: Sanction and grant the trade licence, or reject with reasons.
time_limit: Per corporation's notified SLA under UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 (indicative ~7-30 days).
on_reject: Written rejection with reasons; appeal to the first appellate authority under UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011, then second appellate authority.
note: Nagar Ayukt is the licensing authority under the UP Municipal Corporation Act 1959; power is frequently delegated to a Zonal/Additional/Deputy Commissioner.

action: Issue the trade licence on payment of the assessed fee; deliver certificate / download.
note: Licence issued on the e-Nagar Sewa portal or at the counter after fee payment.

action: If SLA lapses or service refused, escalate to first then second appellate authority.
on_reject: First appellate authority, then second appellate authority under the 2011 Act; parallel Jansunwai grievance / RTI for status and delay reasons.
note: Verified escalation lever: Jansunwai-Samadhan portal (jansunwai.up.nic.in) sends deadline-lapse reminders and pushes stalled municipal grievances up the chain.

action: Renew the annual licence before expiry to keep the trade lawful.
note: Trade licences are typically annual; running without a current licence invites penalty or sealing. Renew on the same portal/office.

action: Open udyamregistration.gov.in and select New Registration for those not registered as MSME.
note: Free, fully online, paperless self-declaration; no intermediary or fee. Governed by S.O. 2119(E), 26 June 2020.

action: Enter Aadhaar number and applicant name; use proprietor/managing partner/authorized signatory Aadhaar per entity type.
on_reject: Correct the Aadhaar/name mismatch against UIDAI records before proceeding.
note: Aadhaar of proprietor (proprietorship), managing partner (partnership), karta (HUF), or authorized signatory (company/LLP/society).

action: Authenticate Aadhaar via OTP sent to the linked mobile number.
on_reject: If OTP fails, ensure mobile is linked to Aadhaar at UIDAI; retry.
note: Aadhaar validation is automatic and mandatory per the notification.

action: Select type of organisation and enter enterprise PAN for validation.
note: PAN mandatory w.e.f. 1 April 2021 (S.O. 1055(E), 5 Mar 2021).

action: Validate PAN and auto-fetch investment/ITR-linked details from Income Tax records.
on_reject: Fix PAN mismatch; investment data is pulled automatically from ITR filings.
note: PAN & GST-linked investment/turnover taken automatically from government databases.

action: Enter GSTIN where the enterprise is required to be GST-registered under the CGST Act.
note: GSTIN required only as per applicability of CGST Act 2017; not required for enterprises exempt from GST registration.

action: Validate GSTIN and auto-fetch turnover details from GST returns.
on_reject: Reconcile GSTIN details before proceeding.
note: Turnover pulled automatically from GSTN; no manual document upload.

action: Fill enterprise details: name, address, bank account, NIC activity codes, employment, dates.
note: Self-declaration; no documents/proof are uploaded to the portal.

action: Classify enterprise as Micro/Small/Medium from investment and turnover figures.
note: Thresholds are set by notification and revised periodically; the portal applies the current criteria automatically.

action: Submit the final self-declaration and confirm the declaration checkbox.
note: Furnishing false information is punishable under Section 27 of the MSMED Act 2006.

post_name: District Industries Centre (DIC) / MSME-Development & Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO)
action: Provide optional in-person assistance / single-window support for registration.
note: Facilitation only, not an approval gate; also Udyam Assist Platform (UAP) for informal micro enterprises without PAN/GST.

post_name: MSME Champions Control Room / grievance cell
action: Escalate registration problems or grievances via champions.gov.in or the portal helpdesk.
note: Support: champions@gov.in and champions.gov.in; DIC single-window as backup.

action: Register/log in on UP e-District portal or file via CSC (Jan Seva Kendra) / tehsil counter
note: Online through edistrict.up.gov.in; CSC operator or tehsil can file offline. Apply under the citizen's own login or authenticated CSC.

action: Fill income-certificate form listing all family members and total annual family income; upload documents; pay fee
note: Nominal fee (commonly ~Rs 15-30 via e-District; CSC may add a small service charge). Self-declaration/affidavit of family income is the core input.

action: Register application, generate application number, and route file to field verification
note: Application/acknowledgement number lets the citizen track status on the portal.

action: Conduct field verification of declared family income and residence; file verification report
on_reject: Report adverse finding upward; application may be rejected with reason recorded on portal
note: Ground-level revenue functionary; the substantive check on the income declaration.

action: Review and countersign Lekhpal's verification report; forward to reporting officer
on_reject: Send file back to Lekhpal for re-verification or reject
note: Supervisory revenue check between Lekhpal and Naib Tehsildar; role naming varies by tehsil.

action: Scrutinise verified file and recommend issuance to the Tehsildar
on_reject: Return for correction or recommend rejection
note: Reporting/recommending officer in the revenue chain; some tehsils route directly Lekhpal -> Tehsildar.

action: Decide and digitally sign/issue the income certificate (Designated Officer under Janhit Guarantee Act)
time_limit: ~15 working days (Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam notified limit; verify current schedule)
on_reject: Record reasons; applicant may apply to First Appellate Authority under the Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam
note: Tehsildar is the notified Designated Officer and issuing authority; certificate is digitally signed.

action: Download digitally-signed certificate from e-District portal or collect from tehsil
note: Certificate carries a verification number checkable online. Validity commonly 6 months to 1 year depending on use.

action: Hear first appeal if certificate is delayed past the statutory limit or refused (First Appellate Authority)
on_reject: Escalate to Second Appellate Authority (District Magistrate / notified officer)
note: First Appellate Authority under the Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam is the officer above the Designated Officer (typically SDM). Exact designation per the district's notification.

action: Hear second appeal and direct issuance; may impose penalty on defaulting officer
note: Second Appellate Authority under the Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam; certificate is ultimately a District Collectorate revenue document.

action: Immediately gather transaction ID/UTR, amount, date-time, fraudster UPI/account/number, and screenshots.
time_limit: Act within the golden hour (first few hours)
note: Speed is decisive for a freeze; reporting is free. Real actor = the victim.

post_name: 1930 Helpline Operator (I4C Cyber Fraud Helpline, National / MHA)
action: Call 1930; operator records the complaint and logs it into CFCFRMS.
time_limit: As soon as possible after the fraud
note: 1930 is the national cyber-fraud helpline run by I4C, MHA. Not one of the six rural posts; real national designation.

post_name: Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting & Management System (CFCFRMS, I4C)
action: System relays the flagged transaction to victim's bank and beneficiary bank/wallet.
note: CFCFRMS is the ticketing backbone linking 1930, portal, banks and police. Confirm exact routing per state.

post_name: Beneficiary Bank / Payment Service Provider (Nodal Officer)
action: Place hold/lien on the disputed amount in the recipient account to stop withdrawal.
time_limit: Within golden hour; before money is moved on
on_reject: If money already withdrawn/moved, freeze fails; recovery then needs court process.
note: Bank decides the hold; success depends on speed. Real financial-institution designation.

post_name: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in, I4C)
action: Register formal complaint under 'Report Financial Fraud'; enter incident details and upload evidence.
time_limit: Same day; ideally right after the 1930 call
note: Phone call and portal report are two halves of one process. Verify current menu labels/OTP flow.

post_name: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in, I4C)
action: Portal issues an acknowledgement / complaint reference number to the complainant.
note: Save the reference number; it is needed for all follow-up and status checks.

post_name: Victim's Bank / Card / UPI Provider (Customer Care, Nodal Officer)
action: Separately notify bank of unauthorised transaction; freeze card/account and reset PIN/passwords.
time_limit: Report to bank within 3 working days for zero liability
note: RBI DBR.No.Leg.BC.78/2017-18: report within 3 working days = zero liability; 4-7 days = capped liability.

action: Provide shadow-reversal credit for the disputed sum in third-party-breach cases reported in time.
time_limit: Within 10 working days of customer notification
on_reject: If reported late/negligence attributed, liability shifts per bank Board policy.
note: RBI zero/limited-liability circular; value-dated to transaction date. Bank decides eligibility.

action: Conducts field verification of residence/caste/income at the declared address and files report
on_reject: Negative verification can lead to rejection
note: Lekhpal checks khatauni, voter list, neighbours

post_name: Nodal Cyber Cell Officer (State/UT Cyber Crime Cell)
action: Receive routed complaint; assign to jurisdictional cyber crime police station for action.
time_limit: Often within days; complex cases longer
note: Execution devolves to state/UT police (e.g. UP Cyber Crime). Real designation, not a rural revenue post.

post_name: Station House Officer (SHO/SO, Cyber Crime Police Station)
action: Assess complaint and decide whether to register an FIR for a cognizable offence.
on_reject: If FIR refused, escalate to Superintendent of Police / DCP under CrPC/BNSS complaint provisions.
note: IT Act 2000 + BNS 2023 cheating/forgery. SHO is a listed real post.

action: Investigate: trace money trail, seek disclosures from banks/platforms, pursue recovery.
time_limit: Days to months depending on complexity
note: Recovery of frozen funds to victim typically needs a court order. Uncertain timeline.

action: Track complaint status online and follow up on 1930 quoting the reference number.
note: May require login with same phone/credentials. Verify current status-check flow.

action: Apply for Learner's Licence via Parivahan Sarathi portal or at jurisdictional RTO; submit Form 2.
note: Form 2 application with Form 1 self-declaration of fitness; Form 1A doctor's medical certificate required for transport vehicles or applicants above the age threshold (commonly 40+, varies by state - flag). Grounded in CMV Rules 1989 R.10-11.

action: Upload proof of age and address, photos; pay the statutory learner-licence fee online or at counter.
note: Exact fee is state-specific under the U.P. Motor Vehicles Rules 1998 (flag). Documents per CMV Rules 1989 R.4/R.10.

post_name: Regional Transport Officer / Assistant Regional Transport Officer (RTO/ARTO)
action: Verify submitted documents and schedule the learner's test slot.
on_reject: If documents deficient, applicant is asked to re-submit; escalate to RTO officer in charge.
note: RTO/ARTO is the licensing authority designation under the state Transport Department (real post title; outside the provided revenue/panchayat list - noted). Slot booking confirmed on Sarathi portal (LL Test Slot Booking).

action: Sit the computerized learner's test on traffic signs, road rules and safety at the RTO.
on_reject: On failure, re-book and re-take the test after the permitted interval.
note: Pass mark commonly ~60% but state-specific (flag). Some states allow a supervised at-home online test. Confirmed as a service on Sarathi (Mock Test / LL Test).

post_name: Regional Transport Officer / Assistant Regional Transport Officer (RTO/ARTO)
action: Approve and issue the Learner's Licence on passing, usually same day.
on_reject: Refusal without cause appealable to the Regional/Deputy Transport Commissioner, then State Transport Commissioner.
note: Learner's Licence issued as Form 3 (confirmed on Sarathi: 'Print Learner Licence (Form3)'); valid 6 months. This decides the LL request.

action: Wait the mandatory minimum 30 days after LL issue; then apply for permanent DL within the 6-month LL validity.
time_limit: Minimum 30 days after LL issue; apply within 180 days (LL validity)
on_reject: If the 6-month LL lapses, re-do Stage 1 (fresh learner's licence).
note: Statutory 30-day minimum interval under CMV Rules 1989 (R.15). Applying beyond LL validity requires a new LL.

action: Apply for permanent Driving Licence via Form 4 on Sarathi or at the RTO.
note: Form 4 is the statutory DL application form (CMV Rules 1989 R.14; confirmed as 'New Driving Licence' on Sarathi).

action: Pay the driving-licence and driving-test fee; book a driving-test slot.
note: DL fee plus test/slot fee; exact amounts state-specific under U.P. Motor Vehicles Rules 1998 (flag). Slot booking confirmed on Sarathi (DL Test Slot Booking).

action: Conduct and evaluate the practical driving test at the RTO track or Automated Driving Test Track.
on_reject: On failure, applicant re-books and re-tests after a short waiting period (e.g. ~1 week - varies, flag).
note: Applicant arranges a vehicle of the class applied for. ADTT (Automated Driving Test Track) increasingly mandatory in larger cities (flag). MVI is the real statutory testing designation (outside the provided list - noted).

post_name: Regional Transport Officer / Assistant Regional Transport Officer (RTO/ARTO)
action: Approve the permanent Driving Licence on a passed test.
on_reject: Refusal without cause appealable to Regional/Deputy Transport Commissioner, then State Transport Commissioner.
note: Licensing authority approves issue after the MVI's pass report. This decides the permanent DL request.

action: Print and dispatch the smart-card Driving Licence by post, or hold for collection.
note: Permanent DL valid 20 years or until age 50, whichever earlier; the MV (Amendment) Act 2019 revised age brackets and renewal rules (flag). Print DL confirmed on Sarathi.

action: Escalate service delay/refusal up the chain; invoke Right-to-Public-Services deadline where scheduled.
time_limit: As scheduled under the U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (where the DL service is notified)
on_reject: Designated appellate officer under the Janhit Guarantee Act; Parivahan grievance channel for portal/technical failures.
note: Escalation ladder: RTO officer in charge to Regional/Deputy Transport Commissioner to State Transport Commissioner (department head). RtPS coverage, notified deadline and appellate officer are state-specific (flag).

action: Escalate bank service failure (no action on timely report) after bank grievance redressal.
time_limit: After 30 days of unresolved bank grievance
note: RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme 2021 for banking/digital-transaction grievances. Verify eligibility.

post_name: Superintendent of Police / DCP (District Cyber Cell)
action: Escalate persistent police non-action in person with reference number and evidence.
time_limit: If lower level does not act
note: Higher police authority for grievance against non-registration/inaction. Real designation.

action: Cross-checks and endorses the Lekhpal's verification report
on_reject: Report returned for re-verification
note: supervisory endorsement of field report

action: Gather establishment, owner, premises and employee details; register on Nivesh Mitra portal.
note: No employee threshold - even a zero-employee proprietor must register. Registering officer of record is the Labour Department, not the municipal corporation (draft's flagged uncertainty confirmed correct).

action: Submit Common Application Form (CAF) on Nivesh Mitra to generate the Unit ID.
note: Single-window: one CAF drives all sub-registrations including the trade-licence requirement.

action: Under Department of Labour, start new Shops & Establishment Act 1962 registration application; upload documents.
note: Documents: premises photo with name board, owner Aadhaar + PAN, address proof + utility bill, bank proof, employee list, constitution proof.

action: Pay the consolidated registration fee online; fee auto-calculated by employee-count slab.
note: Indicative slabs: ~Rs.40 (no employee), ~Rs.200 (1-5), ~Rs.300 (6-10), ~Rs.500 (11-25), ~Rs.1000 (25+). Exact amount auto-computed on portal.

action: Scrutinise the application and uploaded documents; may route for premises verification.
on_reject: Query/objection raised on Nivesh Mitra; applicant resubmits corrected details.
note: Inspector is a designated officer under the Act (included in the Chief Inspector definition, Sec 29). On the single-window this stage is largely system-driven / near-automatic.

post_name: Inspector / Labour Enforcement Officer, Labour Department
action: Where required, inspect the establishment premises and verify declared particulars.
on_reject: Adverse inspection findings returned as objections; applicant cures and resubmits.
note: Physical inspection is not routine for low-employee shops under the single-window regime; retained as a possible statutory check.

action: Fill Form 2 application and Form 1 self-declaration of fitness on Sarathi/Parivahan portal
note: Online at sarathi.parivahan.gov.in routes to the jurisdictional RTO; some RTOs still accept paper submission at the counter (verify locally).

action: Upload age proof, address proof, photo; attach Form 1A medical certificate if transport-vehicle class
note: Form 1A must be signed by a registered medical practitioner; exact document list varies by state and vehicle class.

action: Pay the statutory learner-licence and test fee online
note: Fee is prescribed under CMVR Rule 32; exact current amount (roughly Rs 150-350 with class/state surcharges) not verified this session.

action: Verify application, documents and jurisdiction; schedule the learner-test slot
on_reject: Application returned to applicant for correction/re-upload of documents
note: Real designation: RTO dealing hand/clerk; not one of the six standard office posts. Slot allotment same-day to a few days per RTO load.

action: Sit the computer-based learner test on road signs, traffic rules and safety
on_reject: On fail, re-test after paying re-test fee (retakes vary by state)
note: Under CMVR r.11; pass mark typically 60% (about 6 of 10 questions). Some states allow home/online test.

action: Verify test result and confirm applicant meets eligibility for the class applied
on_reject: Learner licence withheld; applicant advised to re-sit test or cure defect
note: Real designation: MVI/ARTO under the State Transport Department; not one of the six standard posts.

action: Sanction and authorise issue of the Learner's Licence on a pass
on_reject: Refusal recorded; applicant may re-apply or appeal to Transport Commissioner / Appellate Authority under MVA
note: The Licensing Authority under MVA 1988 s.9 is the sanctioning authority (a gazetted RTO/ARTO officer of the State Transport Department), NOT a Secretariat officer. This is the approval step.

action: Generate/print Learner's Licence in Form 3 or release it for portal download
note: LL (Form 3) valid 6 months; permanent DL test allowed after a minimum 30-day wait and within the 180-day validity.

action: Escalate unresolved grievance via RTO help counter, then Parivahan grievance link, then Transport Commissioner
note: Escalation ladder: RTO public-grievance counter / Sarathi helpdesk -> Regional/Additional Transport Commissioner -> State Transport Commissioner. State RTPS appeal may apply if the service is notified.

action: Applicant files a demarcation (paimaish) application at the Tehsil counter / e-District portal addressed to the SDM.
on_reject: Incomplete application returned for correction; resubmit with missing documents or fee.
note: Attach current khatauni/khasra, the plot map (naksha/tippan), latest revenue/tax receipts, ID, and a sketch showing the disputed line. In UP the channel is e-District / Bhulekh (upbhulekh.gov.in) or the Tehsil; a nominal application/measurement fee applies. Demarcation is filed as a revenue application to the Sub-Divisional Officer, not a police matter.

action: Diarises the application, assigns a case number and issues a dated receipt.
note: The dated acknowledgement starts the Right-to-Public-Services clock where demarcation is a notified/scheduled service under the U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011.

action: Registers the demarcation request and directs the Tehsildar / field staff to carry out the measurement.
note: Under U.P. Revenue Code 2006 Ss. 24–26, fixation/demarcation of boundaries is a function of the Assistant Collector / Sub-Divisional Officer; the SDM directs the paimaish and later passes the operative order.

action: Fixes a survey date, orders adjoining owners (including the neighbour) to be notified to attend.
note: Both parties must be formally summoned so the result binds them; measurement done ex-parte can be reopened. The Tehsildar routes the file to the Revenue Inspector / Lekhpal for field survey.

action: Verifies the report against records and forwards the file to the signing authority
note: record-check layer

action: Conducts the field survey: re-measures the plot against khasra/map from fixed reference points (increasingly ETS/DGPS).
on_reject: If parties obstruct or reference marks are missing, survey is re-scheduled or referred up.
note: The Lekhpal/Patwari (village revenue accountant) is the first officer a citizen meets for any land matter; the amin/surveyor executes the chain/instrument measurement against the recorded khasra and map.

action: Supervises/verifies the field measurement and countersigns the measurement sheet for correctness.
on_reject: Report returned to Lekhpal for re-measurement if inconsistent with the record.
note: Revenue Inspector (Kanungo-level supervisory layer) checks the paimaish against the map/khatauni before it goes up for the demarcation order.

action: Compiles the paimaish report and boundary map (naksha) and forwards it to the SDM.
note: The demarcation report states where the correct boundary lies relative to the neighbour's occupation; it is the authoritative measurement, subject to the SDM's order and any appeal.

action: Passes the demarcation order fixing the boundary and directs erection/repair of boundary marks.
time_limit: where notified under the Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, within the scheduled limit (often ~30–45 days)
on_reject: If the applicant disputes the survey, seek re-demarcation, then appeal the revenue order to the Additional District Magistrate/Collector, and onward to the Commissioner and Board of Revenue.
note: U.P. Revenue Code 2006 Ss. 24–26: the SDO fixes boundaries and orders boundary-marks; disturbing/removing lawful boundary marks is itself an offence under the Code. This is the 'who decides' step for the demarcation itself.

action: Obtains a certified copy of the paimaish report and the updated boundary map.
on_reject: If the copy is withheld, escalate to the SDM / Tehsildar and use the Right-to-Public-Services / RTI route.
note: A certified copy is what the applicant relies on in any later encroachment-removal application or civil suit; get the map (naksha) as well as the narrative report.

action: On a written encroachment application citing the report, decides removal of the encroachment on recorded land.
on_reject: If the neighbour asserts a bona-fide title claim, the SDM cannot decide title — the applicant must file a civil suit; the revenue order is appealable to Collector → Commissioner → Board of Revenue.
note: U.P. Revenue Code 2006 S. 67 empowers ejectment of a person occupying land without title and damages for use/occupation; unauthorised occupation of Gram-Panchayat/common land is dealt with under Ss. 59/67. Revenue authorities act only where the record clearly shows the land is the applicant's or is public/common land, not where ownership is genuinely contested.

action: Draft succession-certificate petition under s.372 listing heirs, death, debts/securities sought
note: Not in the named UP post list; real designation is an enrolled Advocate engaged by the petitioner. Petition filed in the District Judge's court where the deceased ordinarily resided or where assets lie (s.371).

action: Attach death certificate, relationship proof, ID/address proof, asset list; swear affidavit; pay court fee
note: Court fee is ad valorem on the value of debts/securities under Court Fees Act 1870 Sch. I Art. 12; exact percentage varies by state amendment - not verified here.

post_name: Reader / Bench Clerk of the District Court
action: Register and number the petition; scrutinise for court-fee and formal defects; list for hearing
on_reject: Office objections returned for curing before admission
note: Ministerial court staff (Reader/Sarishtadar); not in the named UP revenue post list - real court designation used.

action: Conducts field enquiry, checks khatauni/khasra entries and possession, files field report
on_reject: Adverse field report may lead to rejection or conversion to contested case
note: first person a citizen meets for any land matter

action: Verifies and countersigns the Lekhpal's field report and khatauni check for correctness
on_reject: Report returned to Lekhpal for correction
note: Kanungo supervisory layer over the Lekhpal

action: Reviews field verification, ensures record consistency, forwards case to the Tehsil court
note: supervisory layer over the field staff

action: Issues proclamation (public notice) inviting objections from interested parties
note: s.35 proclamation; objections define uncontested vs contested branch

action: Lists the case for hearing before the Tehsildar/Naib Tehsildar after the objection period lapses
note: Reader manages the revenue court cause-list

action: Hears uncontested cases and passes the mutation order directing khatauni amendment
time_limit: target disposal within 45 days of application
on_reject: Appeal to Sub-Divisional Officer (SDM) within 30 days of the order
note: s.35(1) uncontested branch: NT directs amendment

action: For contested cases, adjudicates the dispute after hearing parties and passes the mutation order
on_reject: Appeal to SDM within 30 days; further to Collector/Commissioner
note: s.35(1) contested branch decided by Tehsildar; may take longer

action: Gives effect to the order by amending the khatauni (record of rights) entry
note: Record update executed at village level

action: Updates and preserves the amended record of rights in the tehsil record room
note: maintains the authoritative record copy

action: Issues a certified copy of the updated khatauni to the applicant
note: Certified copy is proof of mutation

action: Citizen applies via e-District/CSC or Tehsil counter; application captured with documents
on_reject: Incomplete applications returned for correction
note: e-District UP is the official channel

action: Generates the acknowledgement number and dated receipt, starting the service clock
note: Acknowledgement triggers the Janhit Guarantee time limit

action: Places the verified file before the Tehsildar/SDM for signature
note: Reader manages the signing queue

action: Reviews and digitally signs the caste/income/domicile certificate (SDM where designated)
time_limit: within the Janhit Guarantee statutory limit (~7-15 working days total)
on_reject: Appeal to First Appellate Officer within 30 days; second appeal within 60 days
note: designated officer under Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011

action: Delivers the digitally-signed certificate via e-District download / CSC to the applicant
note: Certificate verifiable online by certificate number

action: Publishes RTE round notification and readies the state RTE portal, block school list and seat matrix
note: admission is only into entry class (Class 1 / pre-primary) per s.12(1)(c)

action: Parent applies online on the state RTE portal, uploading eligibility documents and choosing neighbourhood schools
note: citizen-facing step; submission is by the parent online

action: Receives application plus documents and verifies eligibility (age, EWS/DG income/caste, residence, distance)
on_reject: reapply in next round or appeal to Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA)
note: neighbourhood: within 1 km (primary) / 3 km (upper primary)

action: Confirms the verified applicant pool for the block/district and forwards the eligible list into the lottery
on_reject: grievance to BSA / District Education Officer
note: only BEO-verified applications enter the draw

action: Oversees the online lottery/random allotment of verified children to specific schools per seat availability
on_reject: waitlist / subsequent round; appeal to CEO/BSA
note: lottery is the decisive allotment event under the 25% quota

action: Admit petition and order publication of general notice inviting objections (s.373)
note: s.373(1): court fixes a day for hearing and issues notice to those it thinks fit. District Judge is the competent authority under Part X (matches district-court office class).

action: Allotted private school admits the child free of charge and records enrolment against the RTE seat
on_reject: school denial appealable to BSA / District Education Officer
note: actual admitting authority is the private school head

action: Confirms admission, records the child for state reimbursement, and closes the grievance channel
on_reject: appeal escalates BEO -> BSA -> District Education Officer
note: state reimburses per-child cost to the school under s.12(2)

action: Household submits registration application for a job card at the Gram Panchayat with ID/photos
note: registration is free; no fee may be charged

action: Verifies household details, residence and adult members claiming registration
on_reject: complaint to Gram Panchayat / Block Development Officer
note: verification done in the village for transparency

action: Gram Panchayat approves registration and orders issue of the job card to the household
on_reject: appeal to Programme Officer / Block Development Officer
note: job card issued in presence of local residents

action: Receives the worker's dated written work application and issues a dated acknowledgement receipt
on_reject: can also apply to the Programme Officer at block if the GP refuses the receipt
note: dated receipt is the legal trigger for the 15-day guarantee under s.3

action: Prepares/selects a work estimate from the shelf of projects to be opened for the demanded labour
note: work drawn from the approved GP shelf of projects

action: Sanctions the work and directs allotment of employment to the applicant household
time_limit: work must be allotted within 15 days of application
on_reject: failure triggers unemployment allowance under s.3(1); grievance to Programme Officer/Ombudsperson
note: the 15-day guarantee is the core statutory entitlement

action: Opens the muster roll and records daily attendance of workers at the worksite
on_reject: discrepancy raised at social audit / to Programme Officer
note: attendance read out to workers at day's end for transparency

action: Measures completed work in the Measurement Book to determine task-rate wages
on_reject: remeasurement / grievance to Programme Officer
note: wages proportional to JE measurement against task norms

action: Checks measurement, prepares the wage/muster-roll bill and forwards the Fund Transfer Order for payment
note: electronic FTO routes wages to worker accounts

action: Authorises wage payment; wages credited to workers' accounts
on_reject: delay compensation at 0.05% per day of unpaid wage under s.3(3)
note: delay beyond 15 days triggers automatic compensation

action: Gram Sabha conducts social audit of works, muster rolls and payments
on_reject: findings referred to Ombudsperson / Programme Officer for redress
note: social audit is the primary statutory accountability route

action: Receives the citizen's building plan and documents online/at counter, generates acknowledgement receipt
note: OBPAS single-window intake; registration of application

action: Checks completeness of documents and fee, forwards the file to the technical branch
on_reject: deficiency memo to applicant for resubmission
note: preliminary completeness check

action: Conducts site inspection, measures plot, verifies setbacks and ground reality against the plan
on_reject: adverse site report returns file for correction
note: field measurement and site-report to higher engineers

action: Technical scrutiny of the plan against bye-laws, FAR, coverage, setbacks; endorses the JE report
on_reject: raises query/objection to applicant via OBPAS
note: AutoDCR auto-scrutiny supplemented by AE bye-law check

action: Download the mutated khatauni and certificate; present to bank, employer, insurer and revenue office.
note: For bank deposits/shares, debts or contested property, institutions may still require a court succession certificate (Indian Succession Act 1925) — a separate judicial track (district court), not the collectorate.

action: If stalled or refused, escalate: SDM/RDO, then Collector/DM, then First/Second Appellate Officer under RTS.
on_reject: File time-bound-service complaint under UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 (penalty on defaulting officer); CM/district grievance portal.
note: Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 makes notified services time-bound with a First and Second Appellate Officer and penalty for delay.
